en: A relaxing walk through woods and small waterfalls.
The stone circles of three thousand years ago.
The exhibition center of the Monteparma Foundation opened in 2018, with temporary exhibitions and museum halls of the painters Amedeo Bocchi and Renato Vernizzi.
The most important monumental testimony of Triggiano.

The karst area between Sonnino and Terracina, one of the largest in the Mediterranean basin; the symbol is the Rava di San Domenico, known as the Cathedral of San Domenico, an 18-metre limestone pinnacle shaped by water, the most photographed attraction in the area.
The masterpiece that revolutionized art.
Fresh stop between rocks and water.

Roero country dominated by the Baroque Castle of the Alfieri, 17th century residence built on the site of the medieval fortress, on a hill overlooking the valley of Tanaro and the Langhe: in its halls the Museum of the culture of plaster, the Landscape Theatre and the chapel of the SS. Crucified.

High tower made of stone with square base with Ghibelline merlons, next to the parish: it is what remains of the defensive system and of the fourteenth-century castle erected to protect the village, of which the ruins of the entrance with the drawbridge remain.
Water and wood together.
Park in the area of the stadium, mentioned among the gardens that characterize the city.

The highest building in the centre, the ancient seat of political and military power, with the clock tower, houses the historical archive, the Carlo Guarnieri Museum and the Museum of the Mineral of the Toscano Mineral Circle.
The streets of the noble palaces built during the two centuries of lordship of the Ordelaffi, between Corso Garibaldi and Via Maroncelli.

On 1 December 1923 the central pillar of the dam yielded under the pressure of about 6 million cubic meters of water: the wave overwhelmed Bueggio, the sanctuary of the Madonnina and the hamlet of Dezzo, where 209 people died, and reached Lake Iseo in about 45 minutes, with over 500 total victims. The ruins, in a basin at the foot of Mount Gleno, can be reached by two paths from Piazza and Nona; in summer a shuttle connects Vilminore to Piazza and are possible guided excursions for small groups.
Chestnuts and mountain cuisine.
Neighborhood life arbëreshë.
The Casino Nobile with the Villa Museum and the collections of the Roman School.
A Tuscan Medici villa on the Friuli hills.
The sanctuary of the saint of Corinaldo.
Maiolicas and marbles in the churches of the country.

Museum of peasant civilization of the Pinerolian plain created by the association Gruppo Ricerca Piscina (in 1979 according to Turismo Torino, in 1981 according to the Municipality): tools, objects of daily use up to the mid-Twentieth century, agricultural machinery, tools for bachiculture, photos and documents; the name comes from the rubat, stone roller and wood for threshing. Opening on request.
The main square of the city, meeting point of the crotonese, surrounded by porticoes of the second half of the nineteenth century; from here Via Vittoria leads to Piazza Duomo.
The Renaissance cloister of a Norman abbey.
The typical dish in the square.
Castle built in 1470.
The symbol of the country of the zolfatari.
The city stratified under the alleys.
Village on top of a hill with a wide panorama, dominated by the 11th century Romanesque Cathedral with the frescoed crypt and the diocesan Museum.

Born from a medieval palace of the fortified village, of which remains sections of walls, from 1830 belonged to the Counts Faina, who at the end of the nineteenth century gave it the current appearance: three floors with wing of the greenhouse to L, portal bugnato in terracotta, windows with parapets in cast iron and terracotta decorations perhaps of the sculptors Perugini Angeletti and Biscarini; inside the living room of the parties, dining room, gallery and skyscraper. Municipal since 1962, it is the seat of the City Council and a congress center; the large public park hosts parties and events.

Islet about 200 meters half a kilometer from the coast of Marina di Maratea, frequented by the Roman era: there remain tanks for the production of garum and the seabed have returned Greek and Roman anchors and amphorae; it houses a rare lizard, the Podarcis sicula paulae.
A century ago the Caserta countryside, object by object.
The ruins of the residence of the bishops princes.
In the heart of Pescara Vecchia, the house where the poet was born: nine rooms open to the visit.
The collection was born from half a century of painting awards.

Gate of the National Park of the Metalliferous Hills on the lignite route: of the mine of Ribolla you visit most of the original complex, with accommodation and dormitories, recreation room, lighthouses and wells. Here in 1954 a gas leak killed 43 miners, one of the most serious mining tragedies of the post-war period: the site is also a place of memory today.
Ancient courtyards and fireplaces of a Salento country.
A garden hidden downtown.

It preserves the canvas of Vincenzo Pagani "Madonna enthroned with Child and Saints Giovanni Battista, Giovanni Evangelista, Maddalena and Caterina" (mystical bride of Saint Catherine), of 267 x 215 cm, which after a restoration carried out in Urbino was relocated on the right wall of the left arm of the transept. The municipal source indicates the influences of Raphael, in particular the Madonna del Pesce and Madonna di Foligno.

Site of Community Interest: dunes formed between 7,500 and 3,500 years ago, among the best preserved in Italy, up to 12 meters tall, with Mediterranean juniper maquis, sparto, lentisco, rosemary and thyme.

Borgo dell'alta Valle Scrivia of probable Roman origin, documented by 1127, walled fief passed by the bishops of Tortona to Malaspina and Spinola; it preserves the sixteenth-century Palazzo Spinola, the castle of Borgo Fornari and the fifteenth-century bridge on Scrivia, with the hamlet of Porale in the Parco dell'Antola.
A church of the year 1000.
The papal palace of Vignola.
The seventeenth-century portrait of the village in the Pala del Salmeggia.

Probably started at the end of the sixteenth century, with three naves, with a high altar in rare marble and two baroque altars; it preserves canvases of Biella (XVII-XVIII century), a San Bassiano perhaps of the shop of the square and a sixteenth-century wooden statue of Saint Lucia.
Portals and coats of arms of five centuries in a few steps.
A mine from 5,000 years ago.
About two kilometers of white and soft sand and clear water, with camping and camping areas behind; here landed in 1875 the first prisoners of the penal colony.

Remains of the Roman city built at the bottom near the Tiber: forum, theater, thermal baths, water lilies, a stretch of the ancient Via Flaminia, funerary monuments, amphitheatre and the oldest necropolis, of the VII century BC; the  "great substruttures," buildings of 12 rooms on two floors, have still uncertain function. The park is also habitat of various flora and fauna.
The palace of the Varanos.
Historical building of the center of Vicenza, among the architectures open for the big events of the city.
The story of the bread that lasts fifteen days.

Great sixteenth-century fortress on the sea built by the Genoese to assert the dominion over the city; in the fifteenth-century Loggia of the Castle Nuovo the Civic Archaeological Museum and the City, inaugurated on April 7, 1990 at the reopening of part of the complex.
Art and archaeology of the Cenedese.

Cyclopedonal path on the sea that connects San Lorenzo al Mare to Sanremo, between tunnels and bridges: in Riva Ligure it crosses the historic center, between fields and alleys, after Santo Stefano al Mare and before Arma di Taggia. Along the route bike rentals and rickshaws and large parking lots.
A look at Africa in Verona.

15th century shrine in the chestnut wood accessible from the village. The façade has a rose window made from a single block of stone; inside a wall frescoed by Pietro Guido da Ranzo with Stories of the Passion and a Madonna with Child in Carrara marble by sculptor Filippo Parodi, pupil of Bernini.
One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Garda, among the ruins of a castle.
A lake inside a dead volcano.
The heart of the world cult of Santa Rita.

Rural church dating back to 1114 (XI-XIII century according to the Park), in front of the medieval fountain, probably built on the remains of a temple of Hercules in the area of the ancient Superaequum. On February 4 and 5, the 'pagnotta di Sant'Agata' is blessed, bread in the shape of a wet bosom in the water of the Fonte di Sant'Agata and linked to the protection of puerpers.
Where the Ticino feeds the Villoresi Canal, between walks and bike paths.

The municipality of Briana was built to the east of Lambro, whose name comes from the "Brugo" shrub of the heathers; the parish church of San Bartolomeo houses the relics of the Magi Kings, preserved for centuries in the church of Sant'Ambrogio, and in Moncucco stands the Temple of San Lucio, Renaissance chapel brought here from Lugano.

A mountain country about 1455 meters in the Germanasca Valley, with the talc mines of the Ecomuseo (DiscoverMiniere and DiscoverAlpi), the Waldensian Museum in the ancient temple of 1556 in Ghigo and the glacial basin of the Thirteen Lakes.

The parish church of San Pietro Apostolo was built in Baroque forms by the Rospigliosi princes in the early eighteenth century, perhaps on an older church: it has a Greek cross plan and an elliptical dome 46 meters high. The Collegiate Church of San Lorenzo, dedicated to the patron saint, is in Vignolesco style, with the façade attributed to Carlo Maderno.

The fourteenth-century polychrome portal of Raimondo di Poggio, 15th-century square bell tower and mosaic floor of 1845; rebuilt in Baroque forms in 1741. The cloister is in the former convent, today the town hall; inside also the Clarisse parlour and the wheel of the exhibits.

The largest blade in the province of Bari, erosive incision in the mesozoic limestones that crosses the territory with karst caves and different vegetable environments, partly modified by agriculture. Along the course remains of settlements from the Neolithic to the classical age and nineteenth-century villas on the margins; in Triggiano the archaeological area of Monte Telegrafo. There is no well-equipped route: the walk through fragno and roverella woods to the sea is just a project.
The heart of the country.

Municipality of the Bergamo plain linked to the Gambarini family: Villa Giavazzi, built by Carlo Maria Gambarini in Napoleonic age and today seat of the Town Hall, with its nineteenth-century romantic park, the Neoclassical Mausoleum of 1823 and, in a factory abandoned on the avenue of entrance, the Museum of the territory dedicated to the peasant civilization.
The oldest church in Acre.

The oldest noble residence of Bagheria, built by Giuseppe Branciforti, Prince of Pietraperzia and Count of Raccuja, with the inscription "O Corte a Dio" at the entrance; neoclassical forms, colonnade porch, picture gallery and halls frescoed with crystal chandeliers. From its terraces start the fires of the feast of Santa Rosalia on July 14.
Fortified gate of 1199, symbol of the village, today municipal theatre.

Medieval village from the origins between the IX and the X century, closed by the walls with three doors (Verziere, Borgo Vecchio and Monte) corresponding to the three districts; from Piazza San Francesco, climbing the staircase, opens the view on the Umbrian hills.
A cove for every taste.
A medieval village overlooking the Maremma.
Pasta with seafood and risotto alla pescatora, spaghetti with fresh anchovies, vermicelli with anchovies and pecorino cheese and soup, fish soup born from the least valuable fish.
The Mugello before the Medici.
A rock full of fossils in the woods.
A demanding excursion to one of the most beautiful panoramic points of the Aosta Valley.
An itinerary from Gothic to Baroque in a few streets.
The western Murge plateau, where you enter, climbing from Andria towards Castel del Monte, which rises inside the park.
The 16th century frescoes of the village.
All the theatres and museums at a glance.
The Jewish memory of Asti.
The beach of Troisi's film.

The seaside resort of the Teramian coast with the pine forest that arrives at the sea, planted on the initiative of the Filiani family of Atri (about 2,000 pines) and sung in the name, inspired in 1925 at ...The rain in the pine forest of D'Annunzio; symbol is the sixteenth century Torre del Cerrano, heart of the Marine Protected Area, while on the hills rises the medieval village of Mutignano.

The museum, opened since 1969 on the initiative of Mgr. Luigi Bosio, is located in the College of the Virgins of Jesus, founded in 1608 by Cinzia, Olympia and Gridonia Gonzaga, nephews of St. Louis, with wrought iron gates of the seventeenth century; he preserves paintings and objects belonging to the Saint and his family. Free entrance with the pilgrim's bag of the Pastoral Unit.

Built between 1476 and 1482 for Giovanni della Rovere, lord of Senigallia and nephew of Pope Sixtus IV: Luciano Laurana designed the residential part and Baccio Pontelli completed the defensive structure. It is a plain fortress with quadrangular plan with cylindrical towers at the corners, designed for firearms.

Museum founded in 1960 with relics of the regiment and the countryside in North Africa 1940-1943, in three rooms dedicated to the fallen and the commander, the countryside and the Afrika Korps and the opposing forces; a historical office keeps library, photos and documents. Outside, beyond the tomb of the commander, the alert of remembrance with cippi for forgotten departments. Recognized by Regione Lombardia as a museum regiment.

Built at the end of the eighteenth century by the will of the Odescalchi on the ruins of a monastery of the Humiliates, it passed in 1787 to Count Andrea Passalacqua who transformed it into a sumptuous dwelling, with decorations by Giocondo Albertolli and frescoes by Andrea Appiani. Vincenzo Bellini stayed there between 1829 and 1833, finding inspiration for Norma, La strangere and La sleepambula.
Exhibitions in the chic district.
Inaugurated in 1999, it combines graffiti by master Angelo Gatto and a bronze statue by the sculptor Sergio Comacchio.
The landscape of the quarries that made Albiano's fortune.
the MiC card indicates "closed" every day without hours; telephone contacts. 335 7789139, associationcasadei@gmail.com

A novenary and country church of the 13th century, rebuilt in 1632. At the beginning of September there is one of the most important festivals in the country, with the procession from the church to the parish.

The convent of the Friars Minor Reformed rises at the foot of the village, outside the walls; it dates back to the second half of the XVI century, on the foundations of the church of San Cataldo collapsed after the earthquake of 1456, and was largely rebuilt after the earthquake of 1930. In the adjacent little church, recently restored, the Madonna dell'Incoronata, patron saint of shepherds and tractures, is kept.
On the third floor of the same building of MAAM the sacred works of art, mostly of Sienese artists.

The city of the sarcophagi is on the Via Clodia, inhabited by almost three millennia: the Romanesque basilicas of San Pietro and Santa Maria Maggiore, the Etruscan museum in the former convent of the Rest and the necropolis.

Small sixteenth-century church at 1,375 meters with sailing bell tower; presbytery and apse have frescoes dating back to 1564, and the Trinity returns to the bezel of the façade, to the altar polyptych and to the ceiling.

Church of the village still visitable despite the earthquakes have severely damaged the architecture of the area; the municipality signals its portal, the bell tower and the stained glass windows inside, in a harmonious building and well inserted in the town.
In the village of Vivaro, it offers astronomical observations, visits to the planetarium, educational activities for schools and guided walks.
Castle of the 11th century that has marked the history of the territory; remain a beautiful tower and some stretches of walls, reachable by a short walk.

The basilica of the patron founded in the fourth century, cathedral until the ninth, with the Paradise Gate, the octagonal bell tower and the cloister; here the foreplay of the peace of Constance was prepared (1183).
Rocks, sands and meteorites in a former military village.
The oldest history of the valley, from the Paleolithic onwards.

Capital of a bishopric from the 11th to the beginning of the 19th century, called "small Salzburg": the medieval and Baroque center between Isarco and Rienza brings together Duomo, frescoed cloister, Bishop's Palace with the Diocesan Museum, the Portici and the White Tower, with the Plose as a mountain home.
Porticos and lake in a walk.
The sanctuary of the miracle that saved Treviglio, with the helmet of Lautrec.

In the Art Nouveau building of the former Sandretto plant, with a small park: the collection, started in 1985 by Gilberto Sandretto, has over 2,500 pieces in eight rooms, from hand painted calendars-posters to an injection press by the Brothers Sandretto, with a last room on the environmental impact of plastic. Re-opened in 2016 by the Cannon Group, the polo shirt also includes the Textile Manufacture Museum and the Cav Machine Tools Collection. Modesto Sandretto. Open Sundays and holidays from April to October, with guided tours every hour from 15 to 19 (season 2026).
Meet the wolf.
You go up into the clock.

Access is from Passo Croce d'Aune, at 1.015 meters, reachable from Pedavena with the state road 473 and starting point of hiking itineraries, on the route of Alta Via n. 2. In summer the mountain offers pastures and pastures for walks, in winter downhill slopes and a cross-country trail; it is frequented by the free flight and preserves archaeological traces from the Neanderthal era onwards.
The large Norman ruins in red bricks.
€5 a museum, €7 both

The palace, built since 1628, closes the north side of Piazza della Libertà: the façade is by Carlo Maderno, continued by Bernini, author of the gate of the garden; an inscription recalls the intervention of Alexander VII in 1660. He hosted the Vatican Observatory, which was transferred here from the Roman College. Since 2014, at the behest of Pope Francis, palace and gardens are open to the public as a museum pole. The Pontifical Villas, an extraterritorial area of the Holy See, include 55 hectares with Villa Barberini, Villa Cybo and the Italian gardens.

Built in the 16th century by the Dominican monks, who had left the cenobio of Santa Margherita Vecchia alla Chiaiolella for Saracen raids; the ridge on which it stands took the name of ... The already secured parts host exhibitions and cultural events.

The center retains the medieval plant; the name recalls Marino Caracciolo, feudal lord who married Maria de Sangro, who brought the territory into dowry. At Christmas, the "'ndocce" wood charms lit, illuminate alleys and squares transforming the country into a large living nativity scene.

Among the twelve hamlets, Ludrigno (560 m) is one of the oldest, with a well preserved architectural facility of interest for the minor architecture of Bergamo; Piazzolo (780 m) preserves rural houses from the 14th and 15th centuries; in Cacciamali (1100 m), today almost uninhabited, a small church of the 16th century with frescoes.

Among the best preserved medieval castles of Amiata, developed by a palace perhaps erected by the Marquis Ugo of Tuscany between 970 and 995, expanded by the Aldobrandeschi, besieged by the Sienese in 1331 under Guidoriccio da Fogliano and then passed to the Medici State. Inside the collection of arms Emo Mecheroni (about 175 weapons and helmets from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, first floor) and, on the top floor, the Museum of the medieval landscape on the fortifications of Amiata and Maremma, with finds of Castel Vaiolo, texts in Italian and English and tactile paths; from the same floor you climb on the tower of 28 meters.

Medieval church erected in 1480 on an ancient Roman temple and renovated several times: it preserves a pulpit of the fourteenth century with trilobed arch and figures of saints, two saints on Romanesque lions coming from the destroyed church of St. John the Baptist, a canvas of Neapolitan school with the Baptist and, in the apse, the Creation of the world frescoed in 1949 by Amedeo Trivisonno.
The historical collections of the city, from Gentile Bellini to Lorenzo Luzzo.

Hill of 831 meters east of the village, on the valleys of the Belici and the Salìto, inhabited by the Neolithic at the Iron Age; in the sixth century BC there arose an indigenous center then Hellenized, probably Mytistran, which resisted the Romans in the First Punic War. There remains a necropolis of the Copper Age, Greek tombs of the 4th century BC, the city walls, the Hellenistic acropolis and traces of the archaic town. It is reached from the crossroads Chibbò.
Carsica cave that preserves the fresco of a Madonna orante, probably of the eighth century.
On top of the village, inside the original walls, next to the remains of the Fortress of San Pietro dei Colonna (today Piazza San Pietro); the altar was consecrated in 1537.
Butterflies fly around you.
Aleramic residence documented since 1100, in the center of Trino, with direct access from Piazza Garibaldi.
A rare example of a country built around a factory.
The Roman city better readable than the Marche.

Wine village Doc above the Riviera dei Cedri, with the medieval nucleus of Bonifanti and the Torre dell'Orologio, the chapel of the Madonna della Snow with frescoes of the sixteenth century, the mother church of the Assunta and the Ecomuseum of wine in the former prison; famous the rite of the Battenti of Holy Thursday.

Made to be built in 1447 by Giovanni and Francesco Pico in late-Gothic forms, with original polygonal flanks and apses, 17th century bell tower and neo-Gothic façade; severely damaged by the 2012 earthquake, it was restored and reopened in 2019. Among the works mentioned by the Touring two paintings by Sante Peranda, a Crucifix frescoed by Pietro Annigoni (1983), a seventeenth-century ancone in golden wood of school mirandolese and, in the sacristy, a canvas by Alessandro Tiarini (1612).
The circular village.

The "Venice of Friuli": Piazza della Libertà with the Loggia del Lionello under the Castle Hill and its civic museums, the Tiepolo of the Archbishop's Palace, the Duomo and the Oratory of Purity, Casa Cavazzini for the twentieth century and a city of gardens.
The Lucan Mantegna.
The first residence of the Farnese.
The fortress of the Aldobrandeschi in the heart of the village and the medieval church of San Nicola with medieval and Renaissance frescoes.
The historic route.
The Roman Renaissance in the lagoon.
The most beautiful Romanesque in Tuscia.

In the square of the parish church, where centuries of the town's history are concentrated, the fountain of 1828 rises on the site of the Roman thermal baths; another fountain at the Santa Scala has baths supported by elements of imperial age.
At the western entrance of the village, built in the seventeenth century by the Baron of Cly Pietro Filiberto Roncas with material from the castle of Cly.

The garden city: the eighteenth-century Palazzo Estense, a small Versailles for Leopardi, the Sacred Mount UNESCO World Heritage with its 14 chapels, Villa Panza del FAI and the villas museum among age-old parks.

Romanesque church, national monument and among the historic residences of Lazio, built on the ruins of the Temple of Hercules Liberatore; for the municipality is the most remarkable of the buildings of the post-Roman age and example of medieval art. In its garden there is the Arc de Marcantonio.

More than 500 species of the Maritime Alps in 14 environments, at the confluence of the Gesso della Valletta and Valasco streams. It takes its name from the Valderia Viola, endemic, discovered here by Carlo Allioni in 1780: created by the park in 1990, it is the only alpine garden that contains the place of discovery of the species; the nineteenth-century paths are those of the "Giardino degli Inglesi" of the guests of the spa. Open in summer (in 2022 from 11 June to 12 September, 5 €).
From the first cathedral of the fourth century to the Romanesque.

Opened in 1997 in the Comital Palace De Capua, it exhibits archaeological finds from prehistory to the Middle Ages, liturgical vestments of the local clergy of the XVI-XVIII century and clothes and fabrics of the early nineteenth century found in the crypt of the Collegiate of the Assumption, with an annexed restoration laboratory. Three beans found in a dead man's waistcoat have been studied and the bean "Norman of Altavilla" is now cultivated in an experimental project.
The reserve between the Trossa and Ristoto streams, rich in wild orchids, lakes and the Sterza Waterfall, which is thrown into a clear puddle.

Built between 975 and 1018 by the Rogadeo, Pironti and Muscettola families and consecrated in 1276, in the district of the oldest palaces. It preserves an ambo of the twelfth century with mosaics (Jonas and the sea monster) and twenty-one majolica basins of Arab origin, a sarcophagus of the third century AD, frescoes fourteenth-century in the crypt with the Christ Pantocrator and in sacristy a risen Christ attributed to Roberto d'Oderisio or to his circle.
Parish of Romanesque origin dedicated to the patron saint of sailors, near the arcades, with Romanesque bell tower and works of art related to the medieval origins of the village.

Over 10 hectares in Tor San Lorenzo with artificial lakes, ancient varieties of roses, themed gardens and tree-lined avenues, born from the passion of the Marquise Lavinia Taverna and divided into spaces designed in 1967 by the English landscaper Russell Page; exhibitions of plants and guided tours.
A fortified villa of the Pio with four towers.
The tour of Lake Varese by bike, with a stop at the Isolino.

Roman city founded in the first century BC on the Via Postumia and flourished in the I-II century A.D., rediscovered by chance in the nineteenth century during the works on road and rail; the visitable area is about one tenth of the original city. You can see the amphitheatre, the theatre, the streets and two neighborhoods with large decorated houses, including the great mosaic with the myth of Liburgo and Ambrosia. Free admission and free visit, with seasonal hours; accessible to people with disabilities.
seasonal: from 1 April to 8 November 2026, 10-17, closed Monday and Tuesday; guided tours and tickets on the site of the castle

Started in 1621, with unfinished façade: inside a single room full of stuccoes and statues of the Six and eighteenth century and altars with wooden frames carved from the school mirandolese; next to the former Jesuit college, established in 1690.
The highest tower in the province.

City founded in 1168 against Barbarossa between Tanaro and Bormida, capital of the Borsalino hat and bicycle: the great Citadel Sabauda, Piazza della Libertà, Borgo Rovereto and, in Spinetta, the museum of the battle of Marengo.
An eighteenth-century parish in the Po countryside.

Rocky spur frequented by the Mesolithic, with open-air cults between the 10th and 8th centuries BC and perhaps a small Roman temple in Minerva; in the Middle Ages there arose a castle with more walls, demolished by the Bresciani in 1277 after having removed it from the Scaligeri and then rebuilt with two concentric belts and a tower. The Republic of Venice decreed its destruction in 1574 (1575 for Italia.it) because it was a refuge for bandits; the remains, dug recently, can be reached with an easy path up to the panoramic cross on the Island of the Rabbit, the Gulf of Salò and Mount Baldo.
What remains of the ancient Norman castle.

In the former bishop's palace, then seminary, today state, remain part of the buildings of the forum under the current Piazza Regina Margherita: the apsed hall, reopened in 2016, which housed the Mosaic of the Nile, the Erario, the civil basilica with four naves and the Ninfeo dei Pisces (already Antro delle Sorti), cave in the rock with the remains of a second Hellenistic mosaic; an antiquarium exhibits statues of Augustus and Faustina Maggiore.
Waterfalls and exotic trees in the heart of Sardinia.

Borgo of just over 600 inhabitants about 50 km from Sassari and Alghero, the ancient Gurulis Vetus cited by Ptolemy: the Gothic-Aragonese parish church of Santa Giulia of 1520 with the Civic Archaeological Museum next to, the baronial palace on Palattu on the hill of San Paolo and a territory with about 40 nuraghi and the canyon of Su' Entale.

It takes its name from a small castle that controlled this section of the Arno, of which there are few medieval traces like the Portaccia; it was the seat of the municipality until the twentieth century. The church of San Michele Arcangelo, documented in the fourteenth century as Sant'Angelo in Fabriciano, was rebuilt in the second half of the nineteenth century with a clock bell tower instead of the small sailing bell tower.

The ancient palace of the Priors, built in 1246, overlooking the main square where in summer events and concerts are held; you enter it from Porta Garibaldi, door of the medieval walls of which also remains the polygonal tower (XII and XV century).
Carro's minerals and those that shine in the dark.
The Giant of Piazza Carlo III.
A little ladder on the lake.
The sacred art of the country.
In the hamlet of Prabi the church of Sant'Apollinare and the hermitage of São Paulo both preserve cycles of medieval frescoes.
It only goes up on special occasions: Feast of Our Lady of Fire (February 4), St. Mercury and other events
The Carolingian roots of Medolla.
The legend of Peter.
Large park of native and exotic species, including cedars and cypresses, with marked paths and panels.
The work in the fields of the Bassa.

Ring of about an hour and a half (difficulty E, 120 m of difference in altitude) from Santa Croce: descends steeply to the river Orfento in the woods, follows it towards Ponte di Caramanico on wooden walkways between rocky walls and climbs with steps. The Park recommends that you withdraw the free access to the Carabinieri Biodiversity Visit Centre.
Vittone's palace with the atrium painted with illusion.

The town of Val Borbera with castles and churches scattered among the hamlets: the thirteenth-century tower of Molo Borbera, the village of Torre Ratti with the fourteenth-century Casa del Fante, the church of Persi with a altarpiece of Luca Giordano and the Strette di Pertuso, canyon of about 4 km excavated by the stream Borbera.

In the historic centre, the medieval church of Santa Barbara and the parish church of the Assumption Virgin, dating back to the second half of the eighteenth century, with stone façade. During Holy Week on Friday the processions of the Crucifix and de on Scravamentu take place.
The river is just a stone's throw from downtown.

Remains of the ancient castle, inserted in the Network of the Historical Houses of Lazio: on a plateau, controlled the Sacco valley and the Latina street. From the castrum Fluminariae would derive the name of the locality.
The large beach of San Teodoro, also convenient on foot from the center.
Byzantine ruins in the Salento countryside.

To the south of the basilica, it is one of the most important buildings in Lombardy and, for Italia.it, among the masterpieces of early Christian art in Lombardy: the lower part is dated to the V-VI centuries, the upper one to the VII. Small brick building with octagonal plan with alternate circular and square niches, illuminated by eight windows and a lantern at the top of the dome; the hexagonal baptismal font with painted cross is unusual in Lombardy and typical of the area of Aquileia and Istria. Rediscovered under the road plan in 1935 and recently restored, it preserves high medieval frescoes.
Designed by the architect Piero Portaluppi and built in 1912-1914, among the oldest power stations in Italy, with the building richly decorated with geometric motifs. It's seen from the outside.
Case-torre along the Caprio stream.
The ancient Cathedral of Ogliastra.
privately owned castle, not accessible interior
Near the summit of Monte Peglia, the park houses a protected wildlife area and the Environmental Documentation Centre of Monte Peglia.

Rare pre-industrial plant, probably from the 17th century and still in operation, bought by the Marinelli family in 1880 and moved by the water of the Rabbies stream: inside a large hammer of 1834, a double stone forge with a hood over 7 meters high and a collection of anvils, hammers and tanks. Visit by reservation, with guided demonstrations of iron processing when provided; suitable for families.
One of the most important prehistoric sites in Europe.

Roman city at the foot of Mount Santa Croce, among centuries-old olive groves: the Castello Pandono with the horses painted in relief for Count Enrico, the archaeological museum in the former convent of Santa Chiara, the Roman amphitheatre of Verlasce, the cathedral built with the blocks of the Roman theatre and the basilica of San Nicandro.
A Gaudenzian fresco in a country sanctuary.

Two rooms with more than 160 works by the painter Rudolf Stolz (1874-1960), largely self-taught and considered, after Egger-Lienz, among the most important Tyrolean artists of the first half of the twentieth century: sketches, sketches for frescoes, watercolors and studies, with paintings by Albert Stolz. Every summer a temporary themed exhibition.

Palazzo dei Mazziotti, barons of Celso and opponents of Bourbon absolutism, with fifteenth century plant and current appearance of the late eighteenth century; declared national monument, it preserves frescoes by Matteo Cilento and surrounds three sides of the main square of Celso with a facade with twelve balconies and two watchtowers. The chapel of St. Nicholas is placed on it; in 2010 it appears in the film "We believed" by Mario Martone.
In the shade of two bell towers, the purest Romanesque, with masterpiece façade in grey stone of the master comedians.
The children's beach.
The living room of the city of St. Louis.

The ancient ossuary has been transformed into a small museum: at the center a cycle of late-Gothic frescoes of the Last Judgment, with other paintings on the redemption of souls who were a catechism for the faithful who could not read. In the showcase are the precious vestments called Sonnenburg and, in a reliquary, the entire skeleton of St. Constantine II. Opening on request.
Tronto sharecropper tools.

At 475 meters on a terrace between the chestnut trees (the boden in Walser means plateau), dominates the village and the plain of Toce: remember the Virgin who in the sixteenth century led home the shepherd Maria Della Torre, lost in the woods; built from 1530 and then expanded, has three naves and a fresco of the Virgin with Child. You can reach it by car or on foot; in front of the church a courtyard with spring water fountain. Open every day 9-17.
A walk between greenery and Roman ruins.
Baroque church with 16th century frescoes; church and bell tower were renovated in 2004-2005.

Established in 1994, about 1,600 hectares of cliffs overlooking the sea with fossil fish and chalk crystals, woods and birds like the pilgrim falcon; five paths and a panoramic road towards villages and the marina of Baia Vallugola.
Alleys and underpasses on a rock spur.
Spa center with swimming pools, whirlpools, saunas and Turkish bath, which with the casino has made the town a tourist destination.

A path of about 2 km, with 140 m of difference in altitude, which climbs from the cliff of Ascea Marina to the remains of the Telegrafo Tower through the Mediterranean maquis; requalified by the Park Authority with the Municipality, with 12 walkways accessing the beaches to protect the dunal flora, a bike path and 8 wooden platforms. The look ranges from Capo Palinuro to the sandy coast of Ascea.

Small natural environment along the Sile between Quarto d'Altino and Portegrandi, reachable by bike Girasile and equipped with a service center; can be visited all year round by reservation with the Ornithological Association Basso Piave.

Borgata marina di Cuglieri: beach in a cove of white limestones with golden, reddish and black pebbles and low sea suitable for children, frequented by windsurfers and kiter with maestral. On the promontory to the north is the 16th-century tower that gives its name to the resort; little further north is the wild stretch of Riu 'e sa Ide.
A large Cistercian complex in the middle of rice fields.

Built at the beginning of the 11th century, it has a simple Romanesque stone façade and Latin cross plan; the bell tower is a nineteenth-century reconstruction. The Bourbon Chapel was built in 1613 by the Marquis Gianbattista Bourbon del Monte; inside a sixteenth-century baptismal font in sandstone with the coat of arms of the Marquis, a 12th-century slab and, on the main Baroque altar, a Madonna with wooden Child of the fourteenth-century carrying the silver keys of the village, deliver them for the feast of Ascension. The crypt-sepulchre of the Bourbon del Monte is not open to the public.

Isola del lago di Bolsena quoted by Dante in the Divine Comedy; there are the church of Saints James and Christopher, the work of the Vignola, and an octagonal edict by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger. You can reach it by boat from the marina of Capodimonte, which also touch the island Martana.

Of the four towers of the Norman castle, demolished around 1600, there are two remaining: the Norman Tower, almost intact, dominates the ancient village and offers a beautiful view over all Rutigliano. Guided tours during the year, access by reservation.
Man's origins.
The view from the terrace, from the mountains to the sea.
The retablo of 1501 of the founder of the school of Stampace.

Open-air museum on the gentle slopes of the Serpent Hill, beyond the Roman bridge over the Carapelle River: the route crosses the archaeological evidences of the oldest past of the city. Free admission; from Tuesday to Friday and Sunday 8-13.30 and 15-16 (times subject to change).
The memory of the peasant work of the village.
A medieval village overlooking the Albegna.
An intact stone village of the Valchiusella.

A small town between the streams Stura and Orba from the historic centre of Liguria, with facades painted in trompe l'oeil legacy of the long Genoan domination: the Baroque Our Lady Assunta with the altar of Alessandro Antonelli, the Oratory of St. John the Baptist with the sculptures of Maragliano, the birthplace of St. Paul of the Cross and the Palaeontological Museum
The village where Pope Silverio was buried.
A royal living room at the station.

Well of the FAI, it is indicated as the smallest historical public theatre in the world, with about fifty square meters of audience; the guided tour includes the stage and the dressing rooms on the lower floor. Open to the public on Saturday and Sunday.

The house of the Pèrkmandl, the imaginary gnome of the mines: a museum near the town hall that tells in an innovative way mines and miners of the valley of the Fersina in the late Middle Ages and their connection with the Mòchena community, designed as an introduction to the mine of Erdemolo. Information and bookings at the numbers of the Mòchen Cultural Institute.

The original nucleus dates back to the 11th century; of the Romanesque church the crypt remains, with columns holding vaults on cruising, where the bones of the saint are preserved and where frescoes of the Nativity were discovered dating back to around 1500. The three-nave interior dates from the 13th and 16th centuries, with 18th-century frescoes in the choir, a 17th-century wooden pulpit and a 33-metre high 16th-century bell tower; on the square stands the 1760 Episcopal Seminary.
The view from the 39th floor.
The Augustinian complex includes a library with collection from the adjacent church and a hospice; outside the bronze monument to Pope Niccolò V, linked to the origins of Fivizzano.
From the hill of the castle the view ranges from the plain to the white peaks of the Apuan Islands and the sea.
A Sansovino in Lunigiana.
Sacred art, archaeology and life of the friars in a convent of the seventeenth century.
Palladio in front of Palladio.
The last door of the walls.

The ancient Teanum Sidicinum at the foot of Roccamonfina: the great Roman theatre renovated in the strict age, the national archaeological museum and the cathedral of San Clemente rebuilt after the war.
The most beautiful view of the park.

Center on the plateau overlooking the plain of Gela, rebuilt in the eighteenth century after the earthquake of 1693, with the Baroque churches of Santa Maria d'Itria and Addolorata, the Sanctuary of Maria SS. del Bosco, the Belvedere on the plain and the Reserve of the Sughereta, the last great relic of corket of central-southern Sicily.
Piedmontese Baroque and a fifteenth-century organ.
The door built in 1561-1565 in place of Porta Nomentana, where on 20 September 1870 the breach marked the annexation of Rome to the Kingdom of Italy; it houses the museum of the Bersaglieri.

512 meters of hill near the narrow of Pinzano, at the western end of the Morainic amphitheatre of Tagliamento, once a hairy mountain for grazing and now entirely wooded. It was the Italian fortified line used only in the retreat of Caporetto, when some departments resisted to slow down the Austro-Germanic advance. The CAI trail 813 of ridge (about 5 km, 2 hours and 30, difficulty E) starts from the parking lot to the second hairpin bend of the scenic road Via al Monte, touches two belvederi and returns to the military mule track "Las Cengles" passing through the church of San Giovanni; on the ridge it is necessary to be careful for the overhanging side. In the sky the griffins of the nearby Lake Cornino.
Originally a small newsstand dedicated to the Madonna della Snow, after a snowfall of August 5th; it preserves the remains of Pier Francesco Grisei.

In Palazzo San Domenico, seat of the Fondazione Francesco Paolo Michetti established in 1952, a few years after the National Prize of painting born in 1947. He has exhibited great works by Michetti, including "The Numbs" and "The Snakes" and the paintings of the artists of the Prize; since 2006 the foundation has collected over 260 works, including painting, photography, video, sculpture and installations, and hosts monographic exhibitions on Michetti and contemporary art.
Franciscan frescoes and the silver of the Counts of Celano.
Inside in local stone decorated with masks; preserves monstrance, pissides and silver cups.

It collects many wooden sculptures of the territory; among the paintings the Madonna del Soccorso di Giulio Vergari of 1521, a Madonna del Rosario of the late sixteenth century and a altarpiece of Saints Biagio and Antonio Abate, recently found and attributed to Pier Leone Ghezzi (1674-1755).
Roman ruins and natural swimming pool on the sea.
The mystery of the Shroud.
The industrial history seen from the gun factory.
private property, visible from the outside

The thirteenth-century tower, with a pavilion roof and two-fores, is the only original tower left; since 1790 it is the bell tower of the Collegiate and seat of the public clock, and overlooks Porta San Pietro in Vigesimo, the main entrance of the village. On the main square, the Town Hall, formerly Palazzo della Cancelleria of the fifteenth century, with a loggia with columns in stone and arches in all sixth and a marzocco in sandstone, symbol of the Florentine power; the excavations date street, square and domus Communis in the mid thirteenth century.
The living room of the city, between plank and market.
The Benedictine red brick monastery nestled in the Crete Senesi near Asciano.
Ligurian finds in the palace of the terraces.

Built from 1222 and then enlarged, it is a remarkable example of Gothic Ligurian with three naves, with the façade with alternating bands of white Carrara marble and local green serpentine; inside a wooden choir of 1589 and a sixteenth century glass. Evening concerts are held on the churchyard.

It rises on a hill with a small hermitage, reached through the arch of San Vittore; according to tradition it was erected by vote in the place where the Saracens were stopped by the fog, saving the country. Every May 14 a procession brings the relics of the saint from the village to the church for the sung mass.
Parish church of unknown foundation, renovated several times; inside the dome the frescoes of Luigi Sabatelli, interpreter of Florentine romantic classicism.
The main gate of the ancient city between Piazza Vittorio Emanuele and Via Rialto: from here begins the oldest part of Belluno to the medieval Piazza del Mercato.

Historical capital of the Camonica Valley, dominated by the largest castle in the valley; in the village the CaMus with the only camuna gallery, the church of Sant'Antonio with frescoes by Romanino, and in Spinera the Sanctuary of Minerva, sacred place from the VII century BC to the IV AD.
visits only by reservation (tel. 338 8713534), driven every Sunday
The turret doors of the medieval village.
The hilly village of the Sienese Valdichiana with the castle of the Cacciaconti and the hamlets of Castelmuzio and Petroio among the olive trees.

It reconstructs with panels, maps and films the facts from 30 June to 7 July 1944, the German rake with killings of civilians to the east of Cisa: the partisan band, the mountain population that suffered reprisals and requisitions, the context of the massacres of summer 1944. Open from April to November by reservation.
A museum accessible only on foot.

The origins date back to the fourth century BC, as suggested by the Etruscan finds of the area; the castle, the Mons Magnifridum mentioned already in 986, was contested by Pisa, Florence and Lucca and in 1435 resisted the siege of Niccolò Piccinino, from which the said At the centre of the village the ancient civic gate called Arco del Podestà, with Ghibelline blackbirds, which became Torre delle Ore in 1655, and the three-storey town hall on Piazza della Repubblica. During the tourist season, the Tourist Office organizes a walk through Palaia, a free guided tour of about two hours on Tuesday morning, in Italian and English, which ends with the view from the highest point of the country.
In the Palazzo dell'Arengario the path in modern art from international avant-gardes to kinetic art.
Little Assumption of the Moroni.
In a room with vaults and exposed stone, he tells the front of the Soča in the First World War, with weapons, the daily life of soldiers and a trenches rebuilt to life size.

The capital for four centuries of the Pico, the city of Giovanni Pico della Mirandola was the epicenter of the earthquake of May 2012: the Duomo reopened in 2019, the Piazza della Constituente with the remains of the castle, the ruins of the church of San Francesco pantheon dei Pico, the museum of the biomedical district and, in the countryside, the marsh valleys with the boats and the bike for Finale Emilia.
A quiet stop between church and water mirror.
Church of the fourteenth century with Baroque façade, in the historic center.
Enter a reconstructed pile, ideal with children.
The market square has always hosted the market covered with fruits and vegetables, today under steel and glass shelters, with stalls of fruits, vegetables, fish and street food.
A corner of Egypt in the Picene Hills.

The mountain of the house above the city, a few kilometers and reachable by cable car: in summer panoramic excursions, family paths (Woodywalk and Lorggen), mountain bike and Plosebob; in winter ski area, winter trails and toboggan runs.
Muggia before Muggia.
Church of the fifteenth century overlooking the lake; church and convent were founded in 1477 by Jacopo da Luino, lay Carmelite.
Camerino's painting school.
In the ancient Stella Palace.
The painted village of Pollino.
The place of the Eucharistic miracle of 1560.
Sixteenth century plasters and Guadagnini's shovel.

Baroque mother church of the second half of the sixteenth century, of Byzantine rite, oriented to the east, with iconostasis and Greek altar; the icons of Christ Pantocrator and of the Virgin Odigitria are of Alfonso Caccese, those of the twelve feasts of the year come from Athens.
The masterpiece of Pomponio Amalteo.

Ancient entrance to the city, it takes its name from Aymone di Challant, a castle that ruled Lanzo for the Savoys in the mid-th century; it was accessed on a drawbridge beyond the moat and remains the hinges of the gate and the traces of the saracinesche. The façade has a pointed arch, ghibelline blackbirds and the coats of arms of the Savoy and the Estensi. Visible only from the outside.
the MiC card indicates "Closed" every day of the week; contact the Municipality (0961 993033) before visiting
The prehistory of Belice in a medieval castle.
Built on the Dora to protect travelers and pilgrims, it was enlarged in 1855; inside the choir and gallery of 1840 on four stone columns, in façade a mosaic of 1957.

The city of pasta, the Orange Flag of Touring, at the eastern gates of the Majella National Park: behind the village open the Gorges of San Martino, which lead to the remains of the Benedictine abbey of San Martino in Valle, while downstream flow the springs of the Green River; in the historic center the medieval village of Terravecchia is reached from the Sun Gate.

In the convent of San Francesco, the finds of the recent excavations of Matelica and surroundings from prehistory to the Renaissance; the symbol piece is the Globo, spherical sundial in marble with Greek inscriptions of the I-II century A.D.
Venice from above.

Municipality of the province of Varese in whose hamlet Cascina Costa is located the Museo Agusta, a business museum founded in 2002 that tells with motion MV Agusta and helicopters the history of the family company Agusta; next, Villa Agusta (1935) preserves the historical Archives of the Foundation. In the village stands the neo-medieval Villa Ricci Montevecchio (1898-1899), designed by Cecilio Arpesani.

Built in 1254 in the heart of the city and enlarged over the centuries, with chapels of noble families from the altars in polychrome marble and stucco; it preserves a Neapolitan wooden statue of San Rocco of the eighteenth century and wooden statues from the suppressed church of Santa Caterina.

Municipality of Pennavaira valley whose village of Colletta, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, is reborn from the ruins of the earthquake as a medieval village telematic on a project by Giancarlo De Carlo.

The seaside resort of the white city, less than 10 km from the village, is made of more settlements along the coast and has obtained for several years the Blue Flag; in Villanova a tourist marina dominated by a small castle, in Monticelli the remains of a village of the Bronze Age.
One of the masterpieces of the Romanesque Lombard, isolated among the meadows.
A place of memory dedicated to the fallen on the other side of the front.
The great historical market.
the Province indicates the castle of private property and in bad state of conservation: check access to the ruins
The ancient Pieve di San Zenone is built almost entirely in sandstone; modified over time, it retains much of the original structure.
The unusual four-leaf plant.
Chapel in the hamlet Oulme, stage of the path of the ecomuseum.
A noble palace built between the 14th and 15th centuries, to be seen outside.
The botanical garden dedicated to the flora of the Apuan Islands, signposted by Visit Tuscany among the places near Massa.
The Gothic house linked to the legend of the king of Italy.
Memories of the Alpine valley.
Nature inside the city.
The ancient broletto on Piazza della Libertà, now home to the art collections of the Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Alessandria.
Pink flamingos a stone's throw from the beaches.
A Renaissance villa on the hill.
A church in the historic center.

The most imposing complex after Su Nuraxi: today's 17-and-a-half-metre mast, which is estimated to have reached the 24, triangular bastion with three towers, the largest known courtyard and a village of 14 huts.
In the Palazzino dei Cadetti at the end of the 16th century: the triptych by Bernardino del Castelletto, a San Leonardo by Jacopo della Quercia and a crucifix attributed to Gian Lorenzo Bernini.
The residence of the Commendators of Malta.
The artifacts of ancient Blanda.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day; times to be checked with the Municipality (0962 85042) or the Wind Oreste Association (0962 85100)

A few kilometers from Gualdo, indicated as the most characteristic archetype of the area: large walls, medieval entrance and high towers. The church of San Bartolomeo, dating back to the thirteenth century, has frescoes from the 16th to the 11th century and two wooden angels from the sixteenth century.

Apulian Romanesque cathedral of the 13th century on the highest point of the Civita, dedicated to the Madonna della Bruna: it preserves a Romanesque rosette, the wooden choir of 1453 and the stone nativity scene carved in 1534 by Altobello Persio and Sannazzaro da Alessano.
The large nuraghe just over two kilometers from the cave.
A thousand years of history on the Biella plain.
The sunset symbol of the city.
Complete the visit of San Vitale, a few steps away.
A former monastery became the civic heart of the country.
Romanesque church on the top of Mount Conero, founded by Benedictine monks in the first half of the 11th century.
The Museum of the Sienese Scientific Academy, reported by Visit Tuscany among the museums of Siena accessible without barriers.
The central vault is frescoed by Christopher II Baschenis.

Country at 925 meters on the right side of the Mòcheni Valley, going up from Pergine Valsugana, known for the cultivation of small fruits and for the farms scattered on the sunny slope; in the ancient seventeenth-century town hall the Museum Pietra Viva tells minerals and history of the valley of Fersina.

In the village are the baroque church of San Biagio, of the sixteenth century, the church of San Lorenzo, of the fourteenth century, and the church of Santa Maria di Ponte Marmoreo, with 16th century frescoes inside.
A rare Sannitic sanctuary perhaps dedicated to Mephyte.
The water mill is still working.
Medieval alleys and the plate of the first seminary.

Roman bridge hidden in the woods above the hamlet of Rijeka, along an ancient branch of the Via Flaminia towards Camerino and the Adriatic; below is the Val Sant'Angelo, with hermitages, cults of the Lombard age and traces of the Bronze Age.
The elegant living room of Rome.

Karst lake at almost 300 meters above sea level, on the border with Abruzzo and Molise, fed by a front of springs about 3 km long that descend from the mountains of the nearby National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise: the water remains at about 10-11 °C all year round. The lake (about 0.28 km2, maximum depth 15 m at the Le Codigliane spring) is surrounded by reeds where birds nest; the reserve, in the system of the regional parks of Lazio, extends for about 400 hectares and hosts the macrostigma trout, which in peninsula Italy lives only here and in the river Ninfa. Six nature trails on foot; at the bottom of the lake since 1977 the Steel Crucifix, brought back to the surface by divers at the beginning of August.

Outside Porta Perugina, the church with gothic façade of the thirteenth century; next to the oratory with the fourteenth-century Crucifix called "Il Pianto degli Angeli" by Jacopo di Mino del Pellicciaio.
One of the most important archaeological museums in Italy, with the Situla Welcome to the ancient Venetians.
For those who love the dark side of history.
€6 single ticket; annual subscription €10; included in the state cumulative from €14
Medieval village about 730 m on the cliffs of Monte Pizzuto, on the edge of the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise: alleys and covered passages (sport'
Outdoor art by the lake.
The oldest place of worship in Lizzano, a pilgrimage destination.
A humid forest where lives one of the rarest amphibians in Italy.
The golden altar of the mountain of Purgatory.
The sea of Sarzana, reachable from the hamlet of Falcinello: low and sandy coast, different from the rocky Riviera.

Palace of 1826 in the historic center, with two entrances at different altitudes on Corso Cusani and via Procusi, seat of the MEG: a didactic itinerary on food and wine and industrial food with a collection of food labels from the end of the nineteenth century to today and a section on the "false food" edited by the University of Salerno Museum. The museum also organizes guided tours, exhibitions, conferences and concerts.
An author's fountain in the square.
Parish church of the village, known for its valuable altar.
The mysterious rocks between Tirreno and Etna.

Along the Via Corone, which climbs from Villa di Incanale to Tessari, Preabocco and Brentino to Pozza Gallet and the Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Crown, rock slabs polished by the Würmian glacier and shaped by water carry about fifty engraved figures, including a steliform anthropomorphic figure in three registers. The date is discussed: for Bagolini and Nisi they would go back to the early age of metals (mid or late of the third millennium BC), for Gaggia and Fasolo would be more recent.
The ruined castle in the holm oaks of the park.
Miniature antiphons and a mother-of-pearl crucifix.

Abruzzo village dominated by the ruins of a medieval castle with Norman octagonal tower; the Sannite necropolis of Campo Consolino has returned the equipment exhibited in the Civic Museum    . Antonio De Nino , and the paved streets in silce recall the stonework that paved the streets of Rome, including Piazza San Pietro.
Municipality of Val Lerrone, behind Albenga and Alassio, home of the multimedia museum of 500 .Dante Giacosa, wanted by Fiat 500 Club Italia and an 18-hole golf course born in 1964.

One of the main churches in the historic center; the current building replaced in 1954 the ancient church of St. Nicholas, demolished, which appears in a canvas six-seventh-century Madonna with Child and Saints, where St. Nicholas entrusts church and village to the protection of the Virgin.
View on the sea, Apuane and Lake Porta from a thousand year old castle.
La Pietà robbiana in the parish church of the village.

A bishop's city rebuilt in the district of Tuba after the earthquake of 1783, with the great neoclassical cathedral of 1935 and the diocesan Museum that houses a San Sebastiano di Benedetto da Maiano; in the surroundings the ruins of Oppido Vecchia and the Hellenistic-Roman excavations of Mella.
The lake of the park is a waterfall, a few steps from the village.

Medieval village of the upper Seriana Valley in grey stone and slate roofs, called "Piccola Toledo" for the forges of white weapons; on Piazza Dante overlook the castle Ginami, the fifteenth-century Palazzo Milesi with the Museum of White Arms and Scrolls and the church of San Gregorio, while outside the center stands the church of San Giacomo.
The parish church of the village preserves wooden altars of the sixteenth century.
The wounded center that reborn after the earthquake.
The finds of ancient Telesia inside the abbey.

Founded around 1000 by the Estensi, it passed to the Malaspinas in 1195 and in 1306 hosted Dante; abandoned after the revolt of 1797, it was rebuilt on the ruins since 1990 by the painter and sculptor Loris Nelson Ricci and his wife Erika H. End is opened in 1998, with sculptures, paintings and architectural projects.
It is located in the fourteenth-century Palazzo del Podestà in Collemancio and exhibits finds of the excavations of Urvinum Hortense.

A path inside the Park of the Alps, carried out by the volunteers of the Speleo Group, which aligns rocks and formations of different geological eras to tell the history of the entire province of Brescia: 18 stages with panels and audioguide, from the mica-scists of Maniva to the formation of Collio, from the limestone of Esino to the Maiolica and the stone of Sarnico, to the conglomerate of Montorfano. Open every day from 8 am to 11 pm, accessible to disabled people; guided tours also for schools on request.

A valley of glacial origin about 5 km wide, the largest of the Adamello Park, with Adamello and Garibaldi refuge in the upper part and the artificial lakes of Avio, Benedetto and Veneroccolo, built between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; it was the scene of battles in the First World War. Walk along path no. 611 (Caldea, Avio, Garibaldi refuge).
The Roman Baroque in the environments of the Gattopard.
The dome of colored majolica.

Three larch trees along the Via dei Masi della Val d'Ultimo, considered the oldest conifers in Europe: the legend gives them about 2,000 years, an age that only the analysis of the rings could confirm. Visitable all year round.
For a short walk between tower, square and palaces.
The church of the Medici rebuilt by Brunelleschi since 1418 for Giovanni de' Medici, with the Old Sacristy, the cloister and the Treasury Museum.
The first Roman church dedicated to the Immaculate Church, with works by Lanfranco, Guido Reni, Pietro da Cortona and Domenichino, and the evocative crypt of the Capuchins.
The tree-lined avenue on the left bank of the Bacchiglione, along which there are several historical buildings.
A classic interior just a stone's throw from the castle.
Witches and Inquisition in Sardinia of the past.

Frazione born around an ancient Camaldolese hermitage, transformed in the sixteenth century with the Palazzo Cervini by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger; a path between beech and chestnut trees leads to the springs of the Vivo.

Shortly before the village, among the olive trees, the Romanesque church is dated from the DMO to 1003; according to the Province the first settlement developed around San Gregorio, lower than the present country.

Country of the Abruzzo National Park on Marsicana, with stone houses, squares, a medieval tower, the Transhumance Museum and the Water Museum in the ancient mill; overlooking the basin of Lake Barrea.
Dinosaurs for the whole family.

In the eleventh century of the Aldobrandeschi and stop on the salt routes, it is among the greatest examples of Gothic architecture of the northern Maremma: the mast keeps original doors and windows and the rectangular tower to the south has two large rooms with vaults. The village, built around the citadel, has alleys carved into the rock and an ancient cistern that supplied the whole community.
The cathedral of the city, with the statues of the patrons of the 24 cities of the Lombard League.
Quadrangular fortress with four circular towers; in a room the Pinacoteca d'arte moderna exhibits an important collection with works, among others, by Schifano, Bargaglia and Brindisi.

Nuragic complex of about 5,000 square meters and 21 towers on the relief of Su Pranu, above the medium valley of the Flumendosa, inhabited between the XIV and IX century BC: the mast, 15 meters high (about half of the original), preserves the dome in tholos and is surrounded by a bastion of five towers and a wall of seven, with courtyards equipped with cisterns, fireplaces and huts. In the 2nd century BC the Romans transformed it into a wine plant, of which two tanks remain; ceramics from the Peloponnese attest contacts with the Mycenaean world. The name, "Gigante rosso" comes from the reddish lichens that cover it. Admission for a fee.
The religious heart of the city, with the treasure and St. Bovo.

A small town in the middle of the Ligurian coast, 25 km from Savona and 44 from Genoa, with the historic centre gathered around the Collegiate Church of Sant'Ambrogio, sandy beaches and the Lungomare Europa towards Cogoleto; inland, in the Park of Beigua, the prehistoric sites of Alpicella and the botanical path of the Desert Hermitage.
The devoted heart of Turin.

Perhaps Lombard fortification enlarged by the Normans, on the highest point of the ancient center; the tower was built by the Sanseverino after 1399, while the Caracciolos dismantled a large part of it in 1620, reusing the material for their palace.
The prohedria with sphinx and winged lion.
The Romanesque with the bell tower.
Church of the XIII century built above the small underground church of Saints Peter and Paul, with baroque façade of the eighteenth century and paintings of Neapolitan artists inside.

Baroque city between Etna and Ionio, famous for Carnival with carts in mache: Piazza Duomo with the Cathedral and the Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul, the Basilica of San Sebastiano frescoed by Pietro Paolo Vasta, the Opera dei Pupi, the Zelantea and the lava coast of Timpa with the Chiazzette towards Santa Maria La Scala.
The fort of the Royal Army.
The trapezoidal castle with its red brick crenellated corner towers, sung by Carducci as the castle

Already Santa Maria in Lama, in Piattoni: started in 1506 and remodelled several times, today it has an aspect between late Baroque and neoclassical; inside a sixteenth-century cross in gold copper on wooden support, of the Marche school. Nearby, the historical municipal buildings of the 16th and 19th centuries.

From the main course the visit continues between alleys and courts of the village perched on the hill, with Palazzo d'Ambrosio, Palazzo De Maio, the ancient Church of Purgatory and the Abbey of San Nicola; the Rione Pesco is a district of caves dug in the rock of the spur Elceto. In August the Day of the Black Pig, in February the Feast of St. Matthias with bonfires and singing all night long.
Cited in an inventory of 1613, home from 1838 to about 1960 of a fraternity of good death; it preserves an organ of 1834.
The Bardi castle above the valley.
Cathedral and crypt free of charge, ascent to the bell tower for a fee
An open-air museum.
Along the river Stanavasso to the truffle where the white truffle is born.
The ancient capital of the castle, around the castle.
Sacred art reigns.
The traces of Byzantine Calabria.
The historic apartments of Palazzo Falletti di Barolo.
All the flora of the Karst in a sinkhole.
Leonardo on paper.
Ride through the Verdicchio rows.
The closed places of the city, open with the guide.

Built in the early Middle Ages on the remains of a Roman castrum to defend the city from invasions: it preserves the bastion, the woundholes and a panoramic observatory on the lake, and today houses exhibitions, conferences and musical events.
The summit of Putia starting from the mills.
A postcard image of Chianti.
The lair party.
The carved portals are worth a stopover.
after the earthquake of 2016 the monuments are partially usable; the card of the Park describes the state prior to the earthquake
The thermal waters used since ancient times, made famous by poets Shelley and Byron.
In the ancient ghetto established in 1696, the synagogue with the museum that tells the Gorizia Jewish community and the poet and philosopher Carlo Michelstaedter.
The Romanesque symbol of the city.
Two cathedrals in the same square.

Erected by Cangrande II della Scala in 1354 and dismantled by the Venetians in 1514, during the war of the League of Cambrai; the walls, the mast and a tower remain. In summer it hosts theatre shows and events, and every May 1st, with the other castle, the re-enactment of Montecchio Medievale. Visits indicated on Saturday 15-18.30 and Sunday 10-12.30 and 15-18.30, in the summer.

The center preserves historic buildings, noble houses and gardens: between the eighteenth and nineteenth century nobles and bourgeois built palaces with gardens of delight and decor. The eighteenth-century Palazzo Sozzi (the Counts Sozzi also built the Filatoio spinning mill, second of the province) and a tower of medieval origin; the town recalls the historic Caffè Pagani,  the "salotto buono" of the village frequented by Giacomo Puccini and Neera writer.

The centre of Valvarrone under Mount Legnone, with houses that slope along the slope, Premana owes its fortune to iron and is known in the world for scissors and knives; the Ethnographic Museum tells about its culture and from the village start the paths to the lakes of Deleguaggio and Pizzo Tre Signori.
Quoted together with the Cathedral among the visits of the country.
The bridge without a river.
€8 whole; €2 reduced; €10 with the Estense Gallery
The Apennine mines in three hundred and fifty windows.

Medieval village among the olive groves of DOP oil of Cartoceto: in the woods not far from the village the Franciscan sanctuary of Blessed Sante, with 14th century cloister and a gold basement gallery; in the village the museum of peasant civilization in the underground environments of the convent of San Marco and the tradition of embroidery, alive from the fifteenth century.
The former Galleria Colonna in Art Nouveau style in the middle of Via del Corso, on Piazza Colonna.
For fans of Tyrolean folk music.

Villa on the left bank in Sambruson, of which the park, the passageway and the last room on the left of the ground floor, the monumental staircase and the central hall of the noble floor are open. Open to the public every first Saturday of the month from 10am to 1pm.
On the Tomino hill stands the church of Sant'Antonio, reached by the Via Crucis with newsstands of about 1735.
The house of the Enlightenmentist Galanti.

Country of the Elvo Valley where, along the river Ingagna, from the end of the sixteenth century the first iron workshops arose; in the area the industry grew more than elsewhere. In the premises of the former Rubino factory, founded in 1896, the Documentation Centre of the Ecomuseum of Biellese tells about this tradition.
Crystal clear waters on the road to Portofino.

Borgo with tower house mentioned in 1313 as "fortilicium" with military garrison; the oratory has vaulted vaults in brick, a rosette of the seventeenth century and an altarpiece of the seventeenth century attributed to the Emilian school. To the west is the Martin Hill, which may have hosted a Celtic-Ligurian village.
Ceramics, stained glass and Liberty decorations of the Chini family, born in Borgo San Lorenzo in 1906.
From Roman villa to castle.

Outdoor museum of 5,000 m2 near the Ötzi's discovery site, which reconstructs the daily life of about 5,300 years ago (the mummy and its equipment are at the South Tyrol Archaeological Museum). Inside there is a permanent exhibition with touchable replicas of Ötzi's clothes and tools and a plastic of the basin of the discovery; outside there are nine life-size houses rebuilt by excavations, fields and gardens with plants of the time, clay oven, pond with monoxyl canoe, long archery and daily workshops of fire, bread and flint. Open every day from Easter to All Saints; the complete visit with the outdoor area takes 3-4 hours.
A hot bath in the water that makes Villamaina spa village.
The living room of the village between church and fountain.

Built in the second half of the fifteenth century on the remains of a medieval structure, already fortified castle to defend the ancient village; on the north side a moat dug into the rock about four meters deep, on the façade the coat of arms of the Protonobilissimo with the dragon. In the courtyard the Granarie pits and the pavement that follows the medieval walls emerged from the excavations; in the underground large monolithic tanks for oil and a room-prison with the graffiti of the prisoners; on the noble floor the apartments of the princes. Today it is the seat of the municipality and cultural space; free or paid entry depending on the event.
The main district is characterized by decorated portals and continues up to the Pieve Vecchia, at the outlet of the Valle dell'Aviana, mentioned since 1145.
The view from above on Piazza Duomo and the Cremosca plain.

A short but scenic route a few steps from the centre, with walkways, waterfalls, pools and rock walls shaped by water, and stone 's monsters sculpted by the artist Antonio Ciccarelli; suitable for those looking for nature without a challenging excursion.
Walk or cycle path through fish restaurants, cafes with dehors and bourgeois villas of the nineteenth century; near is Chianura, the old fishing district.
The civic heart.
An easy walk among centuries-old olive trees to the necropolis.

Built in 1503 and enlarged in 1585 with a superior vault, it has a Romanesque portal and a early seventeenth-century holy waterworks; near the church remains a drinking trough of the time when cattle were brought there. In front is the Column of the Pedoca, coming from the excavations of the pagan temple, to which Bishop Marco Pedoca added the cross in 1587.
Monumental trees of three and a half centuries on the Adige.
The remains of the Roman city of the imperial era of Albintimilium, with spas and Roman theater back home of shows, excavated from the nineteenth century.

Already documented as curtis in 877 and as parish church of the diocese of Reggio Emilia in 980, it passed to the Canossa (Boniface resided there in 1012); the Romanesque church in present brick, with three naves on cylindrical pillars with triabsidated transept and crypt, dates back to the end of the 11th century and was run by a community of canons. Tradition binds her to Matilde, but no document prior to the sixteenth century indicates her as a client. Abandoned from the second half of the seventeenth century, it was restored in 1932 (neoromanic façade and protyro with a Roman bas-relief are of that period); authentic the central nave, the heads of the transept and the apses with arches on semi-colons, while in the plumes of the apse two angels were emerged painted around 1100. Closed temporarily for restoration after the earthquake of May 2012.
temporarily closed to the public according to the Municipality (page updated on 11 September 2026)
The Arch Calabrese of the fourteenth century is the only wooden arch in the area and is perfectly preserved; the Arch of the Thousands, of the fifteenth century, opens onto a wide panorama.

Set up in the former church of the Disciplini Bianchi, a single large hall with walls entirely frescoed in the sixteenth century with the Life and Passion of Christ, attributed to the local painter Orazio De Rossi. The route goes from Prehistory to the Middle Ages and revolves around the relationship between man and the river Churches, with findings of Remedello and the municipalities between the provinces of Brescia, Mantua and Cremona; there are five bronze swords, perhaps offered to the gods of the waters, found in the rivers Churches and Mella. Open Wednesday-Friday 9-13, Saturday 14-18, Sunday 9-12 and 14-19.

Inaugurated in December 2008 in an old oil mill restored and inspired by John Huston's film, it offers seven stage settings, including the history of the country, the descent of darkness, the refuge in caves, an optical theatre and the battle of St. Peter and Montelungo; the visit takes place in the dark, with music in quadriphonie and the projection of a film. The municipality assigns the multimedia project to the stage designer Carlo Rambaldi.
The center retains the medieval facility with churches, houses, noble palaces and gates; the name of the city would come from the "castrum romanum" on which it stood.
The road dug into the rock.
The warmest bathing lake in South Tyrol.

Cultural centre opened in 2003 in the former primary schools of 1908, about 4,000 square meters in Piazza Manzoni. In addition to the Parazzi Museum, it brings together the Galleria Civica d'arte moderna e contemporanea with the Sala della Permanente .Alfredo Saviola, the Museo della Città (Museum of the City) Adolfo Ghinzelli with musical, cartographic and photographic backgrounds and the Library Luigi Parazzi (1862), whose ancient fund with manuscripts and incunabula is consulted by reservation.

In the heart of the village, built between 1286 and 1295 and enlarged around 1400; Gothic, with walls of the Romanesque nave. The bell tower, added in the sixteenth century, is leaning for weak foundations.

The pasture begins at about 2,000 meters; the Radlsee lake, at 2,250 meters, is reached in about 2 and a half hours of walk and is flanked by the Radlsee refuge, with panoramic views of the mountains. A network of trails leads to the Königsanger (2,439 m) and the Lazfons and Villandro alpine pastures; according to legend the lake would be an ancient crater connected to the Mediterranean.

In the seventeenth century Count Catalano Alfieri, general of the sabauda infantry, had built a baroque residence on the site of the medieval fortress, completed by his son Carlo Emanuele; in 1797 he passed to the Support Alfieri and in 1952 the last descendant left him to the parish, which gave him to the municipality. The door in walnut with carved baroque tiles, the staircase of honor, the fairytale hall and the chapel are outstanding; the tradition that binds you to the inspiration of the Saul by Vittorio Alfieri is judged incorrect by the same source. Open from April to October on weekends, 10.30-18.30; accessible by elevator.
Ancient half-cost mule track along the eastern shore of the lake, 68 km in six connected stages in 1992, reachable from the top of the Orrido; certified by the Touring Club between the walks.

At the height of Mount Xibet, the church was the first large collective construction of the Norman period; the monolithic columns were damaged by the earthquake of January 11, 1693. The tower, the only remnant of the ancient castle and today bell tower, is the oldest building in the municipality and was the base of the army of Ruggero d'Altavilla during the siege of Enna.
Space and light in the center.
An intact village between pine trees and the sea.
Pineta next to the Town Hall of Piazza Tasso, with children's playground, mountain bike trails, sports fields, relaxation areas, Adventure Park and fountains.
A altarpiece of Frigimelica where a castle stood.

Collection of objects of peasant life, listed in a catalogue with detailed captions, designed to revive memories and make young people discover a world that seems very far away in time. Not indicated hours: contact the MiC card number (0863 948678).

In 1259 Chieri and Andezeno met in the village since 1034; in 1259 they met. Today we see an eighteenth-century farmhouse closed with barn, stable and a baroque chapel of the Madonna del Rosario, repainted at the beginning of the twentieth century; along the road, among the brambles, remain the walls and the wheel of the old watermill on the Rio Santena. You reach it on a tree-lined avenue.

Convent of the barefoot Carmelites founded in 1605 in an area rich in water and green. In 1612 Pietro Antonio Ferro, an exponent of Mannerism and one of the most representative artists of the seventeenth-century Lucan, frescoed the vault of the apse with stories of Christ and Our Lady, saints, prophets and virtues; the cloister is frescoed by his sons Carlo and Giovan Battista.
The profile you can see from all over the valley.
Highland after Giotto.
The walled village above the Roman city.
The memory of the twentieth century of Roman.

The Gigante di Pietra is built in 1095 on a naturally defended hill; the two side towers are in the city coat of arms since 1222 and in the atrium you can see the coats of arms of the Magdalone and the Alarçon de Mendoza.
