Fortress of 1542 on a project by Gian Giacomo dell'Acaya, about 8,500 square meters with lanceolate bastions; political prison between 1848 and 1852 and then pyrotechnic factory, has been restored since 1982.
A covered walk outside the center.
Medici and multicultural city-port, with fortresses, the canals of the Venice district, the historical market and the Terrazza Mascagni on the sea; home of Modigliani, Fattori and Mascagni.
Church of 1576 in Piazza del Ponte, with 17th century frescoes.
The terracotta of the fifteenth century.
Open from March to November
The city theatre with a museum dedicated to the soprano Alice Zeppilli.
according to the FAI the structure is almost unused for about a decade and opens only occasionally for events

Country 864 meters on the north shore of Lake Molveno, Orange Flag of the Touring with the center closed to traffic, in front of the Brenta Dolomites: the thirteenth-century church of San Vigilio, the Venetian water sawmill, the fortinas "napoleonici" on the lake and the Pradel plateau.

The village is located on a natural platform about 100 meters above sea level, inside the walls; you enter from an arched door in Piazza Vittorio Veneto, heart of the historic center. The origins date back to the Latin colony of Circei (VI-IV century BC); then it was property of the Templars, feud of the Caetans and fortress of the Papal State.
Stories of departures.
On the trail of Ötzi, at over 3,000 meters.
The view from the Karst on the gulf.
The castle of the Scandian plain.
Monastery of the XIV-XV centuries restored by the Municipality: it houses the Lapidary Museum with Roman funerary monuments and medieval and modern works, and a panoramic cloister on the countryside.
Cast gold and Parma painting away from the crowd.

In the hamlet of San Giovanni, attested around 1200, it preserves a cycle of frescoes from 1540-1541 attributed to Jacobino Longo (the date 1541 is on the fresco of Sant'Antonio Abate); neoclassical façade and bell tower of 1928.
Active since the nineteenth century, renovated by Attilio Amodeo after 1944 with stone of Favignana, closed in 1972; today it houses a unit of the Institute for Marine Environment Coast CNR.
The clock tower on the village.

Country at the foot of the Concarena, on the western side of the Camonica Valley, with a historic center largely fourteenth-century: it is known for the Sanctuary of the Way of the Cross, the "Capèle" with the life-size statues of Benjamin Simoni, and for the Holy Crus, the living Passion that is represented every ten years.
A walk between arches and stone doors.
The north beach is wide, sandy and with a shallow bottom, suitable for children; the south beach is sandy and pebble; in the middle the fishing and tourist port, with bike paths along the sea.
Rebuilt in 1675 as a collegiate of Saints James and Philip and then minor basilica; it preserves the statue of St. Revelli declared miraculous by Pius IX in 1856.

Calore is born from the slopes of Monte Cervati and runs crooked under the hill of the village, in some stretches rich in trout; there are canoeing championships. From the ancient mill      ÂDel Principe Â starts a path with an iron bridge of the nineteenth century, along stretches of river where the otter lives.
A legendary church in the pines.
Church of Lombard origin with Romanesque bell tower with two double windows; the recent restoration has highlighted the medieval structure and a crypt.
A seventeenth-century convent with works attributed to Vouet.
It preserves paintings and frescoes from the fifteenth century.
The yellow-green majolica domes.
The museum where glass and crystal were made.

The quadrangular crenellated tower of the 13th century, almost 40 meters high and recently restored, is connected by a high wall to the Doge's Palace, of supposed Angevin origin, on three floors and about 2,500 sqm: you can visit the Hall of representation with barrel vault, two courtyards and the hanging garden; on the vault the coat of arms of the Montalto di Tocco, last feudal.

Established in 1980, it covers 3,280 hectares (89% of the municipality) between about 1,670 and 3,280 meters, up to the Rognosa del Sestriere, the highest peak of the Val Chisone: larch, pine and pine crochet, chamois, ibex, marmots, deer, the wolf returned in the late nineties and over sixty species of birds including gipeto and royal eagle. In the villages of Seytes, Laval and Troncea; at the hill of Beth the mines of calcopite, where in 1904 an avalanche overwhelmed 81 miners. In winter it is a cross-country skiing destination.
He's guarding an Epiphany of Tintoretto.

A small town in the upper Tiber Valley, which is gathered around the 14th century Fortress, now the centre for contemporary art: the Deposition of Luca Signorelli in the Museum of Santa Croce, the octagonal collegiate church of Santa Maria della Reggia, the Franciscan churches and, on the hills, the abbey and hermitage of Montecorona.
The frescoes of Delitala.

The Academy Theatre.

Civic museum re-assembled in the new headquarters in July 2021 according to the researches of Ester Fornara Borla, in three sections: tapestries and fabrics made between 1910 and 1935 by Elena Mars Albert and collaborators, a frame of late nineteenth century still working and a collection of linens, clothes and accessories between the end of the nineteenth and first half of the twentieth century. Visits only by reservation.

Set up in an ex-church restored with European funds (on the portal dated 1363; inside remains an inscription of consecration of 1696), it collects agricultural tools, wheat-feast branches and the reproduction in wheat and straw of the Holy Door of St. Peter, paraded at the feast of 2000 and blessed that year by the Pope in Rome. The track is a carriage without wheels that slides on two wooden shoes; for the feast the ears, softened in water, are woven in figures such as the ball, the niche, the cone and the hair. Times not indicated by the MiC card: contact the Municipality (0874 710134).

Probably born as a church of Basilian rite in the second half of the thirteenth century, in the sixteenth century it passed to the Carmelites, who built next to it the convent today seat of the Town Hall; from 1649 it had the title of Santa Maria del Carmine and from 1767 it housed the lay Congregation of the Most Immaculate, from which the name "Congrega" was given. The wooden door entirely carved is from the 17th century, with a stone frame attributed to Costantino Licursi and Cesare Capparelli. Inside a sixteenth-century canvas of the Annunciation, probably by Pietro Negroni, and the wooden statue of the Immaculate of Carlo Santoro.
The city up.

The Accademia degli Zelanti, founded in 1671, is housed in a neoclassical palace by Mariano Panebianco; the library preserves hundreds of thousands of volumes, with incunabula, and the art gallery painted from the seventeenth to the twentieth century (Pietro Paolo and Alessandro Vasta, Vito D'Anna, Giuseppe Sciuti, Saru Spina). Also displayed are the eighteenth-century carriage of the Senate of Acaese, the Greek-Roman bust found in Capomulini in 1675, weapons, minerals, coins and fossils.
A Marian shrine linked to the cherry festival.
In the old restored railway station of the historic center, ancient tools of winemaking and vine cultivation, with information point, wine shop and laboratory space.
The start of the Way of the Cross towards Santo Stefano.

Built after the earthquake of 1783, it has 10 ramps and 80 steps between colorful houses and the wall of the walls of Palazzo Valensise; it starts from an alley next to the Duomo and goes down to Via Muraglie, where the city center stood before 1783. Nearby, the ruins of the Dominican convent on which stands Palazzo Valensise.
The woods on the hill.

Small village of Sarcidano, at the border with the Marmilla, at the foot of the hill of Santu Antine with the remains of a Punic fortress and one of the deepest sacred Nuragic wells of Sardinia; about a third of the Giara di Gesturi falls in its territory, with the Museo del Cavallino della Giara and the Paleo Archeo Centro.

The parish church of San Nicolao and of the Assumption, built between 1644 and 1649, with a Latin cross and a single nave; the church of the Confraternity of Santa Marta, with a smooth and harmonious façade; the Sanctuary of the Madonna of Loreto, of 1681; the church of Santa Maria dell'Isola, dating back to about the year 1000.

In the western wing of the Apostolic Palace, founded at the end of the nineteenth century together with the restorations of the basilica of Giuseppe Sacconi. He exhibited the hall of Lorenzo Lotto, who spent the last few years in Loreto, with works for the choir of the basilica such as the Baptism of Christ and the Presentation at the Temple; five-sixth-century pharmacy majolica of Spezieria, seventeenth-century Flemish tapestries on drawings by Raffaello, a silver crucifix of Giambologna, ex-vote and a section of contemporary art. Open every day 10-13 and 15-18.

Western gate of the city with fortified bridge, built in 1360-62 for Francesco il Vecchio da Carrara on a project by Francesco da Schicci, once surrounded by water; the blackbirds are a nineteenth-century addition.
A village-museum on the hill between two valleys.
In the hamlet of Montarsiccio, at 788 meters, the remains of a castle documented from the 11th century, where in 1298 Ubertino Landi died, founder of the feudal dynasty of the Landi.
The volcano eruptions are always active.
Contemporary Art Collection of the Province, with Painters (1921-24) by Anselmo Bucci.

On the Varano hill, where the open-air excavations began in 1950 with Libero D'Orsi: villa of about 11,000 square meters with Corinthian columns atrium, spa district, large swimming pool with exedra, frescoed reception rooms and upper garden with tortile columns. Stabiae was a place of holiday; in one of his villas Pliny the Elder died.
Medieval alleys on the Greek Sila.
The three beaches not to be missed, from crystal clear water.
A place of memory on the hill.

One of the oldest areas of the city, at the foot of the Rocchetta and near the medieval walls: the houses rest on large blocks of rock, the "marocche" (marocche), from which the neighborhood takes its name.
The medieval farm of Rendena.
Get off at the village between farmsteads and castle, during the Törggelen season.
The hamlet of Bari, a hamlet gathered around a sixteenth-century tower of sighting against pirates, overlooking the marina at the mouth of Lama Giotta.
The symbol of the village, on the river.

Port excavated entirely in the rock in the Roman age (1st century BC-I century AD), on average three meters deep and sheltered from winds and marshes, with tanks for live fish and premises for repairs and deposits; in the caves today diving, restaurants and bars.
The port in the rock.
The beach of the city, called velvet beach.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione at the foot of the Sila Piccola and home of the painter Mattia Preti, the Cavaliere Calabrese, whose paintings can be seen in the Civic Museum, in the former Dominican convent, and in the churches of San Domenico and Santa Barbara; in the municipal territory includes Villaggio Mancuso, on the edge of the Sila National Park.

Main element of the Ecomuseum, built and managed by the Paneveggio Park, salt from Caoria (850 m) to Malga Vesnota di Sopra (1850 m) with thematic links between rural buildings of the subsistence economy, in four areas: village, meadows, forest and pastures. It starts from the Casa del Sentiero Etnographico, open from 28 June to 13 September 9-12 and 15-18:30; guided tours by reservation.
Art of the twentieth century a short walk from the beach.
Medieval porticos and a palace from Vittone's school.
The ancient church of the city.
Ostuni's Woman, mother 25,000 years ago.
A Romanesque church covered in baroque.
Gubbio's most playful tradition.
Medieval plant of houses leaned on by red roofs, with beautiful views of the vineyards; Casa Cotto of the 13th century, a strong house of a family of bankers, is the oldest residence.
Panoramic views of the Rubicon valley.
A brief pilgrimage among the larch trees.
No museum in the world has so many works of Guercino.
The heart of the country's life.
A maze of narrow streets scented by wineries and oil mills, with Palazzo Pappi, a noble residence in Lecce stone in Catalan-durazzesco style.

Municipal museum in the palace on Piazza del Popolo, with permanent works by artists of the figurative arts, temporary exhibitions and meetings; open Tuesday-Friday 9-13 and 15-18, Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 16-19, Monday closed.
A walk through the Liberty facades.
The panoramic terrace on the gulf.
Small round temple of the first century BC on the acropolis: ten of the eighteen Corinthian columns remain; perhaps dedicated to Vesta or Tiburno, mythical founder of the city.

Municipality of the Vibonese Serre, rebuilt on the plateau of Ciano after the floods of 1951 and 1972-73; in the territory the megaliths of the stones 'castedrati', the Old habited and the new church with the majolica of Pietro Cascella.
The little 14th-century cloister.
The oldest square.

Along the road from Chiusa to Villandro, documented from 1303 and rebuilt after a fire around 1400 with Gothic starry vault; a single nave with lateral tower, has a neo-Gothic altar of about 1870 with the two Valentine's Day next to the Madonna and geometric ornaments of the Style Bello.

In the former convent of the Filippines, the evolution of footwear over the centuries: ethnological section, reconstruction of the shop of the slippers, the footwear industry Marche and shoes of famous characters, including Pope John Paul II. Open from Thursday to Sunday and holidays.
Walking in the Sicans.

At the foot of the Schiara and the Monti del Sole, at the gates of the Bellunesi Dolomites National Park, Sedico combines the protohistoric castle of Noal, the 16th century oratory of San Nicolò in Bribano, the neoclassical villa of Giuseppe Jappelli ai Patt with the historical Museum of the 7th Alpine Regiment and the cycle path of the ancient roges along the Cordevole.
Casatorre and lake view in a medieval village.
13th century cathedral basilica with a severe and square appearance; in the square in front of the lively baroque fountain known as the "Four Fountains."
The parish from which the village was born.

Small mountain village of Carnia, in the But valley, known as the open-air Bible for mosaics, photo-ceramics and paintings with biblical theme on the walls of the houses; it houses the parish church of San Martino and a historic center of ancient Carnic houses.

The eighteenth-century parish church of Our Lady of the Rosary, in the center of the village on a large churchyard, houses three paintings (the Virgin of the Rosary of the seventeenth century, the Pentecost of 1874 and the Purging Souls of 1927) and two marble lions. In front of it stands Santa Croce, in 1677, the seat of the fraternity that takes care of the rites of Holy Week. In the village also St. Peter (XVII century) and the Purgatory (XVIII century).

Already in 1514 the pastoral visit recorded two chaplains, one hospital and seven chapels or altars. Longitudinal plan with three naves with side chapels and in the transepts, vaulted on the central nave and cruising on the side; on the vault the fresco of the Annunciation painted in 1749 by Giovanni Cosenza, then the main altar in marble inlaid with two putti and a wooden choir with two sections decorated by two griffi.

An eighteenth-century building built on a former pottery factory, home to one of the most important families in the country; it was the night of Gioacchino Murat and the pink room with a canopy bed is preserved.
It preserves the cycle of frescoes of the Stories of the Virgin and of the Magdalene and the altarpiece of the Madonna degli Aranci di Gaudenzio Ferrari.
One of the highest water jumps in Europe.
Outside the castle, the open-air museum dedicated to the cultivation of vines, winemaking and wine traditions of Langhe, Roero and Monferrato.
The craft of the Aramai, live.
The exotic garden.
The oldest grappa house in Italy, at the entrance of the bridge, with atmosphere of the late eighteenth century.

On Castrum Leonis Romano, destroyed and rebuilt several times, strengthened by Lucca with five towers; walls 740 meters long and high up to 17. In the summer you visit the brigands' cells in the mastium.
A rare Roman furnace almost intact in the mountains.
The humble origins of the greatest opera composer.
The Salerno baroque.
€3 (no reduced); also included in the state cumulative from €7 with Mausoleum and Palace of Theodoric
The wine of the Castles in the old station.
The stone village overlooking the Valpolicella.
The pentagonal fortress desired by Cosimo I, with high bastions and 360 degree view of the city; below, the park of Prato, shady and suitable for children.
A fairy tale walk for the little ones.

In the former Romanesque church of San Silvestro (XI century) and in the Bishop's Palace: gold-bottomed tables from the XII to the XVI century, paintings, silver and vestments, with a Byzantine mosaic of the VIII century, a Madonna of Taddeo di Bartolo and the San Michele di Antonio da Castello.

Housed in the ancient granaries of the convent of the Carmelite Fathers Scalzi, it collects tools and tools for spinning and weaving hemp, linen and silk, personal and domestic linens, sacred vestments and naturalistic collections of silkworms, chrysalis and butterflies. The path follows the production cycles: for silk from the baco to the finished product, for hemp and flax from plant collection to fabric.

Borgo del Salento at the foot of the Serra Magnone, with one of the most beautiful historical centers in the area: alleys without cars and stairs around the sixteenth century Castello Risolo, the underground oil mills excavated between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries and the convent of the Black Franciscans with the 36-column crypt.

Medieval village in the heart of the Lanzo Valleys, famous for the fourteenth-century Devil's Bridge on the Stura and the Giant's Marmittes; in the historic center the Aymone Gate and Civic Tower of Challant and the Castle Tower, as well as small museums dedicated to minerals, rocks, textile art and mountaineering. Here, according to tradition, a Lanzian doctor invented the breadsticks for the Sabauda court.

Built between 1542 and 1587, probably extending an older church, on the slope above the town to defend itself from the streams and full of the San Carlo stream; it preserves numerous paintings of St. Nicholas. Open every day 9-17.

Inside the Baita Monte Cauriol, in Sadole (1,600 m), a collection of relics of the First World War found in Val Sadole and in Ziano, collected by Aldo Zorzi and others; the hut also has a small library on the Great War and the mountain. It is reached from the village of Bosin by via Sadole, about 8 km partly dirt road with about 600 m of altitude difference, by car or on foot. Free visit in summer, closed in winter.

The last municipality of Valle Aurina, with the hamlet of Casere: here copper was extracted for over five hundred years, today told by the Provincial Museum of Mines in the gallery of Sant'Ignazio; at the end of the valley the church of Santo Spirito, consecrated in 1455, and a 20 km path between farms and antiquities.

Borgo del Maceratese linked to Bishop Nicolò Bonafede, who had the palace-fortress built at the beginning of the sixteenth century, now the town hall and restored Santa Maria della Pietà in Telusiano, where the Crucifixion of Lorenzo Lotto of 1531; in the town hall the collection of ancient drawings by Alessandro Maggiori is preserved.

Belvedere with benches above the city: in 1494 the young Albrecht Dürer, on his way to Italy, drew Closed from here; the drawing is lost, but the engraving remains You will arrive in about 30 minutes on foot from the parish, through the bridge of Sant'Andrea and the path n. 5 to Albions.

Built around 1210 by the masters of the Abbey of Fossanova, with Gothic-borgognoni influences; it preserves remains of a fifteenth-century ciborium and, on the high altar, a thirteenth-century table of the Madonna and Child. Since 1947 it has been the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Graces.

Romanesque church of the 11th century in the center of the village, with simple and pure lines: unique ornaments of the flat pilasters of the apse and the double windows of the bell tower with blind arches. Inside, frescoes from the end of the fourteenth century with Christ the Pantocrator, the parable of the Virgins, the Fathers of the Church, the Apostles and the Evangelists. Visitable on weekends.

Opened in 1989 in one of the oldest houses in the village to recover the memory of the peasant and occitane traditions, it reconstructs a typical house with bedroom, kitchen, exhibition room with tools and Occitan clothes, attic with the ancient oven, stable and cellar; there is also a photographic section. Telephone 0982 94663.
High mountain and memories of the Great War by car or bike.

Built in the eighteenth century and then renovated and enlarged, it preserves paintings of Bignami, stained glass windows designed by Luigi Morgari and a bezel by the painter Vittorio Viviani, nineths of adoption.
Church of the XIII century in Romanesque Apulian, founded on the initiative of Blessed Nicola da Giovinazzo, with the thirteenth-century rose window and the Chapel of the Persio family.

In the present form of the fifteenth century, it was consecrated in 1455 by Cardinal Nicolò Cusano; it rises in an alpine basin at the end of the valley considered a place of energy and peace, with benches for the rest and one of the best photographic views of the area. There passes the Path of Health (6,6 km, about 2 hours) which also crosses the historical area of the mines, the house of the miners of Mösern with its chapel and the deviation to the Röt waterfall.
Ponte di epoca romana also known as Santa Lucia or Ponte Murato, with a painting that recalls the passage of the Holy Shroud.
The farm-house of the Bourbons, reborn after years of abandonment.

The narrow streets paved in silex, the doorposts and the external stairs show the art of the local stonemasons, so skilled that they paved several streets of Rome, including Piazza San Pietro; in the municipal villa there is the monument to the stonemason.

Aqueduct called Aqua Salsa, built in the first decades of the 1st century A.D. in Auguste to bring to Brescia the water of the valley of Lumezzane with an underground path of about 20 km. Discovered in via Antonini during the excavations of the Sewerage Collector of the Trompia Valley, it was partly removed and relocated near the town hall, with restoration curated by the Archaeology Superintendence of Lombardy.

Country of the Lanzo Valleys on the Stura, attested since 1034, with the parish church of the Santi Grato and Rocco, two small museums of rural life (the objects of daily use and the wine of the Society of Workers) and the panoramic path of Monte Momello towards the Sanctuary of Sant'Ignazio.

Beyond the narrowing of the gorges, between high limestone walls inhabited by the Apennine suede, the remains of the Benedictine abbey appear, brought to light entirely from the archaeological excavations of 2009: the ruins of the abbey and the guesthouse range from the IX to the XV century. It is one of the monastic rocks of the Park. The H1 ring from the village (gorges, monastery, green springs and Terravecchia) takes about 3 hours, with 150 m of altitude difference, difficulty E.

The seat of the Town Hall since 1862, takes its name from the Trotti, who took over in 1739 from the Secco Borella who gave it the present form; towards the park it has the U pattern of the villas of Lombard delight. The interior has three cycles of mythological frescoes: the rooms of Cleopatra, Semiramide, Hercules and Minerva (1705-1706), the room of Bacchus attributed to Carlo Donelli called the Vimercati and the rooms painted around 1750 by the Ticino Giuseppe Antonio Orelli.

Born in the 16th century with a single nave on a terrace overlooking the village, damaged by earthquakes, it was rebuilt in Baroque style and enlarged with two naves thanks to Father Agostino Arace (1718-1764). It has four altars, the largest in polychrome marble with a wooden statue of the Virgin, seven chapels and a wooden choir of the eighteenth century; the bell tower was probably a feudal defensive tower. The village of the hinterland of Siracusa, between gentle hills and countryside; on Piazza del Plebiscito overlook the Mother Church of St. Paul the Apostle, started in 1764, and the eighteenth-century Palazzo Requisenz, residence of the lords of the feud.

The centerpiece of the city's expansion to the sea, designed by Pietro Augustoni in 1779; was at Mass Franz Liszt, who played the organ Callido. Step of the Lisztian itinerary with Palazzo Fenili, where the musician stayed, and the square with the bronze statue of Sisto V by Aldo Sergiacomi (1984).

Protected area of 640 hectares among the rice fields, with reservoirs always flooded surrounded by reeds and humid woods of willows, white poplars, black alders and farnies. It is above all a place for birdlife: royal germans, ladles, blackberries, garzettes, herons and major whites, nitticolar and a large colony of sacred ibis. Started in 1748 on a project by Pietro Bernasconi, with the works entrusted to Carlo Patturelli, and finished in 1791 after several interruptions; the tufa of the parts above ground comes from the local quarries used also for the Palace of Caserta. It develops on two levels: at the top the cult hall, which is accessed by a large churchyard fenced above the road; under the moat, ancient cemetery and ossuary dug into the tuff, with two rooms sometimes on rows of pillars. The façade, about 30 meters by 32, is marked by semi-colons and pilasters with ionic capitals and Corinthians.

Wanted by the judges of Gallura in three phases between the second half of the 11th and the middle of the 12th century, it is the most important religious monument of north-eastern Sardinia: three naves in local granite, about 33 for 13 meters and 12 high, on a hill once outside the walls. It is dedicated to Bishop Simplicius, martyr on May 15, 304; in 1614 under the high altar were found the relics of the Saints Simplicius, Rosula, Diocletian and Fiorenzio. In the area a Roman necropolis of about 450 tombs; in mid-May the feast of the patron with costume procession and Palio della Stella.

In Castel San Zeno, the oldest part of the fortifications (1242), the museum has archaeological sections from prehistoric to Roman times (with the stele of the gens Vassidia), a medieval and modern section with works by Paduanino and Antonio Zanchi and a map of 1566-75, and a musical section on tenors Giovanni Martinelli and Aureliano Pertile. The mast, about 38 meters high, offers a view of the plain and the Euganean and Berici Hills.

Small mountain town of the Valle Cannobina, 812 meters above sea level: in Piazza della Repubblica the parish church of the Nativity of Mary and the ethnographic museum of Gurro and Valle Cannobina, with costumes, furnishings and tools of the life of the past.
Romanesque church of the thirteenth century, already of the Knights of Malta, built on the remains of a Roman bridge of Augustan age of the Via Flaminia.

Fortress with four circular bastions in shoe, of Lombard origin or of the IX century, documented from the XII century with Guglielmo d'Altavilla; at the end of the sixteenth century Carlo Gesualdo transformed it into a Renaissance court with a theatre, open to musicians and poets. Since 1855 of the Caccese, which rebuilt the façade, was severely damaged by the earthquake of 1980 and, restored since 2000, reopened at the end of 2015; it hosts concerts and events dedicated to the prince. Saturday and Sunday 10-13.30 and 15.30-19, weekdays by reservation.

On the hill at 490 m, among secular trees, the sanctuary was born from the conversion of the young Lenole Gabriele Mattei, who according to tradition on 15 September 1602 found among the thorns and thorns a early Christian image of the Virgin with the Child, among the oldest in Europe, and collected alms throughout Europe to build around the church, consecrated on 8 September 1610 and elevated to the Papal Basilica in 2015. The interior with a single nave preserves the eighteenth-century painting of the Virgin attributed to the architect Ambrini; in the churchyard there is the Mosaic of the Emigrants and from the travertine of the façade grow for more than four centuries the cypresses of the "miracle of the Cypresses." Open every day 8-18:30, in summer 8-20:30.

The oldest place of worship in the country, dating from the construction characteristics around the middle of the thirteenth century, on a building previously perhaps Byzantine; it belonged to the Vallombrosan abbey of Thamis and was then used as a granite mountain, until the first documented restoration of 1859. It has a unique nave with semicircular apse, sandstone and trachyte cones, facade with false loggias, bifora, sail bell tower and portal with monolithic architrave; inside capitals with vegetable decorations and a face carved on the monophora of the apse.
At about 1 km from the village, near Mount Pasillo (588 m), the remains of the castle belonged to the Nobili family, whose original shape cannot be reconstructed.

Capo Berta closes the Gulf of Dianese to the west (on the east there is Capo Cervo) and is a protected area crossed by the Aurelia and climbed from Milan-Sanremo. On the cliffs grow gariga of rosemary, thyme, broom and dwarf palm, pine forests of Aleppo pine trees and endemic species such as Limonium cordatum and Campanula Sabatia; in the sea there are prairies of Posidonia oceanica. At the highest point, 267 m in the hamlet of Diano Gorleri, stands the Torre dell'Alpicella, circular fortification in masonry of the XIV-XV century, probably a sighting tower; you arrive from Via Diano Calderina following the signs.

Medieval stone village on the slopes of the Corno Piccolo, in the National Park of Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, with houses from the fifteenth century, the churches of San Giovanni (1432) and San Rocco (1530); in the territory the ski resort of Prati di Tivo and the hamlet of Intermesoli.

Piazza Cito is the heart of the village, with the elegant Palazzo Cito; the side of the sixteenth-century Chiesa Matrice di San Leonardo, with two bell towers, overlooks the square. The historic center retains an architecture of great value and beauty.
One of the largest Messapian cities in Salento.

The Roman Laumellum, post office station on the road between Pavia and France, where according to tradition they married Teodolinda and Agiulfo; today it is the village of Lomellina with one of the oldest baptisteries in Italy, San Giovanni ad Fontes, next to the proto-Romanesque basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, and with the Castle Crivelli frescoed, seat of the Municipality, and some sections of the ancient walls.

The Hermitage, of medieval origin, with the sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the Rescue, is flanked by an archaeological park where copies of the anthropomorphic stele, menhir of the Bronze Age are displayed.

Wanted by the Council of the Forties in 1621 and started in 1630 under the Barberini on a plant of the Vignola, it received the visit of Urban VIII in 1641 and was elevated to a minor basilica in 1845, when Gregory XVI was welcomed. Baroque façade on the main square; the ceiling is frescoed with work attributed to Domenico Pistrini and the altar, a sarcophagus of the second century, preserves the martyrs Sixtus and Bonifacio. It is the departure of the sixth stage of the Way of St. Francis.

On a river terrace at about 580 m, on the right of the Serio at the confluence with Val Nossana, it is probably the Parra Oromobiorum Oppidum cited by Plinio. In 1883 there was found a storeroom of bronzes of the fifth century B.C. (the saved part is at the Civic Archaeological Museum of Bergamo); eleven excavation campaigns between 1983 and 1994 have exposed 2,300 m2 of an inhabited area of over 13,000 m2, founded in the final Bronze and lived until the Roman conquest, with stone houses and wood of "alpine house" type. Opened to the public since 2014, it includes the park (Sector A) and the Antiquarium with pottery, ornaments, coins and instruments, which illustrates in particular the processing of copper, bronze and lead.

Villa nobiliaryi of the eighteenth century spread over the municipal territory to form a mosaic, along with numerous kind speakers; among these Villa Seghetti Panichi, already Odoardi, born on a military fortification of the Odoardi of Ascoli.

Begin in 1573 and completed in 1613 by the will of Cornelia Delli Monti, widow of the feudal lord Giovan Battista I Protonobilisssimo, on the ruins of a Byzantine church on the site of the medieval farmhouse of Brongo. The austere façade has two baroque portals finely carved; inside, with a Greek cross, three altars of the late seventeenth century and, on the main altar, a sculptural group of Placido Buffelli of Alessano.

The heart of the city, with the well of Griffins and Lions designed by Antonio da Sangallo and the Gothic Town Hall in travertine, whose crenellated tower rises with an internal staircase up to the panorama of Valdichiana and Val d'Orcia.
The most important example of Romanesque architecture in the Aosta Valley, with three naves with Gothic vaults and late Gothic frescoes in the attic.

14th-century castle overlooking the village above Merano, home of the Counts of Merano and still inhabited by the same family; it is partly surrounded by the moat: a bridge leads to the entrance, beyond the prison, to the courtyard from which an open staircase rises to the halls. In the halls and halls a gallery of paintings and portraits, a collection of historical weapons and art objects of Tyrolean history, relics of Archduke John and a majolica stove in the Renaissance Hall of the Knights. Country of Val Chisone linked to the RIV, the company of ball bearings founded in 1906, and to the Agnelli family: you can visit the Museum of mechanics and bearing, the working villages wanted by Giovanni Agnelli, the anti-aircraft shelters of 1943 and the Baroque parish of San Pietro in Vincoli.
A Benedictine rock church of the Lombard period dug along the Gravina di Picciano, discovered in 1963: the walls have the Virgin Queen, the Archangels and a cycle with the Creation and Original Sin.

Karst complex about 5 km from the village, which the Touring Club has included among the ten most beautiful caves in Italy: a route on suspended walkways of about 500 meters between red rocks, white stalactites and lakes fed by the underground rivers Placido and Rapido, with the Pozzo Rodriguez 23 meters deep and a stalagmitic column of 7 meters. In the Archaeological Chamber were found many oil lamps, a sign of a cult of water already pre-nuragic; in the lakes lives the Stenasellus nuragicus. Visit of about an hour, every day 9:30-17.
The sea of the Ulysses Riviera.
At the bottom of a sheltered cove, alle Grazie, the archaeological area preserves the oldest oil mill in Liguria, with the large oil cell for at least 50 jars; since 2025 there is a new museum.
Built between 1337 and 1346, with the bell tower reminiscent of the Torre del Mangia, the coats of arms of the Sienese and Medici podestàs and the gogna next to the main portal.
A Renaissance masterpiece.
Guided tour €17, reduced €8
The plastic icons of Italian design in the factory where they were born.
The heart of Venice.

Castle built in the 13th century, developed around three quadrangular courtyards with towers and a courtyard with drawbridge; the Visconti settled there in 1448, when Francesco and Guido Visconti took refuge during contrasts with the Ambrosian Republic, and the halls of representation were frescoed since 1590, with interiors renewed in Baroque taste. You can visit the staircase, the private chapel, the Royal Chamber and unusual collections: shaving dishes, 360 stuffed birds, arms and Spanish armor of the sixteenth century and finds of the civilization of Golasecca. Open from April to October on Sundays and on holidays (10-11.45 and 14-18); free under 6 years, reduced for children 6-12 years and members FAI and TCI.

Rocky formations of the seabed a few miles from the shore, reachable by diving; the name comes from the fishermen, who saw there entangle the nets. Those in front of Chioggia are described as the largest and most spectacular of the Adriatic, so much so that they are called Adriatic coral reefs, oasis of biodiversity.
The Florentine Renaissance on the course.
In the former convent of the Carmelite Fathers of Via Roma, today seat of the municipal offices; the main altar is carved in Lecce stone in late Baroque style, with three paintings by Saverio Lillo.
Currently not accessible according to source
Few remains of the 13th century, in memory of the destruction ordered by the Count of Savoy against the lords of Jovençan.

The old town, on a hill overlooking the Gargano and the Dauni Mountains, preserves traces of the various dominations; there are the Baronial Palace, formerly residence of the Carafa and Gonzaga families, the church of St. Paul the Apostle, the first of the village, and the church of St. Nicholas.
A church among olive trees and legends.
The donkey-back bridge of the devil's legend.
Piazza overlooking the sea in the hamlet of Piazza, with the seventeenth-century church restored after the war; since 1967 it hosts on summer nights the Theatre Festival of Borgio Verezzi, born here.

The origins date back to the Byzantines, who during the Greek-Gothic war (535-553) fortified the promontory to defend the landing places; the current structure is Aragonese, from the end of the fifteenth century, with the entrance elevated on high arches and drawbridge and the monumental portal in tuff beating. It has a triangular plan with three circular towers, a large dry moat and walls with a walk of covered rounds, blackbirds and wounds; inside the square of arms, today garden and theatre, the hall of the French to the north and the baronial building to the east. In summer, the municipality indicates opening every day 10-13 and 16-19, in winter reduced hours; guided tours by reservation (Tourist Office 0974 827480).
Where he ruled the free Republic of Carnia.
The most elegant palace in the square.

Private museum of vintage cars founded by Mario Righini, with about 350 vehicles: among them the Auto Avio Costruzioni 815 of 1940, the first car built by Enzo Ferrari before his factory, and the Alfa Romeo 2300 8C belonged to Tazio Nuvolari, as well as Ferrari models, Mercedes-Benz, Isotta Fraschini and Rolls-Royce.
Frescoed salons that open with exhibitions.

The village of the Modena Apennines at 797 m, gathered around the Rocca dei Montecuccoli, which in summer 1944 was the seat of the Partisan Republic of Montefiorino and today houses the museum of the Resistance; in the territory the Romanesque parish church of Rubbiano, the parish church of Vitriola with tower houses and stretches of the Via Bibulca.

Sanctuary about 800 meters in the woods of Subasio, 4 km from Assisi, where Francis and the first companions withdrew in prayer; This is a place that is secluded. You can visit the Cave of San Francesco, the cloister with the well, the oratory of Santa Maria and the Maddalena chapel; it was expanded at the beginning of the fifteenth century by the will of San Bernardino da Siena.
Nuraghe on the outskirts of Lunamatrona, on a 200 m hill, with a central tower and four secondary towers.

Small beach at the crescent at the mouth of the river Trottu, sheltered from the winds, closed by a promontory that degrades to the cliffs and from rocks and Mediterranean maquis; there is a abandoned granite quarry and the name comes from "su molentu" (the donkey carrying the extracted material).
In the Villa La Rinchiostra the museum of the Massese sculptor, dedicated to research on marble and light.
A fourteenth-century sanctuary linked to a legend of pilgrims.

The port was Etruscan port and Carthaginian port (Punicum); the Romans built villas there and the Barberini expanded it in the sixteenth century. The castle, erected by Barberini incorporating the watchtower wanted after the decree of Pius V of 1567, passed in 1773 to the Hospital of Santo Spirito and in 1887 to the Odescalchi princes.
The bronze cross of the 11th century.

Ancient Romanesque church with a single nave overlooking the square of Incino, with square bell tower of the 11th century; it preserves a Romanesque sculpture (X-XI century) in the bezel of the portal, a 1212 holy waterworks, a wooden crucifix and a fresco of the 15th century, while the old canon has three fourteenth-century windows. For centuries it was the reference of the parish, until in 1574 St. Charles moved it to Santa Maria Nascente.
The parish with wooden sculptures.
visits on request (tel. 0942 744950)
Church of the seventeenth century with an Annunciation frescoed in the bezel above the portal; inside a wooden triptych in tempera with the central compartment signed by the Pesina.
The Baroque Camoun of the parish.

In the left wing of the monastery of San Francesco, six rooms exhibit about 300 of the more than 1,600 finds collected by the historical and archaeologist of Irsinian Michele Janora, mainly from necropolis of the Eastern Basilicata and north-western Puglia, from the Neolithic to the Hellenistic age. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 10-20, Sunday 10.30-20, closed on Monday.

On the Colle Santa Maria: legend tells that a hermit, trying to sculpt the face of the Lord in an olive tree trunk, saw that of Our Lady appear. Little remains of the hermitage and the church, but the pilgrims still come to worship the miraculous statue.

Founded in 1966 around the works acquired with the National Visual Arts Award of the city, established in 1950; since 2009 it is managed by a Foundation with founding members the Ministry of Culture and the Municipality, and since 19 March 2010 it has new name and headquarters in Via De Magri, with permanent collection, exhibitions and educational activities. Tuesday-Friday 10-18, Saturday and Sunday 11-19, Monday closed.
Canyon, river and trails on the old railroad.

Founded in 1796 on the initiative of Count Giacomo Carrara, it houses more than 600 masterpieces by Botticelli, Raffaello, Tiziano, Lotto, Moroni and Canaletto, in a five-century itinerary of Italian painting.
The Diocese Museum houses the ivory chair of Maximian and the archbishop's chapel, the only preserved early Christian Orthodox chapel.

28 km from Sant'Anatolia di Narco alle Cascate delle Marmore on the route of the former Spoleto-Norcia railway, between bridges and tunnels, through Scheggino, Ceselli, Arrone and Ferentillo; easy, with a more demanding final stretch.
One hundred frescoed rooms.
Extremeness of the promontory from which you embrace the three branches of the Lario with the mountains in the background, a view celebrated by poets and writers.
In the hamlet of Carda, it houses a polyptych by Mariotto di Cristofano dated 1425 and a canvas by Pontenani.
The harp on the Crati.
Canova and the Lombard and Venetian painting by the lake.
The balcony on Grivola.
According to legend, the gate appeared during the nocturnal invocations of a sorcerer apprentice, whom the devil imprisoned forever.

Venetian villa of the end of the 17th century of the Counts of Claricini, arrived from Bologna to Cividale in the thirteenth century: central body with pediment, two wings, rustic, lemon and chapel of Santa Croce (about 1700) with paintings by Lucilius Candido. Since 1971 it has been home to a foundation: the museum preserves paintings by Giacomo and Antonio Carneo, Sebastiano Bombelli and works attributed to Palma il Giovane, Pomponio Amalteo and Pordenone, furniture, fabrics, weapons and prints. Around the Italian garden and a park with trees from the late eighteenth century. Open to the public on request.
Limestones and wild orchids behind the beach.
The nature of the Strait and the Swordfish.
Sacred art next to the Duomo.

At the first level of the thirteenth-century Torre Frumentaria, in front of the Forum Emiliano: sculptures and architectural marbles including a circular ara Augustea with bucrani, an altar dedicated to Traiano, the Telamone in ancient yellow called Founded in 1894 by Pio Capponi, reordered last time in 1999.
Panorama of the Apennines.
The rural life of Novara, with a view of the rose.

Well temple dedicated to the cult of the waters, of the recent Bronze (XIII century B.C.) and frequented until the early Iron Age, discovered in 1953: about seven meters high, in cones of trachite and basalt leaning on a wall of shale from which flows the spring. A vestibule with seat counters and four steps lead to the small chamber with paved tholos; the double sloping cover has a double sculpted eaves and a triangular pediment, with an acroterium that held twenty votive bronze swords; in the cockpit bronze of tenderers and warriors have emerged. From the village follow the signs, then an asphalted road at the cemetery to the archaeological area and a walking path of several hundred meters.
The Turin market.

Since 1936 in the residence of the Moscow family: the Pala di Pesaro by Giovanni Bellini, works by Vitale da Bologna, Tintoretto, Guido Reni and Mattia Preti, the Renaissance majolica of the Mazza collection and, in the courtyard, the Medusa by Ferruccio Mengaroni; also houses the Sonosphere.
Bruno Munari and contemporary art in a historic building.

The centre has its ancient character, with brick buildings and towers and palaces Santinelli, Grifoni, Clavari and Mercuri; the seventeenth-century Palazzo Fagnani has been a municipal seat since 1838.
A missing lake told along a ring.

Municipal Museum inaugurated on December 4, 1986 under the patronage of the BPD Defense and Space and the collaboration of the Archaeological Superintendence for Lazio: a continuous path of finds from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages. The main attraction is the life-size reconstruction of an elephant with straight fangs, lived in the area about 350,000 years ago. It has a specialist library, workshops and teaching room, and coordinates the archaeological mission at the castle of Piombinara.
In the bishop's palace of Piazza Prampolini, the museum of the diocese; in the façade is recognized the fifteenth-century Baptistery dedicated to St. John the Baptist.

The city of Frederick II at the foot of the Murge: the Cathedral with the crypt linked to the emperor's wives, the Porta Sant'Andrea with the inscription       Â Andria fidelis Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â
A waterfall at the bottom of the canyon.
€5, reduced €2 (18-25 years), free under 18 years
A gorge among carved rocks.
A flat path of 5.6 km across the plain to the mouth of the Ombrone.

Also known as Castel Fornace, it was the mother house of the Roccabruna: Romanesque fortified residence that became a castle since the fourteenth century, passed to the Gaudenti and the Counts of Giovanelli and was rebuilt more sumptuous in the sixteenth century. Sold to the Municipality in 1851, it was partly demolished since 1854 with the loss of rooms and frescoes; since 1992 it is municipal seat. The tower door remains with two slits, the eastern wing with traces of the oldest battlements, a court corner with porch and loggia and a restored solar clock.
The Gonzaghesque center between the square and the park.
The Municipality announces visits suspended for renovation works from Monday 8 May (year not indicated, page updated to January 2025): check the reopening
The seven-sided tower overlooking the Valdaso.
Church in Piazza Vittorio Emanuele, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1799, which preserves the fifteenth-century polychrome wooden statue of the Virgin with the Child called "Madonna dell'Impollata."

Born from the collection donated between 2001 and 2004 to the Province of Avellino by the architects Eirene Sbrizilo and Enzo De Felice and then entrusted to the Municipality, collects in about 250 square meters tools and tools of work of more centuries, Neapolitan nativity scenes with the figures of the crafts (scalpellino, typographer, carpenter, tinker, barber, blacksmith) and scenes of rural life. It also houses the archive of the Amatucci barons, which documents the relationships between owners and settlers. It is located in the basement of the 18th century baronial palace, bought by the Municipality in the 1980s and today municipal seat.

Inaugurated on 12 August 1984, it no longer houses the remains of Monte Pallano, removed after the intervention of the Superintendence; it contains photographic copies of parchments, maps, documents from the 18th to the 19th century, ancient postcards and the archaeological photographic exhibition of 1984. It follows the opening hours of the Town Hall.
MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day: contact the library (tel. 011 9801243)
Green and spring water a stone's throw from the center.
Two large monoliths among which rises the village, on Mount San Leonardo, overlooking the valley excavated by the Basento.

The Baroque was imposed by the reconstruction after the earthquake of 1693, with a new center built next to the ancient one; the UNESCO site includes isolated monuments of the historic center. From the area of the destroyed castle opens the view of the valley of the Anapo.

Parish in the Tuscan Gothic style built on the site of the little church of Santa Maria delle Torri, which became too small for pilgrims; restored in the eighteenth century in Piedmontese baroque, it has three naves and wooden roof. It preserves the wooden Christ who, according to tradition, sweated blood between 1612 and 1667 and attracts pilgrims from all over the island, and a sixteenth-century Trinity; feast from April 30 to May 3.

A labyrinth of narrow and winding alleys, steep steps and paved squares within the ramparts, remained almost intact over time. Among the historic buildings the Palazzo La Loggia, seat of the town hall, and the Palazzo di Eleonora d'Arborea; from the viewpoints of the promontory the view runs over the castle, the coast and towards the Asinara.

Built in the 13th century, destroyed and rebuilt in the 15th century and adapted to residence in the 17th century; since 1566 it is Doria, and the current owner, the Marquis Clemente Doria, lives there in summer. Almost cubic building on two floors plus the path of the round, on a fortified basement with remains of towers; on the first floor the hall of the coats of arms with fireplace of the late sixteenth century and the courtroom where the minor justice was administered, in the cellars the prisons. The legend of the Spectre of the Nun, Sister Constance Gentile, is linked to it.
The St. Christopher of Delitius under the porch.
The great cycle of Pietro Antonio Ferro.
The mother church of the village, with the bell of 1608.
Medieval village on the slopes of Monte Amiata, a land of chestnuts, with the Aldobrandesca Rocca and the Palio delle Contrade of 18 August.
The house that welcomed the Beautiful.
In the Mühltal valley, restored watermills that are a popular hiking destination in summer and winter, with a refreshment place for a snack.
The medieval walls.

The Ladin municipality of the Val Badia between the natural parks Puez-Odle and Fanes-Senes-Braies: in San Martin the thirteenth-century castle of Ciastel de Tor houses the Ladin Museum on the history and culture of the Ladin valleys, and in Lungiarü, the mountaineer village, the valley of the mills (Val di Morins) opens the ascent to the Sass de Putia.
The vintage cars of the queen and the general.

The monastery of the Reformed Fathers, built in the seventeenth century with the contribution of all families and delivered in 1634, has a square plan around the cloister; passed to the Municipality with the laws of 1866. The two-nave church contains paintings by Domenico Guarino (1721-1729), Peccheneda and the Solimena school, an eighteenth-century organ case, the cantoria of 1742, the monument to Emanuela Vitilio, who died of childbirth in 1712, and two crosses in mother-of-pearl of Byzantine origin.
A walled village of the Fermano remained almost intact.

Between via Matteotti, via Corridoni, via Carducci and the square meet the Pharmacy Bracchi and the House of Rigoletto, formerly House of the Madonnina, built in 1875 for Henri Caumont by the foreman Ludovico Tagliavini in neo-Gothic Swiss style with terracotta decorations. Along via Venturini the wall of the Caumont Caimi estate hides in part the villa, probably seventeenth-century, made neoclassical by the Counts Caimi after 1831.
Along the canal.
The church of Vallecrosia Alta was renovated in 1737 and the Baroque façade, with the statue of the saint above the portal, was completed in 1784; a nave in Ligurian Baroque style.

The highest part of the village is one of the oldest and best preserved, with cobbled streets, churches and ancient houses; the village was fortified in the twelfth century and the oldest nucleus preserves the defensive system in the path of roads and buildings. At the highest point stands the bell tower of St. Nicholas, originally a medieval tower of the 12th century of sighting and defence in large blocks of stone; the church of St. Nicholas, cited in documents of the 14th century and damaged by the earthquake of 1915, has on the façade the coat of arms of the legendary Duke Sarchia. The procession of the Saint goes up to the top of the village on May 1.

Complex of sanctuary and monastery of the XI-XII centuries at about 850 meters above sea level, frequented until the end of the sixties and today used as hostel. It is reached by the path of the Leccio.
Romanesque and Gothic together.
Exhibition on the old school, opened in 2001.
The crucifix of the legend of Dragut.
Alleys and towers overlooking the port.
Rosmini's house on the lake.
the source does not indicate time or access mode
The mountain life of the past.
The sky and the space to touch with your hand.
The Holy Face of Tagliacozzo.
Oasis of 12 hectares in the park of Palazzo Corsini at the foot of the Gianicolo: centuries-old trees, bamboo, palm trees, orchids and the Butterfly Eden with tropical butterflies.

Heart of the Costa Smeralda, with about 90 km of coast between Porto Cervo, Cannigione, Baja Sardinia and Poltu Quatu; inland the archaeological park gathers eight sites between the V and the II millennium BC, from the necropolis of Li Muri to the nuraghe La Prisgiona and the tombs of Giants of Coddu Vecchiu and Li Lolghi.
One of the oldest tuna processing factories in the Mediterranean, with guided tours and tastings of the preserves produced on the spot; the bluefin tuna is the symbol of Carloforte.
Wonderhouse.
From 1459 to the end of the 17th century, the parish church of the fourteenth century, with a bell tower, a Romanesque portal and a barrel vault on decorated shelves.
Art in the citadel.

Easy hike of about 2 hours and 640 m of difference in altitude from Torre Pellice (560 m) to 1200 m of the Bars d'la Tajola, passing through Coppieri, Champas and Ruà (a stone bathtub and community oven) and Castelluzzo.

In the square dedicated to the Italian railway companies is exposed from 7 May 1988, in concession of the State Railways, the steam locomotive n. 054 of group 740, built in 1912 by the Ansaldo of Genoa and coming from the deposit of Castelvetrano-Trapani; it is a monument to the emigration and depopulation of the country.

Born as an agropastoral exhibition in 1975, it has since 1993 a home made from old houses in the historic center: everyday objects, traditional costumes, tools and a path on the processing of the broom, from the collection to the fabrics, with many pieces donated by the inhabitants; it has a specialized library and a craft workshop.
A historic garden of palm trees overlooking the Tronto valley.
For a wine cellar tour.
The cathedral on the Cyclopean Civita.
A 17th-century shrine inside the Carmine Park; in July the village has its most heartfelt feast, with three days of celebrations and processions.
The story between Po and Adige.

A circular icebox partly underground with a roof of stone slabs, built around 1870 by Innocent bricklayer Menegazzi: in winter the ice was cut from the pond next door, which in summer was sold in Verona and in the plain, until 1935-36. It has two bocàre, one to store the blocks and one to the level of the road to load the wagons. It is only seen from the outside, with explanatory panel; about 4 km from the center on the road to Malga San Giorgio.

The Science Museum designed by Renzo Piano is open in 2013, eco-sustainable and with shapes that recall the mountains: from dinosaurs to prehistoric man, interactive games and a tropical greenhouse that reproduces the rain forest.

Visitor center of the Park dedicated to the relationship between man and ibex in history and art: multimedia materials, reconstructions including a cave with rock paintings of the first ibex and prehistoric hunting scenes, objects, photographs, paintings, myths and legends. It is located in the historic complex of the Grand Hotel, witness of the elite tourism of the late nineteenth century, partially restored by the Park Authority which has its operational headquarters and a multipurpose hall in the ancient festival hall. Free under 6 years and over 65 years of age; compulsory booking for groups and schools (tel. +39 0124 953321).
The colossal "Palazzo Fuga" wanted by Charles III of Bourbon to welcome all the poor of the Kingdom, the major monumental palace of Naples, today being restored.
Sea and sunsets on the seafront.
The medieval oratory.
The country of artists.

In the basement of the Palazzo Comunale, eight rooms inaugurated in 1998 with tools of artisan and agricultural work, objects, photographs and clothes of the Marche hills; among the pieces the working mechanism of the clock of the civic tower, two film projectors in use until the Sixties and the reconstruction of a nineteenth century printing.

Born around a miraculous image of the Madonna painted on an outer wall of the village: in 1625 the aedicule became a chapel, then it was expanded several times to become a basilica; Pius IX raised her to the Marian shrine in 1854. Neoclassical façade with two bell towers, three naves and, on the main altar, the 16th century fresco of the Madonna del Suffragio carried on canvas; in the presbytery a pipe organ of 1780 still working. The main party is the first Sunday of September.
The city's mother church, with a fragment of the Bergognone.
Pollentia at the museum.
The Roman bridge over the Rio Mannu.
A table from the Vergari of the early sixteenth century.
The multimedia story of Santa Croce.
The church with two naves at the confluence of two rivers.
Neo-Gothic, late nineteenth century, overlooking the square of the historic center; smaller and older the church of San Nicolò in the area of the cemetery.
The 18th century in the house.

Palace built in 1518 by a branch of the Sarcinelli Census, which housed Bona Sforza in 1556 and Enrico III of France in 1574: Renaissance façade with three levels with five arches and quadrifora porch on columns of pink marble, interior with stuccoes and monochrome friezes attributed to Conegliano craftsmen. Since 1988, the site of the gallery of modern and contemporary art and then of exhibitions on painting of the sixteenth century; in the attic the Galleria Novecento. Visits to the exhibitions.
The Stone Theatre.
Understand the ecosystem of the lake.
Two museums in a noble villa: animals from all over the world and the ancient history of Valdera.
A large late Renaissance church with rich baroque altars.
A 17th-century convent with paintings of the time.

The smallest village in the Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise National Park, on a hill on the southern shore of Lake Barrea, with a fourteenth-century tower, the Apennine Wolf Museum and the wildlife areas; it is the starting point for the Chamosciara and the Rose Valley.
The most important religious monument in the province of Sondrio, with the great seventeenth-century organ.
Gothic frescoes in the mountain churches.
A maze under the old hospital.
A glass of the only Sicilian DOCG.

Inaugurated in 1984 on the ground floor and first floor of the east wing of the Florense Abbey, it has a thematic itinerary on the folk traditions of Sila: agricultural and pastoral tools, artisan crafts, domestic furnishings, religious and musical culture, iconography, with panels in Italian and dialect. It contains photographic, audiovisual and documentary archives, including the Saverio Marra Photographic Fund (1894-1978). According to the MiC card (updated 2024) open 9-19 from mid-September to mid-June and 10-20 in summer.
The introduction to the Pianelle wood before going there.

More than 230 hectares along the state road 106, about 5 km from the city: the colony founded at the end of the 8th century BC, with sandstone walls, the Greek model theatre, the sanctuaries of Aphrodite, Persephone and Demeter, the sacred area of Marasà and the artisan district of Centocamere; Roman from 205 BC, abandoned in the 7th to 8th century A.D.
The village of Tonino Guerra's mother, with works by Giovanni da Rimini and Antonio Alberti.
Village of the Aspromonta Greek area, narrow between a bend of the Palizzi river and a rocky spur, dominated by the castle, national monument; on the coast the Lighthouse of Capo Spartivento.
The main church of Genoa.
The wine of the Livorno hills.

Outside the walls, built around a newsstand with the Madonna and Child between Saints Giacomo and Antonio Abate, a fresco of the mid-15th century attributed to the Master of Eggi, enlarged in 1578 by a pupil of Spain with the Assumption among the Apostles. Within two Roman funeral inscriptions, a wooden crucifix attributed to Francesco da Sangallo and the wooden group of the Dolenti.

Borgo on top of a hill between Macerata and the coast, with the intact walls, the ancient gates and Piazza del Comune dominated by the crenellated tower of the Palazzo del Podestà; at the foot of the hill the Romanesque abbey of San Firmano.
The Italian twentieth century, from de Pisis to De Chirico, in the heart of Cortina.

Valle del Rio Seres a Lungiarü, called "Mulini": between the hamlets of Seres and Miscì there are eight water mills, single and double (two with two wheels), including a rope mill called "Tambra" . The route begins at a bridge over the Speckstube Tlisöra.

In Piazza Municipio, in front of the parish, exhibits wedding items, popular costumes and amulets against the evil eye. The ancient costumes come from Frosolone and its villages and many recall the colors of religious and popular festivals, such as that of Sant'Antonio.
Neolithic tombs and country legends.

North-western gate of the Pollino Park on the border with the Basilicata, a painted village of Longobard origin with murals and many churches; a few kilometers away the Sanctuary of the Chapels, the "Jerusalem Calabria" of 1557, and paths towards the Lao gorges. At Easter, the Judea staged the Passion.
The palace of the peasant revolt of 1901.
Walk in nature in 12 stages equipped.
Abano is located in the park of the Euganean Hills, with different natural environments, hiking trails and architectural treasures.
Industrial archaeology almost intact.
San Martino's treasure.
Neo-Gothic castle restored by Alfonso Rubbiani; private, it can be seen only from the outside.
The oldest church in the center, with paintings in the presbytery.
A medieval invented, and successful, in the twentieth century.
The political center of the city, with a copy of David, the Neptune of the Ammannati and the statues of the Loggia, including the Perseus of Cellini.
The nineteenth-century palace with the Pinacoteca, more than 300 works of Piedmontese and Valsesian painting, and the Museum of Natural History Pietro Calderini.
Panoramic walk of the village, beyond the ancient hospital of San Giacomo.

A 17th century church that preserves a black stone baptismal basin and the remains of an anonymous polyptych from the 16th century. In the village also the frescoed chapels of San Bernardo and Santa Croce dell'Ospedale, with works attributed to Pietro Guido da Ranzo.
Alleys and viewpoints on Lake Occhito.
Renzo Piano's project with transparent covers, a agora and the fountain "Fiore d'acqua" by Susumu Shingu.
Quieter than the Collegiate.

Access to the Parco del Monte Subasio, Valtopina rises on the slopes of the mountain in the valley of the river Topino, from which it takes its name: in the municipal palace the Museum of Embroidery and Textile, on the hills the Castle of Poggio of the 11th century, the village of Gallano, the church of Santa Cristina and the Roman remains linked to the Via Flaminia.
Seven centuries of Durantine majolica.
A rock on the lake, with the fish carved on the door.

Born around the Mille as a simple watchtower, fortified and enlarged in the fifteenth century by the Piccolomini, destroyed by the earthquake of 1703 and today consolidated: square plan in white stone with four corner towers and entrance about 5 meters from the ground, reached perhaps with a retractable wooden staircase. From the ridge dominates the plain of Navelli and the valley of the Tirino and was seen on the tractures of the transhumance; there were shot       ÂLadyhawke Â (1985), Â The name of the rose Â Â Â Â Â The American Â . Open every day from 9 am to sunset; you walk up the dirt road or by shuttle from the parking lot along the road.
The northernmost city of Tuscany, on the Via Francigena at the foot of Cisa, with the mysterious stele statues of Lunigiana.
Monferrina campaign tools.
The family villa of Alessandro Manzoni, today museum with paintings, manuscripts and first editions, and art gallery.
Andreas Hofer's house and the history of the valley.
Woods and volcanoes extinguished above the Campidano.
Four kilometers to the lake without a car.
The terracotta bell tower symbol of San Damiano.

Church of the sixteenth century with significant nineteenth-century interventions, with three naves; in the fourth Baroque stucco chapel perhaps by D. and Leonardo Reti and an Last Supper by Giovanni Venanzi in 1668, in the presbytery the ducal gallery of 1760 carved by Marc Vibert and on the main altar a Martyrdom of St. Margherita of the mid seventeenth century of Veronian taste.
The church of the legend of the Bandersi.
For train enthusiasts.
Roman complex included in the itinerary of the historic center of Bacoli along with the Tomb of Agrippina and the pool Mirabilis.
Crowning visits suspended from November 2 for the winter break (Park Calendar 2026)

Built towards the end of the second century BC, it was famous throughout the Roman world for the oracle of the lotes: it climbs on the slopes of Mount Ginestro in terraces, ramps and symmetrical staircases on Hellenistic models, up to the round temple with the statue of the goddess; in the center the Well of the Sorti. It is considered the largest late-republican complex in ancient Italy and its remains envelop the medieval village; the upper part is incorporated in Palazzo Barberini and you can visit with the museum.

Historic villages of Val Nure known above all for the cellars, crossed by the Road of wines and flavors of the Piacenza hills; in Albarola Villa Peyrano and Palazzo Barattieri, noble residences with adjoining cellar.

Ancient rural houses with large courtyards and arched portals; the church of Sant'Antonio Abate (1770) rises next to the former Granatic mountain, now a cultural centre, and in its square in mid-January a large bonfire is lit.

Hiking route 7 km from Rasenna (932 m) to Lake Vigi, in the municipality of Sellano, between mule tracks, pastures and underbrush with steep and stony traits: it requires experience, sense of orientation and appropriate shoes.

From the Portuccia, a panoramic path runs along the eastern edge of the historic centre to the ruins of the church of Santa Veneranda, a single nave, typical of the churches of the 10th century, with near a baptismal font for immersion baptisms; along the way caves used by the Eastern monks for meditation and a large natural arch. From the viewpoint, in good weather, you can see the Gulf of Salerno.
On the hill of Sant'Onofrio, the most complete ethnographic exhibition of the island: early twentieth century clothes, jewelry, fabrics and traditional breads.

A wooded area under Monte Carchio, in the regional park of the Apuan Alps, with varied landscapes and spectacular views of the coast, loved by the poets Ungaretti and Montale; in the second world war it was shelter and theatre of clashes, and among chestnut and fir woods the route of the Gothic Line preserves traces of the German outposts. You reach it through Cerreto, with views of the Apuan and Versilia coast.

About 7 km from the village, in a large wood of holm oaks and beech trees at the foot of the Pollino, the remains of the monastery founded in 1546 and suppressed with the Murattian laws of 1809.

Erected at the end of the sixteenth century in Renaissance style, without side chapels, it became parish church in 1692 under the title of Saints Philip and James Apostles, to which Mary the Mother of God was added; the ceiling, originally flat and low, was then raised in cask, and around 1790 choir, presbytery and sacristy were added (baptistery of 1901). In the choir the fresco of Our Lady with the two patron apostles signed by Giulio Musso di Asti (1894), who also painted evangelists and saints of the nave with decorations by Giovanni Lamberti; the altarpiece of the seventeenth century with the Madonna del Carmelo and four saints is attributed to the Moncalvo school (restored in 2004), and on the right wall there is a penitent Maddalena of 1889 copied by Doré by the Marquisa Vittoria of Clavesana. The ancient steel complex, among the main sites of industrial archeology of Tuscany, opens with a monumental gate in cast iron of the nineteenth century; closed in 1960, houses the MAGMA, the Foundry Theatre Leopolda and the Library of the Ghisa in the The old town coincides with the fence that enclosed the ironworks.

About fifteen rooms on two floors reconstruct Gallura's life: shops of the shoemaker, the blacksmith and the carpenter, cellar, kitchen, loom room where women of the village show live the weaving of the carpet, and a room dedicated to the Chorus of Aggius, founded in 1928 with a letter from D'Annunzio. The MiC indicates it as a permanent exhibition of the carpet from 1600 to today.

Late-Imperial villa on the right bank of Tellaro, identified in 1971 after underground excavations; over twenty years of excavations have brought to light the central body around a peristyle.

A sixteenth-century façade with a four-storey bell tower, inside a nave and two aisles: it preserves an anonymous author of San Michele Arcangelo and an altar triptych by Pavanino da Palermo dated 1472.

Borgo dei Castelli Romani on a side cone of the Latium volcano, between the woods and near the lakes Albano and Nemi, 28 km from Rome: the medieval center is among the best preserved in the province, with the Angel Fountain, the cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and, in the upper part, the Convent of San Silvestro with its Mannerist and Caravaggio's art gallery.

Inaugurated in 2007 by the Municipality with the Superintendence of Agrigento and set up with the University of Messina, it is named after Salvatore Lauricella, mayor of Ravanusa for fourteen mandates between 1946 and 1990. The two halls exhibit the excavations carried out on Mount Saraceno from the twenties of the twentieth century to the beginning of the thirteenth century, from prehistory to the third century BC, ordered for places of worship, inhabited, fortifications and necropolis: polychrome architectural terracottas with a gorgoneion, painted arules, amphorae, loom weights, a turtle-shaped askos and a piss of 520-460 BC from the set of a child sarcophagus of the necropolis of Via Olimpica, with a satire clinging to a donkey.

Museum dedicated to the typical medicinal herbs of the Maritime Alps, in the former town hall next to the Oratory of the Assumption and part of the Museum of the Territory "I Volti dell'Ubagu" . On the ground floor about 150 species of aromatic plants, medicinal and edible with Latin and vulgar names, and machinery and stills for dyes, extracts, herbal teas and distillates; on the upper floor a didactic laboratory with hemeroteca. It is named after the agronomist of Cosio Giovanni Alessandri, Provincial Herborist; since 2020 there is also a room of edible flowers.

Fortress built between 1733 and 1745 on a six-pointed star plant on the shore of Tanaro, enhanced by Napoleon; here in 1821 it waved for the first time the Tricolor. Free access, with Piazza d'Armi and a small museum of uniforms and relics of the Royal Army 1848-1946.

Interactive and multimedia space of 2,300 square meters in the complex of Villa Correr Pisani, dedicated to the conflicts and events of the twentieth century since the First World War; it hosts a permanent laboratory of civic education and is also a tourist information point. Times indicated: Tuesday-Friday 14.30-18, Saturday and Sunday 10-18, Monday closed.
The original table of Our Lady of the Macchie.

Small fishing village on the western side of Monte dei Porri, set in a partially submerged volcanic caldera that forms a green amphitheatre overlooking the sea. Here was shot most of the film     Â"Il Postino" (1994), the last role of Massimo Troisi: via Massimo Troisi descends to the sea passing through the statue of postman Mario Ruoppolo; to the north of the village the Casa Rosa, the house of Neruda in the film, is private.

The fortress, linked to Beatrice Cenci and to a tragedy of the sixteenth century, is reached with a short climb from the center of Petrella Salto; from above the view extends over the village, the woods of Cicolano and Lake Salto.
Ancient village with sixteenth century windows, frescoes, inlaid walnut portals and Palazzo Enrielli of the seventeenth century.

In the territory of the Gargano National Park that surrounds the city, it is the largest cavity of Gargano and the deepest of Puglia, a destination of speleologists.

Borgo del Sannio, still partly surrounded by walls, dominated by the medieval tower with the Carafa coat of arms; in 1861 it was the scene of a massacre of more than 400 civilians. The Civic Textile Museum tells the tradition of handlooms.
The museum exhibits a wide collection of mechanical equipment and documents that evoke the years of the foundation of RIV and FIAT; on the ground floor is rebuilt an ancient workshop.

San Biagio, begun in 1648 on a project by Giovenale Boetto, has a major altar of Genoese Baroque and frescoes and decorations by Giovanni Borgna made between 1881 and 1894. Next, the oratory of Sant'Antonio in Piedmontese baroque, started by Francesco Gallo in the early eighteenth century and completed between 1737 and 1740 by the Luganese foreman Giuseppe Scala.
Nuraghe and well temple in limestone of the X-VII century B.C.: the temple, 16 meters long and 7 meters wide, has tholos, vestibule and two atriums, with the chamber of the well 4.5 meters deep.

At 2,150 metres on the Croda Rossa are still trenches, stations and barracks of the front of the First World War between Austria-Hungary and Italy, with panels and guided tours of the Bellum Aquilarum association; the exhibition "Unvergessen" and the fort of Mitterberg are linked.

Among the oldest examples of Franciscan architecture in Calabria: the bell tower, the entrance and the wooden choir remain. In 1429-1430 St. Francis of Paola stayed there, as he remembers a letter dated A.D. 1429.
Archaeological park with the remains of the Castle in the sea, near the port of Cala.

The village is located on calcareous-clay soils, with climate mitigated by the Apennine and Adriatic currents, between Verdicchio vineyards and olive groves; Italia.it recommends visiting a wine cellar by booking in advance. Built in Romanesque style in the 12th century and restored several times; in 1113 the judge of Torres donated it, with San Lorenzo, to the Camaldolese monks.

Former provincial asylum founded in 1881 in a building that had been a seventeenth-century convent of the Friars Minor; with its historical archive it was opened for the FAI Fall Day 2023 and has been repeatedly reported to the Places of the Heart.

On the highest point of the village remain the ruins of a fortress built by the Arabs as an outpost and observation point, then transformed into a castle; today it is a cluster of ruins with panoramic views of the valley.

It preserves the icon of the Madonna della Navicella, surrounded by the "tolele" , votive tablets donated by the faithful; in the altarpiece the saints of the lower part are attributed to Giambellino, the upper part to Antonio Marinetti, while the face of the Madonna comes from a fresco detached from Palazzo Granaio.

Sanctuary on the edge of the town, begun in 1418 and consecrated in 1506, with frescoes and a grandiose golden wooden ancona on the main altar.

The medieval village in the hills, distinguished from the lower part along the Flaminia state road, preserves the Town Hall, the clock tower, a crenellated tower above the entrance door, the wrinkles and ancient places of worship.

Remains of the Roman city with paved streets, cardoon and decuman, a thermal building, a foundry and a second thermal plant in Santa Lucia, outside the walls; near, in 295 BC, Rome defeated Sanniti and Galli in the Battle of the Nations.

Founded in the Lombard age at the castle of Borgonato, it has a complex that recent studies date from the 12th century; it is located on a hill visible from the road and contains fragments of frescoes from the 15th century.

The symbolic tower of the village, rest of the castle built by Florence, with views of the countryside and the Balze; in the village the Town Hall of the first fourteenth century and San Filippo Neri with works by Matteo Rosselli.

Villa built around 1600 by the family Fillangeri, now home of the Town Hall: it preserves liberty frescoes, has a staircase to two ramps and a large park with many species of Mediterranean flora. Next is the Basilica Soluntina, an example of the late Sicilian Baroque.
The largest and most touristic lake of the Moorish amphitheatre of Ivrea, between waters and hills of glacial origin.

About 7 km from the village, in the Piana di Giardinetto: built in 1680 as a luxurious hunting estate of the Guevara, on three floors and about 60 for 20 meters with 80 rooms, it was among the royal residences of the Aragonese courts and then Bourbonic of Naples.

Building at the highest point of the Court floor, in front of Santa Maria delle Grazie: lower floor in cutting stone with two lower arches, upper floor in bricks with four openings in all sixth and external staircase; perhaps storage of grain, oven, stable and seat of the Parliament. Today it houses the Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions with over 3000 objects of local material culture.
