Founded in 1996 by the association Ij Canteir to enhance the traditions of the Orco and Soana Valleys, it reconstructs with mannequins, vintage clothes and tools the shops of rust, segantino, magnin (raio), slippers, carpenter, blacksmith, glassmaker, miner and chimney sweep; complete the path agricultural tools, a room on the costumes of the Alpine valleys and a research on the ancient shops of Via del Commercio. Open on Sunday afternoon in the summer season, on other days by reservation (tel. 340 6115520, 349 4975573).

In the Palazzo d'Errico, built between 1829 and 1833 by Agostino d'Errico, father of the patron Camillo, who defined the current Corso Manfredi. The collection of Camillo d'Errico has 298 paintings with works attributed to the Neapolitan school (Salvator Rosa, Luca Giordano, Micco Spadaro), Roman (Guido Reni, Carlo Dolci, Maratta) and Flemish (Van Dyck, Brueghel, Snyders); in the palace also the library of about 6000 volumes.

In the Borgo di Dentro, the oratory of St. John the Baptist is the seat of the Confraternity of the Disciplinanti (Disciplinanti), founded in 1262, and preserves an urn with part of the ashes of the saint; the oratory of Our Lady of the Rosary, built in 1660, is the seat of the Disciplinanti .
Church of the 11th century with trapezoidal plan with the intact Romanesque part and symbols engraved on the stones; inside two baptismal sources in marble and the canvas of the Madonna del Rosario.
The tomb of Elio Callistio in the middle of the second century AD, nicknamed after the collapse of the façade and linked to medieval legends on the throne of Satan.

Fortified village donated to the Abbey of Farfa in 1118 by the Count of Todi and rebuilt from 1524 by Ludovico degli Atti on drawing by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger; the church of San Biagio is of the sixteenth century.

Arcades leaning on the mountain of a 16th century irrigation channel that led the waters of Marmore to the fields of the mid-valley.

The Doric Nympheo, in via Gramsci, dates back to the Republican era and was probably part of the villa of Clodio; the Bergantino Nympheo, on the western coast of the lake along the Via dei Pescatori, is called "Bagni di Diana" for a mosaic with the goddess of hunting.

In the medieval village of Sant'Eustachio, also called Villa di Mezzo, the church of 1495 houses two fifteenth-century tables attributed to the Master of the Tondo Lanthrop and to the Master of Stratonice and a Madonna with the wooden Gothic Child of the fourteenth century of the Pisan school, attributed to Tino di Camaino; the altarpiece of Vincenzo Frediani depicts the Madonna and Child among saints.

Among the highest Renaissance buildings in Umbria, started in 1508 on a project attributed to Bramante and completed in the early seventeenth century.

The largest of the three municipalities of Salina, on the north coast of the island between Monte dei Porri and Monte Fossa delle Felci, founded according to the tradition by Amalfi refugees in the 12th century: the eighteenth-century church of San Lorenzo, the terrace of Piazza Rosa dei Venti, the cove of Scario, the Aeolian Museum of Emigration and, in the hamlet of Pollara, the caldera where it was filmed "Il Postino" (The Postino).

The halls historically and visually reconstruct the countries that have welcomed immigrants and the Italian and Piedmontese protagonists who have contributed with their work to build entire nations. Open on Saturday 10-13 and 14-18; educational workshop for schools, accessible.

Fortification of Byzantine origin (IX-XI century), with round towers wanted by Ferdinand I of Aragon; in 1911 the Ministry of War allowed its demolition for building purposes and the oldest part was demolished.
The country shrine of the September festival.

In the park of the medieval castle of the Trissino, family of Lombard origin remodelled several times over the centuries, survive two villas: the Villa Trissino Paninsacco, with Italian gardens and eighteenth-century statues of the workshops of Marinali and Cassetti, and the Villa Trissino Da Porto, now Marzotto, completed in the eighteenth century on a project by Francesco Antonio Muttoni (with interventions by Dal Pozzo and Calderari). The interiors are visited by reservation; closed in August and during the Christmas period.

The town of the Metauro valley, capital of the white truffle and home of the painters Taddeo and Federico Zuccari: the Domus del Mito with the mosaics of the Roman Tifernum Mataurense, the Santa Maria extra muros complex, the Palazzo della Ragione with the tower "el Campanon" and the museum of old crafts.

In the Plattner farm of Costalovara, a monument of rural architecture of over 600 years restored by the Gramm family with the protection of cultural heritage: the largest private collection of South Tyrolean beekeeping explains the production of honey, and a naturalistic path on the hill tells the world of bees. In the season from April to October, admission from 10 to 17; free with RittenCard.
A rare geological phenomenon.

In the center of the village, reached by a staircase, it was built at the end of the sixteenth century on a more ancient building mentioned in a document of 1341. The interior with three naves combines Gothic-Aragonese and Renaissance elements; portal with carved columns and reliefs of popular taste on the bell tower. The patron saint is celebrated in late August.
The nineteenth and twentieth centuries among the parks.

Itinerary of the Stone between the church of San Michele Arcangelo, Villa Gargallo and the hamlets of Treppio, with the water mill of Docciola; then the stone arch bridge and the fountain of Casa Nuova, Campaldaio, the Mill of Casina in Poggiolino, a dryer in Tortello and a large sack wall in Piano.

It was first mentioned in 1358, it rises between the two villages of the village; the bell tower was started in 1656 and the title of parish church arrived in 1794. Inside the pulpit carved by Eugenio Manzoni and gilded in 1726 by Girolamo Agnese, a red marble stove from the early eighteenth century, a crucifix of Bavarian workshop and the organ of 1753, paid with the funds of the emigrant cramârs in Bavaria and restored by the Zanins.

Modern church of the Sixties designed by Carlo Siffredi, with internal walls decorated by Luciano Bartoli; the bell tower, begun in 1929 by Corrado Meano, is inspired by that of San Giorgio in Venice. In the baptistery there is a paleo-Christian marble relief with two deer under a vine branch; there is also the seventeenth-century painting of the Virgin of the Suffragio from San Rocco.

Church dating back to the fifteenth century, in Baroque forms, which preserves an ancient organ and in the apse frescoes on the life of St. John the Baptist. On June 24, the feast of the saint provides a ritual bath in the Liri and a procession with fireworks.

Born in the 15th century as Santa Maria del Mulino, destroyed by the earthquake of 1693 and reopened in 1699; the neo-Gothic dome was completed in 1894 and the bell tower in 1936. Of the original building remain the pillars and the arch with sharp sixth of the central nave; inside a wooden ceiling attributed to the Barbalonga of Messina, stuccoes and sepulchral monuments. An eighteenth-century villa in Rococo style in Riscossa di Mira: the first news dates back to 1718, when it was donated to Elisabetta Tornimbeni and to her husband, Count Diodato Seriman; in 1750 it passed to Duke Gabrio Serbelloni and after the Napoleonic era to the Widmann-Rezzonico, who adapted it to the rococo taste. The festival hall has mythological stuccoes and frescoes, including the Gloria of the Widmann family, with works by Giuseppe Angeli and Girolamo Mengozzi Colonna; Goldoni, D'Annunzio and Stravinsky stayed there. The barchessa houses a collection of ancient carriages and the park has statues, avenues of lindens and pine trees and a nineteenth-century pond; since 1984 it is public (today Venice Metropolitan City). Opening on reservation at least 48 hours before.
The oldest church in the village and the tomb of Russolo.

An abbey turned into a cellar.

One of the largest Roman villas explored, on terraces with a front of more than 250 meters, excavated between 1750 and 1764 for Charles III of Bourbon: it has returned about 90 sculptures and over 1,800 rolls of papyrus, mostly epicurean texts of Philodemus of Gadara.

In Pracorno, at the entrance of the valley: one of the few water mills still working, with the millstones and the family house of the nineteenth century, today museum of mountain crafts of the nineteenth century. Guided tours by the Mill Ruatti Association, seasonal openings and sometimes by reservation.
A fishing village in the middle of the lake.

One of the oldest streets in the medieval city: at number 14 the house of Emanuele Repetti, where according to tradition he was guest Francesco Petrarca in 1343.

The only fortified part of the city, seat of political, religious and military functions: there rise the temple C, begun around 560 BC and attributed to Apollo, among the oldest known Doric temples, the temple D dedicated to Athena and the temples A and O. At temple D the North Gate opens, with sections of the Hellenistic walls reinforced after 409 BC under Hermocrates.
Baroque shrine that guards the remains of the patron saint.

It rises on the Bridge of Diocletian where was found the statue of the Madonna, rebuilt in the eighteenth century according to a design by Carlo Fantoni, with frescoes by Giacinto Diano and the bell tower 37 meters from 1610-1614.

Water jump embedded in the rock around the Passo del Ballino, reachable by a path through woods and meadows.

Two noble villas among high ash trees, a long residence of the Ceretti family, which in 1796 founded the "Pietro Maria Ceretti" (Pietro Maria Ceretti) by starting the Villadossola industry. In November 1943 Villa Lena, German garrison, was conquered by the insurgents and then resumed; it retains the signs of the bombing of the Junkers 88, remembered by a stone. The village of the Lower Atesina on the Porphido plateau, with Redagno, where the gorge of the Bletterbach, the Grand Canyon of South Tyrol opens, and the smallest of the nine UNESCO World Heritage Sites systems since 2009; in the village the museum of sacred Baroque art and along the stream the mills of the open-air museum.

Over 100 espresso coffee machines, from the first column and steam machines of 1901-1940 to the post-war lever models and the first automatic machines of the 1960s and 1970s.

Romanesque church of the 11th century with a polychrome wooden group of the 16th century (Madonna with Child), a canvas of the Baciccia (17th century) with the conversion of Saint Paul and a Baroque crucifix; the bell tower is from 1914. From the back of the church you can enjoy the view of the lake.

Walled city at the foot of the Colle della Rocca, in the Euganean Hills: from the Piazza Mazzini with the Civic Tower and the Loggetta you go up to Castello Cini, to the ancient Pieve di Santa Giustina, to the Jubilee Sanctuary of the Seven Churches of Vincenzo Scamozzi with Villa Duodo, up to the Mastio Federiciano of 1239 on the top; from the center also starts the path of Mount Ricco.

Medieval village of the Ciociaria on a plateau overlooking the Sacco Valley, called "Balcone della Ciociaria": you enter from the Gate of the Valley between stone alleys, the church of Santa Oliva, the Clock Tower with the exhibition on Nino Manfredi and the viewpoint with the monument to the Mother Ciociara; lower the Archaeological Civic Museum and the Roman villa of Casale di Madonna del Piano.
A place of the battle of 1848.

From the Neanderthal era to the imperial era: the statue called "Fanciulla di Sezze" is a polychrome mosaic from a domus near Porta Romana, hundreds of ex vows in terracotta from a sanctuary perhaps dedicated to Junone and finds from Forum Appii on the Appia.

Built between 1873 and 1876, it preserves the bell tower of the previous church, collapsed; inside a painting from the first half of the sixteenth century with Saint Francis of Assisi and Saint Francis of Paola and an eighteenth-century organ. Presented as the first museum in the world dedicated to the life and work of the emperor, it is a virtual route of projections and installations in 16 rooms, in the Palazzo Ghislieri where Frederick II was born in 1194. From October to May open Thursday and Friday 15-20, Saturday and Sunday 10-20.
A Perugine school pity.

Country of Baronia in the valley of Cedrino, with murals and an international festival of the organnetto since 1986; on Mount Senes the nuragic sanctuary of Janna 'e Pruna and the sacred source of Su Notante, whose findings are in the Antiquarium municipale, and a part of Mount Albo.
The shrine on the lake.
Rural church in the territory of Caporciano, registered by the Ministry of Culture.

In the former town hall, on two floors, Irgoli tells from Neolithic to the Middle Ages with almost all finds of the territory, especially from the shrine of Janna 'e Pruna and Su Notante: axes, millstones, melting pots, ceramics, a pintadera to decorate the bread, milk pots, necklaces in glass paste, broochs and bronze bracelets, votive offerings, betiles and a model of nuraghe in basalt. Workshops for children with excavation simulation.
An eighteenth-century interior with works by Santi and Canal.

Opened on November 13, 1966 in the former Palazzo Ripanti, next to the Cathedral: nine rooms with works of art and crafts of religious inspiration and, since 1990, a section of contemporary art. Open Monday to Friday 9.30-13.30 and Sunday 16-19; it does not have a separate ticket but is part of the unique ticket of the museum network.
A walk through granite houses after the sea.
An open-air mural museum.

From the top you can enjoy a wonderful view of Lake Orta; there is a monumental complex with the convent built in 1600 on the remains of a castle of the fourteenth century and various chapels along a processional path. The area also has archaeological interest (celtic, Gallic and Roman-Imperial finds) and wooded slopes with chestnut and oak. Managed by the Ticino and Lake Maggiore Protected Areas Management Authority.
Roman asculum on a bridge.

Historical district gathered around the former Franciscan convent, now Town Hall, with a large cloister and a monumental baroque entrance; near stands the church of San Francesco, founded in the fourteenth century.

Small isolated Romanesque church at 1112 meters between Poggio della Pagnotta and Monte Fiegni, at the border of four municipalities; it preserves fragments of frescoes with a Crucifix and the Maddalena, perhaps of Cola di Pietro (1370-80).

The medieval core is surrounded by some preserved fourteenth-century walls, with narrow streets with an ancient appearance; you enter them from the Porta Farnese, opened in 1576, and the route touches the Palazzo Abbaziale (1285-1300) to the Porta di Sotto. From the village you can see the Tiber Valley and the Soratte; on July 6, 1849 Garibaldi camped there with about 4,000 men and Anita.
The Cathedral was reborn after the earthquake.
The Guercino that leaves breathless.

Collegiate parish church of the historical centre, recognizable for the Baroque façade and the bell tower with three orders of Romanesque-Gothic triphores; inside a table of the 16th century Ligurian painter Luca Cambiaso.
One of the most beautiful villages in the province.
Cisterns that collected rainwater as an emergency reserve; public ones in the historic center are visited with a guide.
The white and black checkerboard square of the village of the Rangoni, with the Clock Tower, the Prison Tower and the view of the Lambrusco hills.
On the Castagneta Bastion, over a thousand plant species between flower beds, groves and a pond; since 2015 it is flanked by the Biodiversity Valley in Val d'Astino.
The quietest Tuscan Romagna.
A limestone island above the Tiber Valley.
The living room of the city, dominated by the Triton Fountain.

Sacello of early Christian origin (IV century A.D.), ancient multi-pageng parish church on the eastern bank of the Muson, at the edge of the Prai. It contains a fragment of white stone sarcophagus cover with head of Medusa, of the second century AD, found in 1975 and two fragments of bas-reliefs with Longobard crosses (VII century) inserted in the walls of the apse and the facade; in the surroundings were found Longobard burials.

It is defined an open-air museum for the concentration of works by sculptors and architects between 1850 and 1950, from Santo Varni to Leonardo Bistolfi; admired by Nietzsche, Maupassant, Mark Twain and Elisabetta of Austria.
The Piceni of the Aso Valley in a medieval convent.
Water springs and a Romanesque church reflected in the lake.
Count Ugolino's castle, overlooking the Cixerri.
Romanino in the heart of Breno.
Ancient church linked to the tradition of pilgrims, with the central nave flanked by double side naves; the bell tower next to dates back to the Middle Ages.
Romanesque church in the locality of La Frusta with frescoes from the 13th and 14th centuries.
Look for the stars on the facade.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Perabò, built at the end of the sixteenth century for the Counts Guilizzoni on the lakefront of Cerro and purchased by the Municipality in 1968; the museum opened on May 9, 1971 as Civic Collection of Terraglie. It tells the Lombard ceramic production from the mid-nineteenth century (Laveno hosts ceramists from 1856) to today, with pieces from the Richard Ginori collection, Art Nouveau objects, rare Italian and foreign sanitary items, sculptures and panels by Biancini, Campi, Andlovitz, Melandri and Gariboldi and works by contemporary artists.
The spiral ride of the village over the valley of the Conca.
Season halls.
The millennial tower above the village.
The abbey over the hermit cells.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione at the foot of Monte Rosa, with hamlets of Walser tradition, a gold mine and alpine lakes.
The portal removed from the Duomo in 1841.
The church of the origins of the village.

17th century church with a single nave with unfinished façade and baroque interior of white stuccoes, gilded and frescoes; altarpiece by Giovanni Francesco Guerrieri, works by Ridolfi and Diamantini and stuccoes by Tommaso Amantini. It hosts concerts and events.
The municipality of Val di Merse is surrounded by woods, nature reserves and thermal waters, on the border with the Maremma.
Built in 1903, about 2000 hunting trophies and specimens of regional fauna.
One of the Romanesque masterpieces of the Marche.
Contemporary architecture of reconstruction.
On Shakespeare's trail.

A hilly village known as the Piceno viewpoint: from the centre, from via Tarursi, you reach the 43 cm wide alley; along the course the seventeenth-century Palazzo Bruti Liberati and the Casa Bruni, home of Ascanio Condivide, the first biographer of Michelangelo.

Fortification attested in the 11th century as possession of Malaspina, passed in the 14th century to the Landi who in the second half of the 15th century transformed it into a residence: the courtyard with loggia has friezes, capitals and medallions in terracotta by Antonio da Lugano and Antonio da Pavia, the facade with tympanum and the staircase are eighteenth century. Visit the 25-metre hall with monumental fireplace and coffered ceiling, the green and falcon rooms, the gallery, the frescoed playroom, the large kitchen with original furnishings, the basement and the dungeons; the weapons museum houses three flags of the Sarmato saxophones on the Christian ships in Lepanto (1571) and finds collected in the Amazon by Ermanno Stradelli at the end of the nineteenth century. Visits only by reservation (at least 24 hours before).

On a basaltic hill just over 3 km from the village, along the road to Macomer: a court castle built by Ittcorra, brother of Judge Barison II, attested in 1196. In 1668 Countess Francesca Zatrillas took refuge before fleeing from Sardinia; shortly afterwards he was abandoned. There are still traces of the perimeter wall, watchtowers and underground, and from the top the view ranges to 360 degrees to the coast.

Cylindrical fortress in grey stone at the foot of the Rocchetta, built at the beginning of the sixteenth century (1507-1508 according to Visit Trentino) to protect the village, mined and destroyed by French troops in 1703 and restored under the Province's Superintendence. Walk up in about 20 minutes or with the panoramic elevator from via Monte Oro (about two minutes); on top panoramic terrace over town, port and coast up to Torbole and a bar-restaurant.

Small town of the Eastern Brianza along the cycle paths of the parks of Rio Vallone and Molgora, with one of the accesses to the Park of Rio Vallone; in the hamlet Commenda rises Castel Negrino, rest of ancient defensive settlements of the Knights of Malta and the Templars.
The nature of Piedmont.

Built in 1259 and transformed from a medieval fortress into a Renaissance residence, it is one of the best preserved castles in South Tyrol and has belonged to the Trapps for over 500 years. The courtyard is surrounded by a painted Renaissance loggia; inside the Romanesque chapel, the room of Giacomo with carved ceiling, the hall of the Matsch with family portraits, the oldest sounding organ of South Tyrol and the armory, the most important private dynastic armory in the world, with armor made for family members. Guided tour only; from the village about 20 minutes walk.
The shrine overlooks the Lao.
The bifora with the angioin coat of arms.
Secular horse chestnut, element of the landscape and symbol of Arzo, location above Morbegno.
The engraved topaz and the byssus.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for hour 1 of the 2 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Palace of 1501 with rustic diamond tip, double-fores and blackbird in Sicilian-Catalan style.

Fortified heights perhaps part of a defensive line of the late bronze age; the top of Mount Barda was frequented by the Romans between the II and the I century BC, and Roman coins and other finds are preserved at the National Archaeological Museum of Cividale. A nature trail climbs from the Klanac saddle to the Roba (301 m) and Barda (260 m).
The square with its sixteenth-century well, with the Municipal Palace, the Palace of the Captain of the People and the Palace of the Priors.
A fortress of the late nineteenth century guarding the Moncenisio.
The shortest river in the world.
A Guercino in the country.
Historical districts: the Giudecca housed the Jewish community, the Baglio the artisans.
The Last Judgement and the Ascola goldsmithy of the fifteenth century.

In Castoia di Salino, a chapel dedicated to Mary Help of Christians built in 1870 on the spot where in 1810, after a flood of the Malmidili river, a stone was found with the image of Our Lady with the Child; a pilgrimage destination on May 24th.
District with medieval structure divided between the upper and lower Stampace, with the monumental churches of San Michele and Sant'Anna along Via Azuni and the Punic and Roman remains.
On the trail of the water and the roads of Rome.

The side valley of Val Pellice, the heart of Waldensian history: the meadow of Chandforan of the Synod of 1532, the cave-refuge of the Gheisa d'la Tana, the schools of beards in Pradeltorno and the ancient schools of hamlet.
The Etruscan heart of Volterra
From 7 January 2026 closed for renovation works (the conference room, the twin rooms and the embroidery room remain open)
The miniature theatres of half of Europe in a noble palace.

The market of Wednesday and Saturday between Piazza Cavalli, Via Sopramuro and Piazza Duomo, up to the cloisters of the Duomo, in the political and economic center of the city since the thirteenth century.
The millenarian parish church in the valley.
The lake with the Etruscan archaeological park, with free entrance, to be combined with the Archaeological Museum.

Ancient stone village of Langa between calanchi and woods, with views from the Ligurian Apennines to the Langhe: the medieval village of Montechiaro Alto, the parish church of San Giorgio with the relic of the Sante Spine and the museum of peasant civilization in the former church of Santa Caterina.
A stone's throw from the road, with a stairway of a couple of hundred steps, or from the sea; better go in the morning, because in the afternoon the cliffs are shaded over the bay.

It dates back to the end of the 10th century, remodeled in Romanesque forms in the 12th century; the façade was built in 1231 by master Zano. Inside fragments of Byzantine sculpture, including Daniel in the lions' pit on Roman columns in the presbytery, the wooden choir of the seventeenth century and the funerary inscriptions of the lords of Bovino.
The valley of once in a historic house.
Granite mass is the largest erratic rock in Europe, today a climbing and bouldering gym.
The king's estate.

Built in 1758 by Don Giuseppe Antonio Requisenz as a country residence of the lords of the fief of Solarino, it has characteristics of Catalan art, of which the Municipality indicates it as the only specimen in Sicily. Since 1993 the Sicilian Region has recognized it as a monument of historical and artistic interest.
One of the few hydraulic forges still active in the Alps.

Ancient Greek city on the Gulf of the same name: the walls of Capo Soprano, the oldest thermal complex discovered in Italy, the acropolis of Molino a Vento and the new Museo dei Relitti Greci in Bosco Littorio; in the center, rich in Liberty residences, the church of Sant'Agostino of 1439, and to the east the reserve of the Biviere for birdwatching.
The wildest Po, among gorges, reeds and farms.
The houses of prehistoric fairies.

A pedestrian ring of about 20 km, to be done in two or four stages with bus stops, starting from the Götsch farm after the gorge (Klamm), whose road was built in 1814 for the mine. Along the route historic farms such as the Steger (1618 about, 1821 stube), the Innerbichler with Gothic barn and 1612 stube, the late Dogotic Brugger, the Nothdurft (1554), the Großbach mill (1705) and the Auer mill, the chapel of St. Anthony wanted by the director of the mine and the Verweserhof with coats of arms of 1696.
The walking path to climb to Chamois, with 93 narrow curves.
The square that opens beyond the course, dominated by the facade of the Duomo slightly raised.

Ruins of the medieval village (X-XI century) destroyed between 8 and 16 December 1943 and rebuilt further downstream, declared a national monument in March 2008: it preserves the plant with churches, passages and walls with square towers, crossed by paved alleys to steps. In the centre, in the ...Picco della terra" (Picco della terra) the mother church of San Michele Arcangelo, documented from about 1513 and symbol of the village; also remains the Arch of the Barons, Gothic, probable entrance of the old castle, with traces of frescoes. This is where John Huston shot the Fifth Army ... The Battle of St. Peter and Monicelli scenes of the Great War.

Founded by the Benedictines in the fourteenth century, with Franciscan cloister of the fifteenth century, two Gothic polyptychs, a large canvas by Luca Cambiaso and a seventeenth-century altar in polychrome marble.
An eighteenth-century stube carved.

Place of worship very well known, reached by the Via della Ginestra, route between country roads, vineyards, cypresses and villas (about 7.5 km, 2 hours and a half). Next to the sanctuary was found an ancient Etruscan well.

Built between 1745 and 1750 on a project by the Dominican Fra' Antonio Cantalupi, instead of the medieval San Pietro Martire; the façade, considered the most emblematic example of the martinese baroque, has capitals with mermaids between acanto leaves, musical putti, a window framed by a cherub and the tympanum broken at will.
Walk over a whole Roman village.
The frescoes of the year 1000.

Borgo della Valle di Susa with the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta and its 11th-century Romanesque bell tower, the medieval Casa Amprimo and the Mulino Varesio; in the village Foresto, on the Via Francigena, the chapel frescoed by Antoine de Lonhy and the Orrido with the Lazaretto.
The elliptical square with the colonnade of Gian Lorenzo Bernini, where every Sunday at noon the Angelus is recited.

Città di mare sulla Riviera di Roma, patria di Nerone e teatro delle disembarkazione alleato del 22 gennaio 1944; in the seventeenth-century Villa Adele the Civic Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Landing, on the coast the remains of the Imperial Villa and, towards Lavinio, the Natural Reserve of Tor Caldara.
A military path to the horrible Rio Secco.

A walled town on the Colle delle Capre, in the Bellunesi Dolomites National Park, Feltre was rebuilt after the invasion of 1509 of the troops of Massimiliano I of Habsburg: in Piazza Maggiore, dominated by the towers of the Castello di Alboino, the Teatro de la Sena where Goldoni debuted; around buildings with frescoed facades, the Rizzarda Gallery and the Diocesan Museum, under the churchyard of the Duomo the archaeological area of Feltria Romana and, just outside, the Sanctuary of the Saints Vittore and Corona and the reserve of the Vincheto di Celarda.
Wall of the early thirteenth century with six doors, some still decorated with paintings and town coats of arms.
Interior of the Town Hall: Check access to the Council Hall
The Roman basolate in the open countryside.
Medieval neighborhoods perched on the cliff.

Founded in 1995 in Casale, it documents the rural and artisan life of the valley: agricultural tools, pastoral and forestry, miners' trades, coalsmiths, blacksmiths, blacksmiths and shoemakers, the rural house and collections on chestnut and ancient varieties of apples and pears.
After the great flood of 1882 the confluence was regulated: today the two rivers meet at the southern end of the Rapp Gardens, home in May of an installation of the Water Light Festival.
Sacred art in the stone alleys.
The Longobard epigraph of 752.

Already dedicated to Saint Anthony Abbot, it preserves the Saint Anthony Abbot between the Saints Marcello and Paul Hermit of Perugino, detached and transferred on canvas after the earthquake of 1861.
Walk in the Habsburg town of Collio.

The medieval village with the seventeenth-century enlargement opens from the Roman Gate; among medieval towers stand out the Fontana dei Delfini, sixteenth-century and attributed to Vignola, the Secca Fountain with the coats of arms of Campagnano and Orsini, Palazzo Venturi dei Chigi (who obtained the village in 1662) and the ...Tifo , a medieval figure in relief that tradition compares to the Pasquino of Rome.

Erected between 1487 and 1493 at the behest of Caimi, a national monument: on the partition wall the 21 scenes of Christ's life frescoed by Gaudenzio Ferrari in 1513, with the Crucifixion in the center.
visits to Palazzo Vecchio through Pro Loco
A young work by Antonelli overlooking the village.
The tower with Civita di Bagnoregio in front.
Sunny hill country at 870 meters at the entrance of Valpelline, 7 km from Aosta, with views from Mont Emilius to Grand Combin.
The civic palace of the Cadore since the fifteenth century.
On Thursday reduced rate for residents in Parma and province

Country of the Valle di Scalve in the Prealpi Orobie, for centuries linked to iron: the Bonicelli mining park in the galleries of Gaffione, small museums of local history and the ring in the pine forest for cross-country skiing.
Remains dated between 1200 and 1248; the side tower, the best preserved part, shows traces of frescoes from the fifteenth century.
Natural terrace of the high village from which opens a wide panorama on the Adriatic coast.

Built between 1685 and 1689 for Prince Giovanni Battista Pamphilj on a project by Mattia de' Rossi, Bernini's favourite pupil, instead of a thirteenth-century Gothic church of which the ancient baptismal font remains; it was consecrated on 27 May 1703. The semicircular and colonnade façade is flanked by two bell towers and surmounted by a dome; the six side chapels preserve works by Agostino Scilla, Andrea Pozzo, Giacinto Brandi, Ciro Ferri and Pietro Locatelli, while the central cap has the altarpiece of the Assunta by Lorenzo Gramiccia. It preserves the wooden processional statue of the patron Saint Louis Gonzaga and the burial of Cardinal Oreste Giorgi (1856-1924).
The view of the lake from a giant bench.

Triangular fortress with an ogival watchtower similar to the bow of a ship, begun at the end of the fifteenth century by the Orsini and completed in 1507 by Ladislao II d'Aquino, Marquis of Corato, who had purchased the fief in 1501; the project is attributed, without certainty, to Francesco di Giorgio Martini.
He preserves works by Simone de Magistris, Orazio Gentileschi and Pasqualino Rossi.
Closed for redevelopment (Parma Welcome, November 2025)
The Madonna of the miracle.

In the hamlet of Seuni, about 2 km from the village, stands the sanctuary of Santa Vittoria martyr, of sixteenth-century origin (1581) and rebuilt in the middle of the twentieth century; the saint is celebrated in May, as Saint Isidoro. In the hamlet there is a stretch of Roman road.

Highland in the Alto Garda Bresciano Park, with the village of Pieve overlooking a cliff excavated by glaciers overlooking the lake; there climbs the spectacular Strada della Forra of 1913, while on the lake the village of Campione is an industrial village become paradise of windsurfing.
The belt of the Cinque-Seicento, among the few examples in Italy of intact walls: over 4 km with bastions, above which runs a tree-lined avenue to walk or by bike.
The 360 degree panorama of the Ciociaria.

Municipality of the lower Brescia 33 km from Brescia, rich in water and springs, known for the Calvisius caviar produced since 1977 by Agroittica Lombarda; it preserves palaces, villas and churches like Palazzo Lechi with its towers and the church of Santa Maria della Rosa in Malpaga.
The funeral theater of the Dukes of Este.
Industrial archaeology overlooking the sea.
Hiking route of about 48 km from Casona di Marano to Montese, which touches Monte Belvedere (1,140 m).

The hexagonal tower with remains of walls that dominates Vernante: it is what remains of the castle's mast, built at the end of the thirteenth century by the counts of Tenda (Lascaris) as a tolling place on the road of the Colle di Tenda, destroyed by the Spaniards about three centuries later. You reach it with a dirt road in the woods.
The main square of the walled city, overlooking the Duomo; near are the Town Hall Loggia and the Pretorio Palace.
The dukes' mills on the river.
Trekking in the Pollino from the village.
Equipped sandy beaches and pinewoods, the usual destination of the Romans.

A watchtower that precedes the town of Serramazzoni, probably built between the 13th and 14th centuries to connect the hilly fortifications to the castles of the Apennines, in support of the castle of Monfestino.
The sandstone spur in the valley.
The memorial of the Great War in the woods above the city.
You really get into the mine.
Oreficeria and painting of the fifteenth century in one place.
The birthplace of Giovanni Pascoli, with objects, letters and the garden.

Born from a church of the fifth century on a Roman building, united in the eleventh century to a Romanesque basilica and the votive chapel, with facade of the fourteenth century; five naves, frescoes, goldsmiths and sarcophagi of the martyrs of Trieste.

Piazza Orsini is the lively heart of the village, overlooking the Collegiata and the Palazzo marquisale Camponeschi-Carafa, with a beautiful portal and traces of frescoes inside. In the center you can see the two arches of the ancient Palazzo dell'Università at the entrance of via del Municipio, the small square of the Conserva with the old wash-house and Casa Catini, with fifteenth-century facade and portal adorned with lions.
Gothic and Renaissance in a suburban church.

The civic museum, in the Egidio Isaac Space, houses the naturalistic civic collection, temporary exhibitions and other cultural initiatives. From 17 February 2026 it is open Tuesday and Thursday 9:30-12 and 14-17, Wednesday and Friday 9:30-12, Saturday 9:30-11:30; closed Sunday and Monday except events.
The largest winter station of the northern Apennines: about 50 km of slopes served by 17 plants and two cross-country rings for 15 km as a whole; it also includes the Val di Luce.
An octagonal building rich in Renaissance masterpieces, supervised by sixteen 'testoni', according to tradition it was born after in 1487 the image of the Virgin cried during a fight.
The fifteenth-century portal.
from 2019 access to closed number in high season to protect the ecosystem
The baroque in the Sabino village.
Wellness center mentioned by italia.it, with sauna, emotional shower and Turkish bath.

Museum opened in 2007 in the White Tower, symbol of the city, which was together civic tower and bell tower: models explain its historical and religious role, miniature bells reproduce the sound of the original and you see the interior of the original globe of the bell tower and the work of the guardians of the tower. Particularly suitable for children.
Steps and clear water.
A museum of world importance in the inventor's country.

Channel about 500 meters long excavated in the overhanging walls of the left side of the Clarea Valley, up to about 300 meters high, to bring to the village the waters of the Clarea stream (about 550 liters per second). Designed already in the thirteenth century and completed in 1400, it takes its name from the noblewoman Maria Bona, wife of the feudal Andrea Aschieri, who according to tradition donated a gold emina to build it; the plaque dedicated to her is from 1914. Next to it runs a flat path, with stretches to be followed with caution close to the walls; audioguide in Italian and patois.
The gothic jewel of the village.

Opened in 2005, it is dedicated to the Sardinian polyphonic singing proclaimed by UNESCO as a masterpiece of the oral heritage: in four rooms with headphones and four totems in a circle allow you to listen to the voices bassu, contra, mesu goche and goose separated or together, with music from the different areas of the island. It is also a polyphony research center.
Procida's largest coastline.

The Provincial Museum of the Vietrese ceramics occupies the Torretta and the ground floor of Villa Guariglia in Raito, with terraced park: it exhibits the most representative pieces of the local production from the seventeenth century, between votive plates and domestic holy waterworks, up to the second half of the twentieth century.

Country of Carnia on a flat triangle at the confluence of Tagliamento and Degano, with the 18th-century parish church of San Lorenzo, the early Christian site of Col di Zuca (V-VII century) and the village of Invillino, one of the oldest villages of Carnia, with the Pieve di Santa Maria Maddalena on the Colle Santino.
In the former chromo-litographic plant founded in 1895 by Basilio Cascella, a civic museum since 1975: it preserves 550 works by a large family of artists from Pescia.

On Mount Sacro (872 m), between holm oaks and mixed woods, the ruins of the abbey born from an 11th-century hermitage dependent on Santa Maria di Calena, a Benedictine priory from 1138, influential up to Bari, in decline from the fifteenth century and abandoned in the seventeenth century; remain the pronao with arches and pillars, part of the apse and the Romanesque portal. On clear days the view extends to the coast, the Umbra Forest and Monte Spigno.
Medieval melon building belonged to Cagnolo Nogarola, the "Casa dei Montecchi" of history: private and not visitable, on the ground floor a tavern serves the boil with the peara.
Five thousand years ago.
The Romanesque-Gothic on top of the hill.
The panoramic road on the Adriatic.

Works in cork exhibited in the house where he lived the last thirty years Tonino Forteleoni, artisan who exhibited in exhibitions and biennials, collaborated with the ISOLA and taught in the cork section of the Institute of Art of Calangianus, introducing the bas-relief and mosaic in the art of cork. Subjects mainly religious, but also fronts of chest (one in Liberty style), headboards of bed, furniture and tables; the atelier house is next to the church of Santa Croce.
The museum in the bishop's palace.
The patois house.
The view over the city, the Rose Garden with Folon sculptures and the Japanese garden, and just above the Romanesque basilica of San Miniato.
The canals that warm up the school.
Napoleon, Garibaldi and the Five Days.

Medieval village on the hills of the valley of the Era, among the Pisan Hills, born as a fortified village and then grown as a center of commerce. On the top of the hill stands Villa Baciocchi with the zoological museum, the archaeological museum of Valdera and a botanical park; in the hamlet of Santo Pietro Belvedere there is the layout of a medieval village-castle.

On the hill north of the village, above the road to Apricale, it has hexagonal plant and square mast in local sandstone. It was mentioned in the sources since 1287, linked to the arrival of the Doria at the end of the thirteenth century, and was born as a fortress (1330) and then took residential characters; around 1520 it was briefly held by the Grimaldi of Monaco. Damaged by the earthquake of 1887, it was restored and consolidated in 1989 and in summer it hosts evenings of theatre and music and the Festival of harps.

A noble residence from the 16th century, named after the last owner, today a town hall: Giampaolo Sforza, the first Marquis and son of Moro, lived there, witness of the wedding of Michelangelo Merisi's parents. In the façade tombstones to Vittorio Emanuele II, Garibaldi, Cavour and Mazzini next to ancient openings to Gothic arch; on the noble floor the Pinacoteca civica with works by painters of the Five and seventeenth centuries such as Moietta and Procaccini and paintings of the romantic Moriggia. Visits by reservation.
Aragonese windows and cork shops.
Along a well-restored cobbled path you arrive at the square and the Belvedere Fountain, overlooking the Sabini Mountains and Mount Soratte.

The municipality of Mantua nearest Lake Garda, Orange Flag of Touring, dominated by the Scaliger Castle of 1260-1276; in the surroundings the Ardietti Fort of the Austrian Quadrilateral and the Mincio Park with the Mantova-Peschiera bike.

From the town hall square, an itinerary of 14.3 km (568 m of difference in altitude) climbs through forest roads to Passo Cisa (1,489 m) and arrives at the Monte Corno mountain hut at about 1,710 meters, the highest point of the tour, with refreshment and panoramic view of the mountains and valleys around; you return to the same road.

A 166-hectare forest declared a natural monument in 2019, with centuries-old chestnuts, maples, oaks, ashes and lindens and the historic houses where the mosciarelle were dried, small sweet chestnuts.

A height of about 354 m, SIC area between Pavone and Ivrea in the northern sector of the Morenic Amphitheatre of Ivrea, with centuries-old woods, small marshes, rocks smoothed by glaciers, engraved cups and ruins of sighting towers. The municipal route (4.06 km, about 80 minutes, easy, all year round) starts from Sant'Andrea and reaches San Grato, the Via Crucis and panoramic points on Ivrea, the Serra and the Alpine valleys.
It preserves the simulacrum of the dead Christ of the end of the thirteenth century and the Miracle of the True Cross of Giorgio Picchi.
The home of the writer and Montale guest.

Former fishing village on the beach on the two sides of the mouth of Petronio, where since the Middle Ages were built the leudians, Latin sailing boats with which were transported wine, oil and cheese; the nucleus of Trigoso rises around the church of Santa Sabina and the remains of a settlement of the Fieschi. Today it houses the shipyards founded in 1897 (Fincantieri), the walk Descalzo and is home to the bagnun of anchovies.

Small hilly village of Ogliastra, about 10 km from the beaches of Tortolì and less than 20 km from Gennargentu, among cannonau vineyards and age-old olive groves: two museums built in old mills tell the story of peasant life, and many houses are decorated with murals.
Included in the ticket of the Museum of Palazzo Pretorio

The municipal palace of the first half of the fourteenth century, with frescoes, the Wedding Hall with two paintings of Vasari and the Council Hall frescoed by Parri di Spinello; the route goes up towards the tower.

With three thousand years of history and over one hundred thermal baths, Abano forms with Montegrotto the largest and oldest thermal resort in Europe, at the foot of the Euganean Hills: in the city the great sundial of Piazza del Sole e della Pace, the Cathedral of San Lorenzo, the hill of Montirone, the Museum Villa Bassi Rathgeb and the Museum of the Mask; on the heights the Monastery of San Daniele and the Sanctuary of Monteortone.
Castle and village intact above the valley.
17th century church that preserves a wooden Crucifix attributed to Fra' Umile da Petralia.

Altomedieval castle at the foot of the Martani Mountains, along the ancient Via Flaminia: in the village the churches of San Felice and San Sebastiano; in the territory of Santa Maria in Pantano on the Vicus Martis Tudertium, the Catacomba of Villa San Faustino, the only one in Umbria, the Fonnaia Bridge and the Benedictine abbeys.
The ancient town hall in the heart of Castello, overlooking Piazza Palazzo next to the Cathedral and the Palazzo Regio; today the exhibition center of the Civic Museums.
It rises in Piazza Pierobon and preserves inside frescoes by Jacopo Bassano.

It occupies several halls of the abbey complex: on the first floor four rooms dedicated to the treasure of the abbey, to the abbot Giacomo Crescenzi (the town of San Matteo di Caravaggio for San Luigi dei Francesi), to the precian surgical school and to a pharmacy and a rebuilt alchemical laboratory; works of art, liturgical objects, wooden sculptures, paintings and goldsmiths.
Lose yourself in the maze between roses and secular hornbeams.

The main streets have porticoes with shops that frame Gothic and Renaissance palaces; under the porch of the Marconi College was walking Lorenzo Da Ponte, librettist of Mozart, and in Via Seminario stands Palazzo Venanzio, birthplace of the futurist Luigi Russolo.
The diocesan museum is the usual seat of the reliquary donated by Sixtus V and also preserves a relic of Paul II donated by the pope.
The historical cemetery of the city, inserted by the municipality among the places of the museum circuit.
One of the symbols of Val di Fiemme.
The church of the panella and the Poccetti.
The Civic Archaeological Museum with the Ecomuseum of granite.
The seat of the National Museum of the Arts of the 21st century in Rome.

One of the most picturesque corners of the city, born in the thirteenth century as a stop of the trade of wheat and cereals; on the quay Palazzo Todeschini, with fifteen arches, seat of the town hall until the seventies of the twentieth century and today seat of conferences. Nearby, Malavezzi square in the heart of downtown.

The town is surrounded by two walls around the castle mentioned since 1026; it is the city of the archaeology of the Paleolithic Venus found in 1925 and the mammoth of the Panaro, and it is the birthplace of the sculptor Giuseppe Graziosi.
The mother church of the country.

On the ground floor of the castle, in the rooms with ogival arches, the plaster casts of sculptures of Apulian monuments made in 1911 by Pasquale Duretti and Mario Sabatelli for the ethnographic exhibition of the 50th anniversary of the Unity of Italy.
Buildings joined by arches, with double windows and crossed windows; numerous houses are national monument. It crosses the Via Francigena.
Contemporary art in the woods.
260 million years of mountain history in a hall.
The central square has a sixteenth-century fountain; not far is the Torre del Cassero, of the fourteenth century.
The Barberini Palace beyond the museum.

Born in 1881 and since 1995 in the eighteenth-century Palazzo Mazzarotta: on the ground floor weapons of the Bronze Age and ambre of the Iron Age, at the first the Sannites with votive statues of Hercules, at the second the romanization with materials from Sepino and the tombs of Bulgarian knights of the Plain of Bojano, with a warrior and his horse barred in silver.

About 5 km from the Rotonda Giorgini in Porto d'Ascoli, over 30 meters wide: inaugurated in 1932 on a project by Luigi Onorati, with thousands of palm trees, oleanders and tamarisks, thematic gardens, the bike path and fine sandy beaches with low seabeds.
Minerals and fossils from all over the world in a neo-Gothic tower.
The stories of the mountain told by voice.
free (reservation required)

Benedictine monastery from legendary origins (a tradition ties it to the victory of Charlemagne over the Longobards of 781), with community attested around 884; severely damaged by the earthquake of 990, it was rebuilt from the abbot Theobaldo. Façade with three gates (the age of the abbot Desire, the 11th century, and Angevin), three apses, interior with three naves with rebuilt ambo decorated with reliefs of the 12th century and mosaic floor of 1275; the bell tower is among the surviving parts of the monastery and houses the information center of the Park. Abandoned in the nineteenth century, it was recovered from 1958-59.
The findings of the territory from the VII to the I century BC and a medieval section, reported by the city portal among the civic museums.
Nature and mills along the rivers.
The shrine dearest to the Ampezzo people.
The peasant village and the Matese dinosaur.

Borgo del Partenio among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2017, symbolize the Angevin Tower with the civic museum; you can also see the historic center with the Arch of San Nicola, the Baroque churches, the Grancia of Santa Maria del Preposito and the path to Campo San Giovanni.
€6 (single ticket)
To understand the Romagna peasanta.

In the Stirone Park, it brings together the former paleontological and naturalistic museums: the fossils of the Stirone bed, when the Po Valley was sea, with the only known skeleton of the whale Plesiobalaenoptera fortellii, the immersive room of the whale Wednesday and Friday 15-19, Saturday and Sunday 9-13 and 15-19.
Gothic-Lombard church built around 1459, with apse fresco of Santa Caterina di Michele Baretta (1954).
The small Sicilian Barcelona.
Only on foot, no bikes or horses
Archaeology of the territory from the Bronze Age of Golasecca to the Risorgimento, with a secular park.

Park on the steep promontory between the two branches of the lake, wanted by Alessandro Serbelloni, with 18 km of avenues, paths and terraces and the remains of the ancient castle of Bellagio; the villa, of 1854 according to Italia.it, is of the Rockefeller Foundation and hosts conferences and study stays. Not to be confused with the Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni.
On the trail of the ancient Ligurians.
Heart of the city life, dominated by the church of San Francesco (13th century) and the Doge's Palace, whose double portal bears the coats of arms of the Pignatelli and the Reverera.
The medieval Garessio.

Palace built in the first half of the eighteenth century for the Attems family, seat of the Pinacoteca dei Musei provinciali: masters of the eighteenth century Veneto, portraits of the nineteenth century including those of Giuseppe Tominz and works of the twentieth century.
Roman arch of the 1st century A.D. along the Via Latina, in the garden of Santa Maria della Libera, indicated by VisitLazio as one of the oldest arches in Italy.
Rizzoli botanical park and the sweet life of Ischia.
Civic tower next to the Duomo, the only surviving part of the ancient fortress, dated from Umbria Tourism to the ninth century; it dominates the municipal territory.

Caves at the foot of Mount Julea inhabited by the recent and final Neolithic (IV-III millennium BC), necropolis to domus de janas in Magalàu and Santa Lugia, almost 80 nuraghi, about thirty tombs of giants, about twenty Nuragic villages and a sacred well.
Rare scenes of Gothic hunting frescoed in a medieval building.
A mile of fine sand.

Small village of the Barbagia di Ollolai at 600 meters, surrounded by woods covering 85% of the territory, famous for its orbace: along the Torrei river the museum of industrial archaeology "Le vie dell'acqua" preserves Cracchera de tziu Bellu, the last active ravine of Sardinia.
A Roman mosaic in the square.
The path that goes up into the dome to the lantern, about 60 meters.
A chapel that tells the exile of war.

Built in 1819 by Sante Baseggio and rebuilt after the fire of 1902 with Art Nouveau decorations by Giovanni Vianello: Beniamino Gigli debuted there; opera theatre of tradition since 1967 with free guided tours by reservation.
A short and free stop in the heart of the Dante town.
Tuff canyon with Byzantine rock churches.

Città del Cremasco with a historic centre enclosed by the Venetian walls (1488-1508): the heart is Piazza Duomo, with the Gothic-Lombard cathedral, the Torrazzo and the Renaissance palaces; outside the walls stands the basilica of Santa Maria della Croce, masterpiece of the Lombard Renaissance, and in the former convent of Sant'Agostino the Civic Museum is located.

Manor in dominant position over the Bormida valley, born smaller and enlarged by the Malaspina in the fifteenth century, by the counts of Lodron in the sixteenth and by the Genoese princes Centurione in the early eighteenth century; drawbridge and moat were replaced in 1740 by a stone bridge. Inside a spacious living room once used for the ballcord, the castle apartments, two frescoed rooms with ancient fireplaces and prisons with graffiti and inscriptions; on the southeast tower the coat of arms of the Scotto Centurion, on the corners of the tower the heads of lion of the Lodrone. It is privately owned: the tours are organized and announced on the site of the castle, which also offers visits on request to the contemporary collection (tel. +39 334 376 9833).
Neolithic tombs that imitate the homes of the living.
The antique market that takes place every third Saturday and Sunday of the month around the cathedral.

It was mentioned already in the 11th century, and was guarded by a strategic ford on Tione. The castle-recinct with an original irregular pentagonal plan, contains two polygonal towers, a corner tower with Guelph battlements and an imposing mast; completely restored, it is open to the public.
The finds of Genna Maria and Marmilla.
The museum is the most underrated in Florence.
Olive groves and pajares as far as the eye can see.
Walk over the lake to Maccagno.

To the north-west of the country, tiles registered in Greek have identified the site with Makella, also known by the Decree of Entella. The late-archaic walls, reinforced in Hellenistic times on the south-east side, defended the town, destroyed in the middle of the third century BC during the first Punic war and partly re-used by the Norman age; they remain a public building of the fourth century BC on terraces connected by two stairs and a large cistern turned into barrels, partly dug into the rock. At the walls was found a votive deposit of the late VI century BC with bronze skippers and helmets. For the visit we ask the museum's care staff.

In the square of the church, the manor house (first plant of the XII-XIII century, restored in the XVII century) houses spaces for exhibitions and workshops; in the added environments the museum exhibits images and reconstructions of the ancient Tratalias and the chariot of the procession of the Virgin of Monserrato, Sunday of the Ascension.
An enigma of the Middle Ages.

Dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta, the Gothic-Lombard cathedral with Cistercian influences rises in place of the one destroyed by Barbarossa in 1160 and was built between 1185 and 1341; in the eighteenth century it was altered in Baroque style, and the façade, slender and closed by a gallery, was restored between 1913 and 1916. The portal has a bezel perhaps of the previous cathedral and statues of the Madonna with Child and two saints; the interior with three naves of five spans has a marble rosette with 16 petals, works attributed to Vincenzo Cremasco and, as a true heart, a wooden crucifix of the thirteenth century. The crypt preserves ancient vestiges, Gothic sculptures and tunnels.
Saverio Lillo's paintings between baroque altars.

A green area of about 480 hectares along the river Rio Vallone, a green lung in a very urbanized area, with rich flora and fauna (including 13 species of small mammals such as the wreath) and a cyclopedonal and horseback riding route that touches historical buildings such as the Sanctuary of Ornago and the lazzaretto of Cavenago di Brianza. It has seven entrances, one for each municipality, including Aicurzio; it borders the Molgora Park, the Adda Nord Park and the Montevecchia Park and the Curone Valley. It is also crossed by the regional bike route from Gessate to Carnate and Arcore.

Set up inside the fortress, in the center of Polino, it tells with interactive multimedia models and systems the evolutionary history of Umbria, from geology and paleontology to natural sciences: carbonate rocks, fossils of ammonites and formation of the Umbrian mountains. It has an educational workshop on the ammonites and the information point              • The window on the Black • • with fossil extraction activities in a small nearby quarry.
A medieval castle intact on the edge of the void.
A historic residence and the basilica of Costa Balenae in a virtual version.

New walled land with parallel hosts, Modena outpost on the eastern border; it was born in 1210 as a reference point along the ancient pilgrim's road towards Rome, in front of the Bolognese castle of Piumazzo. At the end of June the San Giovanni fair with the prize of the best family vinegar, the first weekend of October the Mast Cot with the cooking of the must outdoors.

On the ground floor of the Franciscan complex, in front of the former refectory: finds from the prehistory to the Renaissance, with sections on Romanity and the Middle Ages, coins and funerary inscriptions.
The ancient cathedral in the town square.
Mount Carmo.
The glass glass from a thousand years ago.

Among the most important Romanesque churches in Umbria, rebuilt at the end of the 12th century on the place where the Syrian monk Mauro erected a church and a monastery in memory of his son Felice, who died in 535. The façade with rosette tells the life of the saints and the killing of the dragon; inside, a single nave, presbytery with cosmatesque plutei, crypt with three apses with pink stone sarcophagus, an Adoration of the Magi of the first fifteenth century and the blessing Christ attributed to the Master of Eggi.
The panoramic summit.

Hiking route that starts from Traversella, on the left orographic of Valchiusella, with numerous pre-Christian engravings between Piazza Refuge and the Cappia Plans: anthropomorphic figures, crosses, cups and cross-linked figures linked to the afterlife. The Piedmontese name "Senter dj'anime" comes from the oral tradition according to which the souls of the deceased passed by.

Second section of the Museo Don Aldo Rossi, in the former hall of the confraternity near the Town Hall: it contains a fresco of the Crucifixion of 1452, a fresco of Francesco da Città della Pieve and paintings of the XV and XVII century. Entrance from Via della Pitalessa.
Seven centuries of art in a museum born from the donations of the Trevigliese.
Stay frescoed in green.
Opening and visiting hours not confirmed by official sources read

Borgo della media Valtellina, mentioned as "Vico Ponte" in 918 and home of the astronomer Giuseppe Piazzi, discoverer of Ceres: around Piazza Luini the parish church of San Maurizio with the bezel of Bernardino Luini and the Parish Museum, higher up the Jesuit church of Sant'Ignazio with the ethnographic museum and the mulberry centuries-old, and in the locality San Bernardo the observatory entitled to Piazzi.
Byzantine frescoes unique in Sicily.
The Touring Club indicates it is temporarily closed

Borgo della piania dortona, home of the novelliere Matteo Bandello, with medieval and fifteenth-century houses decorated in terracotta; the collegiate of Saints Peter and Paul preserves the Romanesque portal signed by Magister Albertus in 1183, the Last Supper by Alessandro Berri and a fresco of the fifteenth-century Madonna della Misericordia.
The Jesuit palace.

Borgo on a promontory on the south-western shore of Lake Bolsena, dominated by the octagonal Farnese Rocca restored by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger; from the marina start the trips to the Bisentina and Martana islands, and on the hill towards Valentano remain the traces of the ancient Visentium.
Built in the first half of the eighteenth century by the Scolopi, decorated with stucco by the comasco Pietro Piazzoli.
The river and its birds are just a stone's throw from the museums.
The oldest church in the village, with fifteenth century frescoes.

On the square the neo-Gothic Town Hall, already a convent of the Scalzi Carmelites, and the two palaces of the Marchesi of Eschifaldo: one is public and hosts temporary exhibitions and at Christmas the Crib of Enchant; the other, of the Pottino heirs, is a museum house with nineteenth-century frescoes and the table service used for Umberto II Prince of Piedmont.
The walled village that is mirrored in the lake.
A 16th century masterpiece.

A place with a very long history, dating back to the pre-Roman age and experienced the greatest splendor with the powerful Ezzelini dynasty; on the Bastia Hill remains leftovers of the first decades of the twelfth century, where medieval reenactments are held each year.
The symbol of the village, with views from the sea to the Laga.
Natural cave in the Conero Park, a short walk from the village, which hosts shows in summer.
the MiC card reports the museum closed every day, Umbriatourism indicates numbers for the reservation: check the opening before the visit
At the entrance of the village are the walls of the church of San Martino di Castelvero, marked by the Romanesque itinerary of the ATL as a "rarissima," a double apse.
Historical stop of the pilgrims of Francigena.

About 300 metres on Mount Bonadies, of Goto-Byzantine origin, extended by the Longobard Prince Arechi II and never conquered: towers, crenellated walls, the Bastille; houses an archaeological museum with ceramics, glass and coins, a multimedia museum and a park with paths.
The palace that closes Piazza delle Erbe with the late 17th-Renaissance façade with Baroque motifs.

The medieval village, founded around the XI-XII century as Maratea Inferiore, is a network of alleys, stairs and flowering balconies; the oldest part, via Capocasale, dates back to the thirteenth-th century. Piazza Buraglia is the heart of the village, ...The Piazza della Piazza is the shopping street for the walk and from the viewpoint of the Stone of the Sun you can watch the sunset on the Gulf of Policastro. In front of the Annunziata stands the column of San Biagio (1758), in front of the Addolorata the obelisk of 1788 and in Piazza Vitolo the fountain with the bronze Siren of Alessandro Romano (1996).
A city born at the table in the 1920s, with an unusual architecture for Sardinia.
Sunny country in the middle of the Matterhorn valley, with the sixteenth-century arches of the Rû du pain perdu and the lake of Lod.
The living room of the city, starting point to climb to the Fortress.
Crypt of the IV-V century, just outside the village on the left bank of the Cesano, built with materials of Roman era coming from a pagan temple.

From Ceresole Reale, a mule track rises between larch and fir woods to Colle Sià, which connects the headboard of the valley of the Orco with the Vallone del Roc, with views of the glaciers of the Levanna and the possibility to observe the fauna of the Park.
A Roman sanctuary in the woods above the lake.
Theatre and amphitheatre of the Roman capital of the valley.
Taste the IGP nougat and the swordfish.
Two lodges on the water.
A long sandy beach, a favourite destination for the inhabitants of Cosenza.
An entire park turned into a work of art.
Medieval district of alleys and churches to walk.
The village of the Asinara prison.
Church built in the seventeenth century by the will of two brothers priests from Sangineto, Don Carlo and Don Giovanni Battista De Pietro.
In a panoramic position, it has frescoes from the 12th to the 14th century.
The cathedral treasure.

Along the course there are thirteen places of worship and the palaces Di Leo, Oddo, Rollo, Giacone, Fiore, Campisi and Ciaccio; Palazzo Oddo called the Harp, eighteenth century, is the town hall, and the Casino of the Marchesi Beccadelli has a Baroque balcony and a Catalan courtyard.

The city of foundation flies on the shores of the Liri, where you can meet the valleys of Liri, Comino and Rovereto; on the hill San Casto dominates the Fortress Sorella, while in the center you will find the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, San Francesco, the Abbey of San Domenico and the Civic Museum of the Media Valle del Liri. It is the birthplace of Vittorio De Sica.
The Cross-Bearing Christ of Moroni.

Village overlooking Lake Varese, once also known as the "lake of Gavirate," along an ancient street between the Oltralpe, Lake Maggiore and Milan; to see the Romanesque Cloister of Voltorre, the First Italian museum of the pipe and the lakefront from which starts the bike path of the lake. Typical sweet are the "Brutti ma Buoni," recipe of 1876.
Villa liberty of 1926 in the center, made with Belluomini and Chini, author of decorative ceramics.
Palazzo del Cinquecento with the facade decorated with 22 reliefs of illustrious Trento characters.

The Eternal City, founded according to tradition in 753 B.C., with the historic UNESCO World Heritage center: from the Colosseum to the Forums, from the Pantheon to the Baroque squares, to the parks of the large villas.
The waterfalls symbol of the Rabbi Valley.

Protected area with paths leading to the remains of Pirae, city of the Ausoni, and to the Roman villa of the consul Marco Emilio Scauro; the seat of the Regional Park Ulysses Riviera is in the former Sieci furnace of Scauri, example of industrial archaeology abandoned in 1982. From 2025 on the Golden Mountain a Great Bench looks at the Gulf of Gaeta.
At Colle Don Bosco, the ethnographic museum of Salesian Missions in the world.

The territory is rich in springs and streams: Pesco Bertino, Capo di Vandra and Fonte Calante are recommended stops for nature lovers, among the Rio and Vandra streams and woods of beech and oak where you look for truffle, with the possibility of excursions, climbing and canoeing on the Sangro. The black truffle is celebrated with a fair in August, the white with a market exhibition in November.
Castle of 1152 on a rocky promontory in front of the bay, several times modified.

The primitive building probably dates back to the end of the 10th century; it was radically transformed at the end of the 17th century and expanded with the lateral aisles in the eighties of the 19th century. It contains a statue of St. Thomas in golden wood of the fifteenth century, a Deposition attributed to Jacopo Palma the Younger and works by Giuseppe Bernardi called the Torretto.
The gullery landscape at five minutes.
A medieval mining village intact among the chestnut groves.
The frescoes by Paolo Maggi and the restored nineteenth-century sundial.
The villages of Martinengo and paper flowers.
To see the other side of the village, that of the nineteenth-century notable families.
One of the largest underground rooms open to the public.
The 16th century Dominican complex.

Large hexagonal square, studied in the faculties of architecture, from which start the radial streets that reach six peripheral squares; the project was traced by the prince of Butera with brother Michele da Ferla and the first stone laid on 18 April 1693. At the centre is a bronze by Turkish artist Murat Cura, part of a sundial, with a man kneeling wrapped in circles reminiscent of an armillary sphere; the bronze statue of the prince of Butera by Paolo Guarrera has one foot on Occhiola and the other towards the new city.

In the hills of the Parco dei Colli di Bergamo, the hamlets of Bruntino, San Mauro and Foresto I and II preserve traditional rural architecture. Bruntino, joined Alme in 1926, returned autonomous in 1948.
The peasant life of the Cilento interior.
Knoller's shovel.

A few hundred meters above the castle of Romeo; feud of the Pileo in the thirteenth century, passed to the Scaligeri in 1311 and was bought by the Municipality in 1742. In the restorations of the 1930s there was built a restaurant with a panoramic terrace; the statue of Romeo, located in 2016, welcomes visitors.
The civic museum of natural sciences, reported among the museums of the official tourist map and along the itinerary of the Renaissance Addition.

The eighteenth-century Casone, formerly the residence of the Bardi Counts who moved the seat of power in the seventeenth century, is today the town hall; the adjoining oratory, of the early eighteenth century, has paintings of the eighteenth century, one of the last Traeri organs still working and a permanent exhibition on the Gothic Line.

Born from a medieval fortified nucleus, of which the central tower remains, it passed in 1441 from the Visconti to the Federici and then to the Cusani, owners until 1936, who between 1673 and 1730 transformed it into a villa of delight: Giovanni Ruggeri built the shelter to the north (1695-1703) and Cardinal Agostino Cusani added the four corner towers; the salon was frescoed by 1760 by Pietro Cremascoli and Bianchini, with the ceiling of the four seasons. Pope Clement XI, Napoleon and Francesco I d'Hapsburg-Lorena stayed there; around there is the French garden on terraces with the "Teatro delle Uccelliere" and in the basement the Museum of History and agricultural civilization in Lombardy - Lombard Wine Museum.

The village, founded by the Pignatelli in the 16th century to attract settlers, preserves the sixteenth-century chapels of the Madonna della Grazia and Sant'Antonio and the palaces Virgallita and Rusciani, the latter with a beautiful internal staircase.
Art of the seventeenth century in a convent.
The devotional treasure of the village of the abbot.

Wanted in 1590 by Alonso III Sanchez de Luna in front of the Doge's Palace, instead of the church of the same name demolished, it was embellished in 1754 on the initiative of Mgr. Marco De Simone reached its current appearance in 1884: 44 meters long Latin cross plan, facade with two bell towers and eleven altars. It preserves the eighteenth-century high altar with baroque balustrade in polychrome marble, paintings of Luca Giordano school, wooden statues of the Madonna di Atella, of Sant'Elpidio and of San Francesco di Paola and a mechanical organ of the nineteenth-century Criscuolo, restored. Open every day 7-13 and 16-20:30.
A Norman church in the country.
Countryside, woods and bike paths along the Villoresi at the gates of Milan.
The Gothic merchant.

Reserve that includes oak woods, Mediterranean scrub, the pastures and rocky heights of the Rocca Busambra, sanctuary of flora and fauna and in particular of rare raptors; numerous paths, including the historical points of the "Pulpito del Re" and the ancient charcoal. In the area with the Sosio Valley there are the Dragon Gorges and the Giant Marmittes.
Nature and fauna on the large lake between Puglia and Molise.
Instruments from all over the world to play, not just to watch.

On the hill remain the foundations of a church of the year 1000, valued as an archaeological area. At the beginning of the 20th century there were three Roman tombstones and a rare Etruscan tombstone, a sign of a very ancient visitation of the place.
Access to the castle.
The monument of 1881 dedicated to the king who named the main square, surrounded by arcades and palaces Roverella and Roncale.
The remains of a Ghibelline castle.

Natural area on the edge of the ancient riverbed of the lake, with periodically flooded meadows, humid woods, reeds and small water mirrors; birdwatching destination, with hiking excursions organized by Legambiente Valdera.
Byzantine icons carved into the rock.

Born in 1986 on the initiative of the Association Arma Aeronautica, the year of the twinning of the country with the 9th Stormo . "Francesco Baracca" today has its headquarters in the school building "Giuseppe Restaini." It exhibits a permanent exhibition on General Umberto Nobile, the diary of Francesco Baracca, showcases on the two world wars and on the War of Liberation, the reconstruction of the plane accident of 10 November 1936 in Roccagorga in which the second lieutenant pilot Andrea Fumo (of which the saber is exposed) died and a library of about 300 volumes on aviation. Visits only by appointment with the curator.
Birdwatching paradise on the Tiber.

Monumental neoclassical villa designed by Alessandro Antonelli and built between 1842 and 1848 on the hill of Monte Cucco, surrounded by a remarkable park with many tree species. Owned by the municipality, it houses the Ethnographic Historical Museum of Lower Valsesia and is a cultural centre; it is reached from Viale Antonelli, with ample parking.

Hidden among chestnut trees about a kilometer from the centre, it probably dates back to the early 11th century; the frescoes, dated 1482, depict the Christ Pantocrator, the symbols of the four Evangelists and scenes of the life of St Bernard.
In the municipal territory the springs of the river Nera are born, where there is also a mineral water bottling plant.
The origins of Lanciano.
16th century villa of the Gonzaga, country residence of the court outside the village towards Bagnolo in Piano, with late-Manierist frescoes and well-preserved 17th century stuccoes.
The legendary crucifix.
The thirteenth-century tuff of trifora and bell tower.
Church consecrated to San Leonardo in 1116, with a major neo-Gothic altar, a white marble baptismal font linked to Andreas Hofer and a remarkable mural painting above the sacristy door.
Travertine columns and an underground chapel.
It was founded by Saint Francis, with a cloister of the fifteenth century.
Nuraghe, forest and panorama in one visit.
A small temple on the water.
The museum of the University G. d'Annunzio in the historic center, in the former ENAL Palace, with collections of natural history, history of sciences, archaeology and paleontology.
The place of the Pyrgi gold plates.
The 300 citizen.

The Gulf of Terracina is closed to the north by the Circeo and to the south by the promontory of Gaeta; the beach has the Blue Flag (2024) and is one of the ten Green Flags of Lazio, suitable for families with children.
Visit Tuscany indicates the museum temporarily closed to the public for restoration, while the municipality reports regular times; check on minecavriglia.it
Woods and views over the valley.

Benedictine building a little outside the center, indicated as one of the oldest churches in Abruzzo, with simple stone façade; above the portal two small bas-reliefs, the patron who cuts the cloak to give it to a poor and an Agnus Dei.
open only by reservation
A Franciscan monastery linked to the protomartyrs.

Romanesque church originally dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta, considered built in the 12th century as a small votive oratory at the edge of the town, in the typical Romanesque style of the Po Valley, with hulled roof, Romanesque door and rose window and bell tower. It preserves a painting cycle of the sixteenth century; some frescoes of the Zavattari, Leonardesca school and Bernardino Luini were detached, restored and exhibited in the eighteenth-century parish church of San Giulio, in Piazza Libertà.

Casa del Cinquecento on three floors, inhabited until a few years ago by the town's seamstress, which shows how you lived in Parre at the beginning of the twentieth century: kitchen, "selter" (the coolest room used as a refrigerator), tailoring workshop, stable, rooms, room for honey and loft. Many objects were handmade by Pierina's father, often with recovery materials; notebooks, fashion magazines, drawings, ribbons and lace document his craft.
A walk in the woods along the Dora.

Romanesque bridge with five stone arches on the Ambra stream, a few kilometers from Bucine, along an ancient important itinerary; near, the hilly village of Pogi Alta, grown around a medieval fortress.

Country of Casentino among the forests of Pratomagno, traditionally linked to the birth of Guido Monaco, the reformer of the musical notation, whose house in Castellaccia is now a museum; in the territory the villages of Pontenano and Capraia and the ruins of the Badia of Santa Trinità in Alpe, the first Benedictine monastery of Casentino.
The sanctuary is reached on foot from Piazzale Bonomelli and has a refreshment point; above the village rise the gray limestone formations of the Corno di San Giovanni and the Rupi della Loverina.
The remains of the Roman villa.
The Norman church in ruins in the valley of the ancient village.
Stop 25 from Sarzana to Massa for Luni and Avenza, with views of the Apuan and the sea to the castle.
The village of the towers.
On the slopes of Monte Termino, in an unspoilt natural environment, it offers picnic areas, restaurants, numerous paths, springs and forests of chestnuts, beech and broadleaf trees.

15th century melting furnace on the banks of Mella, one of the most important monuments of industrial archaeology in the area: the iron ore of the mines of Collio, Bovegno and Pezzaze worked, in the 19th century it was transformed into a sawmill, it was abandoned in the 1950s and since 2002 it houses the museum. Panels, audiovisual and audioguide in Italian and English tell about the fusion; on the ground floor the Giuseppe Ganzola Collection of peasant tools, tools and weapons related to the art of the "ferrarezze" (16th-XIX centuries). Stage of the Via del Ferro e delle Miniere dell'Ecomuseo; open all year round, from October to June on Sunday 15-18, to July-September Saturday and Sunday 15-19.
Peace, a masterpiece of medieval goldsmithery.
The main castle of the Upper Scrivia Valley.
The Gargano symbol faraglioni.

Neoclassical villa (former Villa Aggazzotti) of the Gandini since 1791, designed by Francesco Vandelli, with paintings and decorations of the time; it is the seat of the Municipal Library and is visited during the opening days of the library. The park is dedicated to the Resistance and on the south side has two majestic ginkgo biloba, spectacular between October and November.

It rises on a hill next to the castle, on late medieval walls: two buildings overlooking an Italian garden, the palace to the north of the late seventeenth century and a body to the east of the early nineteenth century; on the sides of the villa, simple but of aristocratic character, the bases of two towers never completed. Purchased by Lana in the early seventeenth century, it passed to the Gandini, the Saints, the Duchess Bevilacqua La Masa and finally to the Barons Pizzini Piomarta of Rovereto.
Copper mines.
Villa, water lilies and secular cedars in Monteferrato.
To be checked: guided tours on limited times
A garden of exotic plants on the seafront.
A large family castle with the park in bloom in the spring.
