The descent to the sea into the rock.

Borgo della valle del Sangro, where the poet Cesare De Titta (1862-1933) was born: his liberty house, the  "Cenacolo di Fiorinvalle" is now a museum house; in the historic center the buildings Auriti and Finamore, and on the edge of the territory the WWF Oasis of Lake Serranella.
The Paleolithic Venus and the Panaro mammoth.
To be checked (recommended guided tour, reservation at the Archaeological Museum)
Velia Cerinei's urn.
Italia.it indicates it among the three main testimonies of the past of Carignano, together with the cathedral and the sanctuary of Valinotto. It is officiated church, with weekday and festive masses.
The fortress carved into the rock that dominates the village and the Ionian coast.
A garden that draws the idea of Europe.

Village of terraced houses, stairs and arches in the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, portrait by Cartier-Bresson and Giacomelli, above the lake in the shape of a heart, the largest natural basin in Abruzzo.

Country of Sarcidano on a plateau at over 500 meters, for a long time the main Sardinian center of copper processing, told with the weaving in the Maratè museum; on the edge of the town the nuraghe Is Paras, with one of the highest tholos of Nuragic Sardinia, and not far from the lake of San Sebastiano.
A chapel at the top of a cliff on the throat.

In the 13th century convent of San Domenico: paintings from the 14th to the 16th century of the chamber school (John Angel of Antonio, Jerome of Giovanni, Giovanni Boccati), fossils of hippopotamuses, elephants and rhinoceros of the plain of Colfiorito, contemporary art and pharmacy vases.
The volcanic lake in the nature reserve between the mountains Venus and Fogliano, with the beech forest of Monte Venere, for canoeing, trekking, birdwatching and mountain biking.

The monumental living room of the Baroque city, with the Palazzo degli Elefanti seat of the town hall, the Fountain of the Amenano and the "Liotru," the lava stone elephant that holds an obelisk, symbol of Catania.
Monumental tree next to a canal, with a trunk of 4.5 meters of circumference and crown over 25 meters of height; it is a green monument freely visitable.
The picture posters.
The Castle of the Flowers on the Arno valley.

The remains of the castle (X-XI centuries according to the most beautiful villages in Italy; the surviving structures date back to the Angevin period according to Touring) dominate the village from a rocky spur to about 915 meters. On the rock is carved a footprint tied to the legend of a Greek queen.
More Crivelli a few steps from the Duomo.
Gagini and the frescoed crypt.
Museum of the University Museum System dedicated to the applications of electricity, on the university campus.
To be combined with the visit of Palazzo Abatellis.
The Grand Hotel Liberty became a congress building.
White rocks and crystal clear water under the Roman villa.

International exhibition of art in nature born in 1986 in Val di Sella, with works especially in stones, leaves, branches and trunks allowed to evolve in the woods: the ArteNatura route, since 1996, on the south side of Mount Armentera, the garden of Villa Strobele and Malga Costa with exhibitions and workshops. More than 300 artists have worked there: among the works the Vegetal Cathedral of Giuliano Mauri, the Third Paradise of Michelangelo Pistoletto, Symbiosi by Edward Tresoldi (2019) and The Broken Oak by Stuart Ian Frost with oaks cut down by the storm Vaia.
The tower building.
Nature and memory together.

Ducal palace born from the extension of the Norman-Svevo castle, which is incorporated there, with the Male and four round crenellated towers. The north side, defensive, preserves traces of battlements; the west side decorations, coats of arms and windows on the Dauni Mountains; on the south side you can see the Quadra Tower and the remains of an Aragonese bifora. An inscription on a balcony on the east side recalls the works of the Marquis Paolo II de Sangro; an overpass connected him to the ducal theatre and the legend wants an underground passage to the Matrix Church of San Nicola.

The town of Ovidio and the confetti in the Peligna Valley, at the foot of Maiella and Morrone: the complex of the Annunziata, Corso Ovidio and, just outside, the Morronese Badia founded by the future Celestine V.

Ring with departure and arrival in Turano (piazza Madonna Pellegrina, 658 m), which climbs to hairpin bends to the village of Armo, with narrow streets, an ancient fountain and the church, follows the valley of the torrent Armarolo with water jumps, pots and waterfalls and touches the clearing of Messane, highest point with a wide panorama, then cross People and Moerna along the ancient street Turano-Moerna, largely dirt. The parish church of Turano offers a panoramic view of the valley.
The mosaics of the late antique villa.
The village and the Piana Rotaliana from above, in half an hour.
Baroque building just outside the village: according to legend a farmer found there the miraculous effigy of the Eternal Father painted on a rock, today kept in a niche.
Visitor center of the Regional Natural Park of the Po Delta, with a great delta diorama.

The most important place of worship of Gragnano, founded in 1555 and completed in 1571, then covered with Baroque decorations between 1720 and 1750; after the earthquake of 1805 the façade was redesigned in 1836 by Camillo Ranieri. The ceiling houses a canvas by Francesco Maria Russo of about 400 square meters, among the largest in Europe; there are the Transfiguration of Marco Pino da Siena, the canvases of the apse and the Last Supper of Giacinto Diano, the Dinner in Emmaus by Domenico Morelli and the Madonna in Gloria by Luca Giordano. You climb up a staircase in lava stone; the carved wooden portal dates back to 1584 and next to it stands the Romanesque bell tower.
Building overlooking the medieval route that connects the Pieve to the Castle; it houses the Antiquarium municipal with Roman finds, including the cippi that marked the Via Claudia Augusta.

Erected by vote after the plague of 1585 and restored in the eighteenth century, it is a national monument for its Baroque lines; the Baroque altar was taken away from the sanctuary of Belmonte by Napoleonic soldiers. It was a burial place from 1600 to 1835 and was restored in the eighties of the twentieth century. Open during functions.
Built in 1922 in 110 days in the Park, with a track of 5,793 meters where disc brakes, guard-rail and draining asphalt were tested.
The look on the castle from the mainland.
Medieval tower known for its panoramic view of the city and its surroundings.
The silvers and statues of the Sardinian sacred tradition.

Founded in 1826 by Francesco IV d'Este in the east tower of the Ducal Palace, where it still is, the University Observatory hosts the museum with historical instruments; guided tours by reservation, with a climb of about 150 steps.
The big exhibitions.
A nineteenth-century neoclassical church overlooking the Val del Fino.
The frescoed feudal chapel of Corenno.
Ancient church renovated to accommodate a small theatre with 150 seats.
The civic heart of the village.

Opened in 2003 in the former dispensary of the Cistercian cenobium: prints by Dürer, Rembrandt, Canaletto, Piranesi and Goya, drawings by Luca Giordano and Camuccini, paintings by Pomarancio and the circle of Sassoferrato, with sections of lithography, sculpture and contemporary art. Open every day 9-12.30 and 14.30-16.30.
The medieval piroga of Lake Bientina.
The cult of Mithra.
Icons from the Christian East.

Documentary museum opened on 18 June 2010 in the former monastery of Santa Chiara, supported by the Fondazione Rodolfo Valentino and dedicated to the actor born in Castellaneta in 1895, divo of silent cinema. The permanent exhibition "Rodolfo Valentino," the seduction of the myth, includes the Hall of the Great Amateur with photographic panels, projections, 35 posters of his films and the reconstruction of the set (the tent) de "The son of the Sheik" (Sheik), among the rare pieces a 1927 chromolithography advertising cigarettes "Valentino" and a biography published in Hollywood in 1926, year of death. Hours: Friday and Saturday 10-12 and 17-20, Sunday 10-12, Monday to Thursday closed.

Mountain houses covered with scandulas (wood tiles) and murals with scenes of daily life; in the center the lategothic church of St. John the Baptist. During Autumn in Barbagia exceptionally open loggias and cellars; in early August you run the Palio di Fonni, and the carnival is known for the masks of Urthos and Buttudos.

Medieval village of the Ciociaria in the Aurunci Mountains Nature Park, with concentric alleys and steps around the Farnese Castle; it is the birthplace of Tommaso Landolfi, to which is dedicated a literary park, and Eugenio Montale set there the Elegia of Pico Farnese in 1939.
Municipal museum recognized by the Lazio Region, dedicated to modern and contemporary art.
The painted way.

In the heart of Salento, Campi Salentina was called "granary of Terra d'Otranto" for its agricultural tradition; the historic center has the mother church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, the marquisal palace of 1627, the "curti" and numerous noble palaces, and in the countryside the menhir Candido and Sperti. It is the birthplace of actor Carmelo Bene.
An ancient theatre of the 1920s in the green.

In the seventeenth-century Palazzo del Pretorio, it preserves Elbani finds in store by the Superintendence: prehistoric, protohistoric sections (with Villanovian materials from Monte Giove and Madonna del Monte) and Etruscan, documentation on granite and materials of the Roman wreck of Procchio.
The mill of the road.

Strade paved, ancient palaces and religious buildings of different eras on the village that dominates the lake; the walk from the Castle to the tip of the peninsula touches the church of San Salvatore with medieval remains, Roman archaeological sites, Piazza Carducci with Palazzo Callas (seats of exhibitions since 2002, over 400 m2) and San Pietro in Mavino. The route "Callas," Arie On Air" takes in 10 stages in the footsteps of Maria Callas with QR code to listen to the airs.
Small wooden theatre in the Palazzo Fregoso of 1603.

Near the shore of the Arno, along an ancient Roman road, it is the most important sacred building of Capolona; the name would call Satres, the Etruscan Saturn, to which a temple was dedicated here. After an early Christian church, the present Romanesque parish church with three aisles and three apses dates back to the 13th century. It preserves two cycles of frescoes: one of about 1370-1380 attributed to the Master of Pieve in Sietina and one of the nineties of the fifteenth century, of followers of Lorentino d'Andrea influenced by Piero della Francesca, commissioned by the family of merchants Bacci Arezzo.

Founded in 1086-1087 on the model of the abbey of Montecassino, it has above the three Roman re-utilization portals and in the center the bronze door to 80 tiles of Barisano da Trani (1179). Inside two marble inlays in front of each other and the seventeenth-century chapel with the vial of the blood of Saint Pantaleone, patron, in Ravello since 1112.

Artificial lake of the dam built between 1936 and 1940, which feeds the central of Ponte. A ring of about 8.5 km (3 hours, 150 m of altitude difference, G00 signpost) starts from the parking lot of the dam at 1,747 m and turns around the lake, recommended from May to October; in winter it becomes a cross-country trail.
The nature reserve in the municipal territory of Siena, signalled by Terre di Siena.

Opposite the Carrara Academy, in a nineteenth-century monastery: 1,500 square meters of spaces and a collection with works by Balla, Boccioni, Kandinsky and Manzù, as well as international exhibitions.
A Byzantine building in the country.

Born in the seventeenth century as a small oratory for an image of Our Lady considered miraculous, enlarged with the arrival of pilgrims: a single nave, frescoes and on the main altar the Madonna delle Grazie.
Sea and evenings on the teramana coast.
Baroque Collegiate with three naves from 1632 in Piazza Martini, with an altarpiece from the seventeenth century, an organ from the eighteenth century and the collection of sacred art of Sant'Urbano.
A medieval frescoed tower overlooking the valley.
15th-century shrine outside Massa Fiscalia; every five years the image of Our Lady goes in procession to the collegiate throughout May.
The castle of the cinnabar mines, with views of the woods.
A Jesuit villa with grotesques, entrance door to the Ticino Park.
From 1557, Montorsoli: Neptune between Scilla and Cariddi; from here the road of Liberty.

Country of the Iblei at 362 meters, crossed by the European Path E1, with a center renovated in the nineteenth century along Via XX Settembre and Art Nouveau facades carved by local stonemasons; in the cave territory, prehistoric necropolis and cave settlements such as Cugno Case Vecchie, with the Jewish hypogeum.
The MiC indicates it as normally closed to the public, with extraordinary openings
Oratory already existing in 1181, where Petrarch went to pray; on the square a Venetian lion watches.

Opened in 2004 in an abandoned parish barn, it exhibits agricultural tools, domestic tools and artisan instruments collected in forty years by a collector of the village, documenting the traditions and customs of the Upper Val Venosta.
The hamlet Flag Orange.
Medieval complex with walls, entrance door and watchtower, panoramic view of the village.

The village is walled in the Sibillini Mountains National Park, called "Balcony of the Sibillini" for the view that goes from the Gran Sasso to the Conero: the Collegiata with the frescoed crypt by Lorenzo Salimbeni, the Pellegrini Hospital and the Pinacoteca "Scipione Gentili," in a center marked by the earthquake of 2016.

The largest island of the European lakes, in Lake Iseo, up to 600 meters high and without private cars; fishing villages like Peschiera Maraglio, the capital Siviano with the Martinengo tower, the Fortress Martinengo of the 14th century and, on top, the sanctuary of the Madonna of the Ceriola with 360 degrees view.
Waterfalls a stone's throw from the village.
Liberty on Tigullio.
The vases of the Jesuit spices.
The Renaissance of Montefeltro.

In the Spinera plain, along the Oglio at the foot of a rocky spur full of caves, it was a sacred place from the 7th century BC at the end of the 4th A.D.: large parts of a building of Roman worship remain, built on a prehistoric cult of the waters, with mosaics and frescoed plasters. The statue of Minerva Hygeia, one of the three known copies, is now at the National Archaeological Museum of Cividate Camuno. It can also be reached with the cycle path along the Oglio da Breno and Cividate.

Walled village called Montepeloso until 1895, Irsina houses in the Cathedral the statue of St. Euphemia attributed to Andrea Mantegna, the church of St. Francis with the frescoed crypt, the Janora Museum, the underground booties and a series of historical palaces.

On Monte Fusco, about 12 km from the village, in the Aurunci Mountains Natural Park, is a pilgrimage destination; from the terrace the view ranges from the Circeo promontory to the plain of Fondi and Monte Ruazzo. On the seven Sundays (or Saturdays) before July 21, the procession rises at dawn from Raino.

In the former seventeenth-century oratory of San Girolamo, it tells of the transformation of the landscape from about 1000 to the 5th century BC into three sections: kitchen ceramics, fragments decorated with Villanovian style, buccheri and the set of a tomb emerged during the reclamation of the padule, with protoetruscan and Etruscan-Roman finds of the inhabited submerged by the lake.

The church rises 298 meters at the highest point of the village; the parish church has been documented since 1230 and the apse is the oldest part. Not far away are the calanchi towards the Rio Mariolo, rich in fossils.
Giant trees 100 years old.
The poet park, clear waters and willows.
A cathedral inside a Greek temple.
In Piazza San Vitale, built on the ancient abbey of San Salvo: single nave interior with chapels, baroque and neoclassical appearance, and in the crypt traces of the medieval monastery.

Municipality of the lower Val Venosta inhabited for over a thousand years, among vineyards, apple orchards and ancient irrigation canals: on the cliff on the Adige the castle of Castelbello, now a cultural center, and at the top, at the entrance of the Val Senales, Castel Juval with the Messner Mountain Museum.
The pharmacy of the Benedictine monks, active from the thirteenth century to 1881, with shelves, vases and mortars still in their place.
The cathedral of the Logudoro.
Punics and Romans by the flamingo pond.
The neoclassical Gaetano Cima in a mountain village.

Municipal exhibition venue for temporary exhibitions, dedicated to the designer Harry Bertoia, in the complex of Palazzo Spelladi, whose original structure dates back at least to the beginning of the fourteenth century.

Born in the late 1970s, in a period of crisis in the wine market, and inaugurated in 1981 by local producers and municipalities to promote wines in the area, in particular Freisa; the building preserves original plaster floors that can be visited with the path of the Museum of plaster.
A stop in the center in lava stone.
The mysterious medieval baptistery.
The fan village.

Borgo del Montefeltro from the medieval center to regular streets, narrow around the Castle of the Counts Oliva, remodeled in the fifteenth century by Count Carlo Oliva, which houses the Museum of Farmwork, the Museum of Earth Sciences and the Erbario delle Marche; birthplace of Evangelista di Piandimeleto, master of Raphael.

It is located at the northern end of the Cinta, separated by San Teodoro from the mouth of the lagoon, overlooking Tavolara, with fine sand, shallow and transparent waters and rocks smoothed by the wind. It is sheltered by tramontana and mistral and is suitable for children. The Marina di Puntaldìa has a marina and a square with restaurants, bars and shops; in the area there are golf courses.

The alley of about thirty meters, 50 cm wide at most, between Via San Giuseppe and the district Terra: traditionally the lovers were meeting there, who walked it from opposite directions to touch each passage.
Augustinian Church at the north end of the center, signalled by Visit Tuscany among the stops of the visit to San Gimignano.
A few square meters, but it is the oldest and intact interior of the mosaics of Ravenna.

Former steam locomotive shed at the end of the Barge-Bricherasio line (launched in 1883, inaugurated on 6 September 1885): two-storey building with central body and two wings, raised roof for the vent of fumes and steam and pit for ashes and water; on the upper floor the drivers stayed. It is indicated as a railway museum, open Saturday and Sunday 16-22.
The panoramic square on the village.
The Romanesque church reborn after the war.
Imperial baths overlooking the sea.

Capital of the Malaspinian fief of Spino Secco since 1221, where the Malaspinas welcomed Dante in the spring of 1306; it has two doors, the remains of the aqueduct and the Malaspina castle, the remains of a Byzantine tower and some noble palaces.
Church on the Cappuccini floor with the adjoining convent of the Capuchins, whose construction began in the first half of the seventeenth century.
It starts from via Nardelli and descends through the vineyards along the slopes around the village.

Fortified village of the 13th century with four doors still preserved: Via Centrale (Stadtgasse), long way between the medieval doors with Erker facades, painted decorations and wrought iron insignia, shops and coffee; Ragen di Sopra at the foot of the castle, with Porta Rain to the east; the high town dominated by Palazzo Sternbach, the great parish and Piazza Cappuccini with the church of the Holy Spirit and the convent of the Capuchins. A historical tour of about 2 km (2 hours) combines the stages.
The culture is in a museum.
A faithful Andria.
A hot bath under the village.
Very ancient bridge with two arches on the stream, recorded by the Province among the cultural assets of the municipality in the hamlet Molini of Prelà.
A small Palazzo Vecchio in Gargano.

The municipality of the upper Val Fontanabuona along the Lavagna stream; in the hamlet of Terrarossa, renamed Terrarossa Colombo, lived the grandfather and great-grandfather of Christopher Columbus, the woollings, and from here starts the Colombian itinerary of 19 km to Genoa Quinto. In Gattorna, on a hill, stands the sanctuary of Our Lady of the Guard.

Medieval village on the slopes of the Martani Mountains dominated by the Rocca dei Borgia (1494-500), where in 1624 Galileo stayed; the territory is an open-air museum of castles of the 13th-XIV centuries, from Barattano to San Terentiano, Marcellano, Saragano and Grutti.

One of the three poles of the Alabaster Ecomuseum, with Castellina Marittima and Volterra, housed in the former Town Hall. It preserves working tools, iconographic material, alabaster artifacts, archaeological finds of the territory and documentation on the quarries, dug in underground tunnels with explosions sometimes dangerous to extract the 'ovuli' then worked in Volterra.
Closed for renovation, reopening not communicated
One of the city's green lungs: the tree-lined boulevard with statues, the pond with the small island and the small temple, the shady grove.
A century of history in 15 halls.

On a limestone hill at the northern edge of the village, it is built in blocks of marl limestone that give it the characteristic white color. Born as a single tower nuraghe in the Middle Bronze (XV-XIV century B.C.), it was expanded in several phases until it became a trilobed fortress with a wall to protect a village of huts (XII-XI century B.C.); there are traces of Roman and Byzantine use. The inner chamber of the central tower, covered with tholos with 37 rows, is almost 12 meters high and is described as the highest in Nuragic Sardinia; you can visit the lower floor. The name comes from the fathers Scolopi ("the friars"), owners of the land since the seventeenth century.
A stone bridge from the 18th century.
Underground cellars dug in the rock, open to visitors with tasting.
The quiet sea away from the crowd.

The park embraces the territories of Genga, Fabriano, Serra San Quirico and Arcevia, with 35 marked paths and rafting and canoeing on the river Sentino; among the routes there is the Trail of the Eagle, panoramic ring on the Apennines.

The main square is a balcony on Umbria: from the terrace the view reaches to the mountains of Lazio and Abruzzo. In the alleys of the village a medieval well-tank and the sixteenth-century portal of the former monastery.
The restored processional machines.

Open-air stone theatre built in 1928 in style inspired by classical antiquity, with a large circular stage, colonnade on the sides and staircase on the front; it takes its name from the consul who ruled the Roman colony of Herba. Immersed in the green behind the Monument to the Fallen of the First World War (1928-1931), until the mid-fifties it hosted performances of famous producers and stage designers and is still used today, especially in summer.
The truest Parma, the one of the barricades of 1922.
The valley of the pastures.
On a rocky spur almost overhanging the river, it is the reconstruction of the first parish church, the oldest religious building in the territory; around it was born the first nucleus of Subiaco.
The strengthest remains over the city.
Next to the Duomo, with frescoes by Tiepolo.
In Palazzo Fauzone, about two hundred years of Monregalian ceramics; here also the tourist office.
MiC card (updated to April 2020) indicates closed every day
The fresco of Ceresa in the main church.
A secret garden above the square.
The museum residence.
The museum of reference of Bassa Romagna.

In the hamlet of Valcasotto, with the parish church of San Ludovico king of France in 1666, an ancient stone mill from the Napoleonic era is still in operation and mature cheeses are produced in underground premises.
Fraction with a compact and square plan, surrounded by a perimeter of canals; there stands Corte Motella, a typical example of a manor house of court.

On the main square, dedicated to the patron, bishop and martyr of ancient Civitas Martana. The current building is from the Quattro-Cinquecento, restored after the bombings of the Second World War; bell tower of 1637. Single nave with barrel vault, Baroque altar with canvas by Giacinto Boccanera da Leonessa of 1723, 16th century frescoes (Crucifixion; Madonna enthroned between the Saints Rocco and Ambrogio) and fifteenth century Folignate school.

On a tufa spur between the Cimini Mountains and the Tiber, it was born as a strategic military fortress for the defense of Rome; at the beginning of the seventeenth century the Duke Pietro Altemps transformed it into a noble residence, with finishes attributed to Carlo Fontana and the double staircase to Giacomo della Porta. In the mid-nineteenth century Altemps passed to Duke Jules Hardouin of Walese, whose daughter Maria, the future wife of Gabriel of Annunzio, walked there with the poet in the park.

Small village of the Amalfi Coast, UNESCO heritage, more collected than the nearby Maiori, overlooking the sea between churches and lemon groves and known as a city of taste; it houses the Roman maritime villa of the first century A.D., the basilica of the patron saint Trofimena and the arrival of the Trail of Lemons.
A Romanesque parish church on the ancient Pitinum.
The heart of the city is federic.

With Paul III Farnese, in the sixteenth century, Castro became the capital of a duchy and was embellished with churches, palaces and walls also by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger; in 1649 the troops of Innocent X razed it to the ground. Today the ruins are covered by the forest: the excavations have brought to light the main square with the Palazzo della Zecca, the cathedral, the convent of San Francesco, the fortifications and Porta Lamberta; you arrive with a path marked by the road Ponte San Pietro-Farnese.
The most authentic Livorno.
High Val Chisone country linked to the largest fortified structure in Europe, with a covered staircase of about 4000 steps.
The tower of Spanish knights.
The elegant heart of Bolzano.
At Sasso Pisano fumarole and showerheads that give the landscape an infernal air; near the Biolago, fed by natural hot water and geothermal district heating.
The altarpiece of the Bergognone.
Church of the sixteenth century dedicated to the patron saint of the country.

The first nucleus of the archaeological park of ancient Abella: built in the first century BC in the south-eastern part of the city, on an area previously occupied by sannitic houses, in cross-linked work on the walls, with substructions on the south-western side for the average and the summa cavea, the latter not preserved.

Brick village on the border with Tuscany, the birthplace of Perugino: five of his works between the Duomo, Santa Maria dei Bianchi, Santa Maria dei Servi and San Pietro, the Palazzo della Corgna and the narrowest alley in Italy.

From the central square, surrounded by stone buildings, you walk along the medieval village, partly surrounded by walls and crossed by a narrow street and many passages; under the castle, towards the valley, there is the Su di Dentro, once accessible by a stone arch, where lived the shoemakers to which the name of the village is linked.
The oldest Romanesque in Varese.
The life of a musician in his manuscripts.
Modern theatre of the 1930s behind a neoclassical façade of 1894-1895, recently restored.
The castle of the Prince Bishops and the Tower of Fame.
The tombs of the kings of Sicily.

The walk Cellina-Eremo has two easy and marked routes, of 1.1 and 2 km, suitable for families, with panoramic stops. For more experienced hikers there is the ring of Santa Caterina del Sasso, about 20 km and 400 m of difference in altitude in about 5 hours between woods, ancient mule tracks and small villages, and the AVLM 01 trail to the Refuge De Grande Adamoli on the Pizzoni di Laveno, about 14 km and over 1000 m of difference in altitude.

Villa of U delight designed by Giovanni Ruggeri for Giacinto Alari, with works from 1702 to about 1721 and chapel of St. Teresa blessed in 1725; garden towards the Naviglio. In 1772-1776 the governor of Lombardy resided there, Archduke Ferdinand of Habsburg, with Beatrice d'Este; since 1831 of the Visconti of Saliceto, in 1948 he passed to the Fatebenefratelli and has been public since 2007. Hall of music, gallery and ballroom have frescoes and golden stuccoes by Giovan Angelo Borroni, Francesco Fabbrica and (attributes) Pietro Maggi; in 2014 it was the most voted place in Lombardy at the ... Places of the heart .
From the Genoese forts to the botanical path above the sea.

According to the tradition reported by the municipality, the gate and tower were built by the Saracens who arrived around 980, who closed with walls and fortresses the lower part of the country forcing the inhabitants to work; the tower, very solid and with small doors hidden for the sortites, watched for centuries the neighborhood with a stable military garrison.
Built in 1102 as a chapel next to the Consulate of the Genoese and renovated in 1639 on a project by Bonaventura Sure.
Two ancient Regi Lagni cities.
Woods, villages and a waterfall in one ring.

In the highest part of the village, the ancient Monteverde, guarding the Treste: around a watchtower the oldest part was built in 1095 by Pandolfo di Sangro; between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the tower was transformed into a fortified noble residence. It dominates the massive tower with a polygonal base with a shoe, cylindrical body and Guelph merli on hanging arches; the complex includes walls, passetto, palazzo marquisale in the 15th century and the chapel of San Carlo, eighteenth century, with stone portal. Restored and owned by the municipality, it hosts the town hall, events and parties.
Looking at the sky in the land of the discoverer of Ceres.

In a former stable next to the Park Visitor Centre, documents the Apennine wolf with a rebuilt skeleton, a naturalized specimen and a diorama of the den; from here start the routes to the fauna of the wolf, on the hill in front of the village, and that of the lynx, in the upper part of the village. Closed on Tuesdays.

Area on the slopes of the Musinè, one of the richest biodiversity in Piedmont, which includes the Upper and Lower Lakes of Caselette and Lake Borgarino. The markedly xerothermal climate and the iron-rich rocks (peridotites and serpentinites) host rare species such as the Alyssum silvereum. A municipal itinerary from Piazza Cays touches the Roman villa, the plateau with the old quarries of magnesite and a lake with rushes and water lilies.

The village of the Ponti della Valle, the three-ordered viaduct of Carolino Aqueduct designed by Luigi Vanvitelli for the Palace of Caserta and part of the UNESCO site; around, the medieval castle mentioned in the Baronum Catalogus and the churches of San Pietro and the Annunziata.
A sporty curiosity in a mountain country.
In the hamlet of Iola, next to the church of Santa Maria Maddalena: thousands of objects that tell the traditional culture of the Modena mountain.
The sea of the Romans.

Opened on August 3, 2002 in the building that housed the town hall and elementary schools, in front of the square, it was born from the collection donated by the parish priest Don Giovanni Bonomo, then enriched by other collectors. It preserves 3,333 minerals found almost all in Valle Antigorio and Val Formazza, including cervandonite, gasparite, fetiasitis and asbecaite. Open from July 15 to August 30 every day and from December 27 to January 4 and Easter, 16-18; other days by contacting the Municipality (tel. 0324 62021).
Overlooking Piazza Grande, the parish church of Santa Maria Maddalena and the oratory are baroque buildings.
The most collected lakefront.

Regional reserve of about 500 hectares between Forgaria and Trasaghis, between the Tagliamento greto and the walls of the Carnic Prealps, home to almost twenty years of an international project to protect the griffin, which is observed in flight especially in the morning; there are also owl real, allocus of the Urals, vulture monk and head vulture. Tour centre with aviaries and terrariums, trails to the lake and Tagliamento, guided tours by reservation.
Walking or mountain biking trails that start from the fortress towards the hills of the Val Conca.

Located in a loop of the Metauro, the center has fifteenth-century plant, regular streets and porticos; from the small Piazza San Cristoforo, with the column of the patron, radiate the central streets, and next to stands the nineteenth-century Bramante Theatre, one of the jewels of the region. Along Via Roma the public gardens with the monument to the Great War.
On the upper square, renovated in 1733, with portico of 1626 and 14 newsstands of the Via Crucis frescoed in the eighteenth century.

The tower was part of the defensive system of the second circle of walls; it became a civic tower and received the clock during the municipal period. Today it hosts a permanent exhibition on the seasons and rural life, with paintings by Giovanni Aiello and tools of work in the fields.

Castle in the form of the fifteenth century, built on a previous building (recipe or castle, according to scholars), originally with regular plan with angular towers, central tower and a moat 12 meters wide attested in the seventeenth century. Renovated from the seventeenth century and transformed into a noble residence by the Arborio di Gattinara, there is now only one tower.

Distillery that offers guided tours to the production and the barricade of aging, the Galleria della grappa and the Enoteca Monferrina, an underground cantinone where you taste grappa, distillates, liqueurs, brandy and fruit under spirit.
The sanctuary of the spring festival.
The flora of the Ernici Mountains in a single path.

In the basements of the former Hospital of the Infirms, built in the 15th century, it follows the cycle of wine from the harvest to bottling with presses, vats, barrels and crushers; the most important piece is the oak press called "frisculu" in 1695. In the rooms next to the wine shop with historic bottles and wines of the territory: tasting for a fee, by reservation.

Built in 1615 by the Marquis Giambattista Castelli, it is a work of late Mannerism decorated with heads of lion and mythological figures; fed by mountain springs, it is the meeting point of the inhabitants.

The view of the Valdarno from the Cerbaie.

Itinerary of the Municipality from Piazza del Sole: in via Costantini seventeenth-century palaces and, in Vico San Vito, the succession of public, semi-public and private spaces of the house at court (n. 41 a poor peasant house); via Montinari with the church of Sant'Antonio, the ancient 'hospitale' for pilgrims, the courts of San Calimero and San Paolo and Palazzo Montinari, which is said to be the residence of the last protopapàs of the Greek rite Sigismondo De Matteis (dead in 1621); the chapel of Carmine with date 1577; in Via Mayro Palazzo Murrone (sixth century nucleus), the birthplace of the Hellenist Vito Domenico Palumbo (1854-1918) and the court and chapel of the Crucifix of 1698, with frescoed vault and wooden crucifix seventeenth century.
The art of the Twentieth Century Valdostano.

Natural amphitheatre from about 1,200 places obtained in 2013 from a abandoned quarry, near the historic center; in summer it hosts shows, exhibitions and the Borgofuturo festival.
The Norman tower and the feast of the black saint.
The Godfather's bar.

Cream-coloured sand crescent mixed with pebbles at the entrance of the village, on the Anglon seafront, dominated by the castle on the promontory: low and sandy bottom suitable for children and two snorkeling fringes; parking, bar and restaurant.

The only hamlet of the municipality, preserves the typical urban structure of a medieval village-castle, with its historical centre with circular plan and pedestrian Belvedere Square, where the exhibition of outdoor sculptures is set up. The church of San Pietro is of medieval origin, renovated in the nineteenth century; recent studies suggest an Etruscan origin of the village, and in the historical center and on the hill of San Rocco are ongoing reliefs on ancient hypogeans.

The municipality of Alto Ionio Cosentino, Blue Flag since 2026: the National Archaeological Museum "Vincenzo Laviola" tells about the settlements from the Bronze Age to Greek colonization, while the castle of Norman origin, then Domus Imperialis Sweva, dominates the Old Rion.

First stone laid on 28 September 1689 by Bishop Giambattista La Morea on the site of four chapels of confraternities; central nave completed in 1709 and consecration on 19 October 1766, when Bishop Nicola D'Amato raised it to basilica. Damaged by the earthquakes of 1930 and 1980, which modified its dome and facade, it was restored in 1988 on a project by architect Sergio Rosanova.
Tognazzi's country house.
The necropolis of the Ligurians.
Built in the eighteenth century in Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, on the space of a previous church of the fifteenth century demolished.

Border town with France: the medieval centre with the Romanesque Cathedral of the Assumption, the Roman Albintiminium in Nervia, the prehistoric caves of the Balzi Rossi and the Hanbury alla Mortola botanical gardens.
Panoramic road that runs over the Melfa river and connects the Comino Valley to the Liri Valley.
Frescoed rooms and Italian garden.
Archaeology overlooking the sea.
The Baroque of the ... Round of the Suffragio.

The palace, originally a grange of the Carthusians of the twelfth century, has a loggia on sixteen granite columns overlooking the Gulf of Squillace and preserves eighteenth-century majolica hand painted and the apartment of Baroness Enrichetta Scoppa with furniture of the second nineteenth century. It preserves the Pala degli Arcangeli (1603), of Michelangelo's school and attributed to Bernardino Poccetti, found in 2007; italia.it signals the chapel.
Wine village on the Via Francigena, famous for its moscato, with sixteenth-century buildings in the historic centre and the ruins of Cly on the hill.

The village stands on a hill overlooking the Langhe: once surrounded by high walls, of which only one arch of the fourteenth century remains, it is a almost vertical village of stairs and sternìe ( steep streets) paved in red bricks, remained closed until the sixties between two arches with acute sixth. From the panoramic points you can see the Langhe and, on clear days, the Ligurian Sea. It was quoted in 998 in a document by Otto III; the Municipal Statutes are dated April 3, 1301.

The spa opened in 2008 in Cadarese, indicated as the most important in northern Piedmont: the spring water, classified hyperthermal sulphate-calcic, flows at 44 °C. It offers thermal baths, spa, beauty treatments and medical treatment for specific pathologies.
The ruins of the town fortress.

Medieval village of the upper valley of the Albegna, on the slopes of Mount Amiata, dominated by the spur of the Stone; in the square the church of Saints Peter and Paul with the triptych of Ambrogio Lorenzetti and, behind, the Oratory of the Crucifix; in the territory the village of Cana, the castle of Triana, the Museum of the Focarazza of Saint Catherine and the reserves of Pescinello and Bosco Rocconi.

Città dell'alto Milanese known for the Sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of Miracles, with frescoes by Bernardino Luini and the dome by Gaudenzio Ferrari, and for the collection of ancient ceramics Gianetti.
The mill was in operation until 1961.

Small karst lake of circular shape, about 120 meters of diameter and 10 meters of maximum depth, at 719 meters of altitude, fed by two sources of drinking water. The 2009 earthquake had cracked its banks threatening its disappearance, but consolidation work recovered it; grassy banks, woods and willows make it a frequent destination on weekends, with area equipped for bivouac.

Overlooking the scenic Piazza Duomo, it has a Norman bell tower and an eighteenth-century bell tower and three naves supported by twelve columns that recall the Apostles. Inside a Deposition attributed to Ribera, a Madonna among the angels of Gaspare Vazzano and, in the right aisle, the first crucifix of Friar Umile (1623).
Green a few steps from the center.

The main street, with portals, late Renaissance and Baroque palaces, porticos, shops and churches; on some facades sixteenth century frescoes of the Virgin with the Child and Saints, linked by tradition to the plague of 1508. The center, of Venetian character, develops on the two banks of the Brenta around Piazza Alcide De Gasperi.

Inside the Fortress, born from the collection of Princess Bona Borromeo Arese; it is indicated as the most important in Europe of its kind. It has porcelain, wood and plastic dolls, handmade and standard, from Germany, Spain, Japan and other countries, with a core of French school, as well as wooden and tin toys and books and newspapers for boys from the eighteenth century to today.
Borgo dell'alta Val Nervia, Orange Flag, with the fifteenth-century loggia of Piazza Umberto I and the frescoes and the polyptych of Canavesio in the churches of San Michele and San Bernardo.
Magnetite tunnels.
seat of municipal offices: the source does not indicate hours of visit of the interiors

Outside Porta Alvaro, the convent arose after 1290; in April 1560 a fire destroyed the church but the consecrated host was found intact and Pius IV recognized the miracle, granting the indulgence of the "Perdoni" (17-27 April). Rebuilt by the Municipality in 1564, the Latin cross church preserves the old bell tower and is now auditorium; in the cloister there is the bust of Luigi Canale of the sculptor Cantalamessa.
A medieval church in the hills.
The small fishing village overlooking the sea of Posillipo, born around the church of Santa Maria del Faro, with restaurants on the sea, wooden gozzos and views of the gulf from Vesuvius to Capri.

The nineteenth-century districts under the castle, expansion beyond the walls desired by Gioacchino Murat, king of Naples: regular blocks, green squares, public offices and shops; on Piazza Gabriele Pepe overlook the Government Palace, the Bank of Italy and the Banco di Napoli.

In the middle of the medieval village, with the remains of the Donjon in the background, exhibits archaeological finds: metal objects (knifes, nails, horseshoes, tools), glass, worked bone, fusaiole, pipe, a base of limestone fireplace with anthropomorphic figure, stone bullets, coins and about 150 ceramics, including glazed XII-XIII and protomaiolic of the XIII-XIV. Contacts: tel. 0827 45031.
A fifteenth-century convent with museums and wine shop inside.
The sanctuary of the miracle of 1555, the heart of the Feast of Forgiveness.
Two centuries of scientific collections.

Museum of art in the center with modern and contemporary art, a historical collection and sacred works of art, as well as exhibitions of contemporary artists; it is located beyond Porta Rienza, in via Fratel Willram.
The history of plastic in the factory that produced it.
The village of the Knights of Malta.

First ethnographic museum of Gallura, in a granite building of the late eighteenth century in the historic center: on three floors it reconstructs the rooms of the Gallura house, with the vinification on the ground floor, kitchen, dining room and bedroom on the first floor and the processing of wool and cork at the last. The symbol piece is the "martello" of the feminine agabbadora, a branch of olive grove of about 40 cm found in an abandoned building near the village, linked to the figure that according to tradition ended the agony of the dying.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 8 of the 10 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Walk between historic villas and the park overlooking the lake.
A country jewel.
Baroque church built between 1625 and 1630, with the dome frescoed by Robert De Longe in 1705.

The historical centre, divided by the Adda, preserves the Rivellino of 1404 wanted by Cabrino Fondulo, the doors Cream, Cremona Nuova and Rescue (the latter on the river) and the Town Hall of the second half of the fifteenth century; on the right bank, Gera keeps almost entire its belt with casematte and an ancient powder keg.
Fortified church of the fifteenth century near the river San Rocco, reached by a mule track, with frescoes from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century.
It reconstructs the shops of the shoemaker, tailor, carpenter and farmer's corner.

At 929 meters on Mount Avena, above Facen, it is reached with a steep path; built by a hermit between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, probably on the ruins of a watchtower, had the pronao in 1863. For centuries, a destination for pilgrims, for the legend of the rainwater of the circular tank that healed from the cough; near is the Sass del Diaol.

From the 12th century, among the best preserved Romanesque monuments of Lombardy, on the homonymous hill reachable on foot from the center with a staircase in the green; it preserves a fresco of San Pancrazio del Romanino (about 1527) and works by Paolo Caylina and Callisto Piazza. Free admission on Sunday afternoon in summer.
The village-seeing on the valley of the Tiepid.

The ancient marine republic protected by Genoa, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: the Porta di Piazza, the Town Hall with the tower, the Loggia della Repubblica, the medieval red brick towers and the castle of Monte Ursino above the village.

Medieval village on a promontory of Lake Bracciano, with the sixteenth-century door of the clock, the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Assunta and the fifteenth-century Tower; in front of the shore lies submerged the Neolithic village of Marmot, of which a pirogue of about 8,000 years is exposed to the Neolithic Museum.
A shrine in altitude on an ancient place of worship.
A wooded hill with traces of an ancient castle.
A giant nativity scene, open all year round.
The long Blue Flag beach.

Country at the foot of the Bisalta, gold medal for military and civil valor for the fires and massacres of 1943: the partisan works of Adriana Filippi in the former spinning mill, the mushroom museum, the chestnut eco-museum in the Marquet park and the sanctuary of Madonna dei Boschi with frescoes from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century.
It is the oldest sacred place in Casalbore, with origins that the sources trace back to the pagan times.
The Sardinian peasant house and the miniature domus.

Seaside town on the Gulf of Gaeta, the ancient Formiae: in the medieval village of Castellone the Roman Cisternone of the 1st century BC, the octagonal tower and the church of Sant'Erasmo; on the port of Mola the Angevin tower of 1289, on the Appian Way the Tomb of Cicero, the National Archaeological Museum with the statues of the forum and the park of Gianola with the villa of Mamurra.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 1 of the 6 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
System of fortifications partly buried or hidden by vegetation, which the municipality is recovering with the Alpine volunteers.

Benedictine Romanesque Abbey in the valley of the Rio Sacro, in Acquacanina, with a Romanesque crypt with three naves, a crucifix of the Lazio school of the twelfth century, a wooden group of the Madonna with the Child of the sixteenth century, the small canvas of the Madonna of the Suffragio of Carlo Maratta and a fresco of the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano attributed to Jerome of John.
One of the greatest masterpieces of the Lombard Renaissance.
visits only by reservation (Common, tel. 0966 964048)
Mother church built in 1761, with facade in limestone and Latin cross plan; it houses a marble altar in polychrome tarsies and a wooden statue of Paolo Saverio di Zinno.

It has one of the oldest doors, the Old Door, already marked in a 1605 print; the current forms date back to changes between the second half of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and on the vault of the subjectic there is the coat of arms of Bishop Antonio Caprioli, dated 1557.

The path of the Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga National Park marked according to the CAI rules, which starts from the square in front of the church of San Bartolomeo and leads to the Abbey of Santa Maria di Casanova, at Villa Celiera.

Country of Canavese a few kilometers from Chivasso, for centuries under the jurisdiction of the abbeys of Fruttuaria: the abbey castle then of the counts Frola, the main medieval porticoed street with Casa Bricca and the Baroque churches.
The Habsburg world in the ancient thermal baths.
A medieval ruin of surveillance on the path of the Seprio.

Borgo delle Madonie, in the Madonie Park, known for its ash manna: the Castello dei Ventimiglia of 1317 with the Civic Museum and the Palatine Chapel of Serpotti stuccoes, the Madrice Vecchia, the Church of San Francesco with the Mausoleum of Ventimiglia and the Naturalistic Museum Minà Palumbo.
The Romanesque parish of the village.
Neoclassical villa that is mirrored in the canal immediately after the bridge, with double garden, amphitheatre, coffee house and glacier.

Well-preserved village of typical stone houses with view, in panoramic position among valleys overlooking the Raganello Gorges. The origins go back to the Neolithic, documented by a burial of about 7,000 years ago in the Cave of Pietra Sant'Angelo; from 1534 passed to the Marquis Pignatelli and preserves traces of the noble families. The name comes from a baronial family that built the first chapel of San Lorenzo. From the village, for the Great Gate, you go up to the highest part of the Park.

Country of land and sea in the Taranto, linked to rural culture and DOC wine that bears its name, with the Civic Museum of Palaeontology and Man in Palazzo Majorano, the rock church of the Annunziata and the Grotto of Sant'Angelo. The Marina di Lizzano stretches for 7 km on the Ionian coast between clear sand, dunes and Mediterranean maquis.

Former fifteenth-century church in via Garibaldi, among eighteenth-century buildings, now used for cultural events.

The diocesan museum, in the sacristy of the church of Our Lady of the Rosary (1630, with the altar of sos paladinos), preserves sacred furnishings, Mannerist paintings, silverware, gold jewels, statues of the XVII-XVIII century, ex vow and sacred vestments.
The sunset on the Tigullio.
accessible only by reservation (card AI Smart)
The most beautiful road in the world is inside the throat.
The oldest church of Bisuschio, with traces of the early Middle Ages.
17th century church just outside the village, on the green shore of a small lake.

According to tradition, the Virgin appeared on 23 June 1607 to the sisters Maria and Caterina Salera during a storm; the first stone was laid on 24 June 1608 and the bell tower started in 1645. Three-nave basilica with 18th-century façade in local stone and red marble, frescoes by Alberto and Cesare Mironi and Antonio Guadagnini and pulpit of the Fantoni workshop; in the presbytery the "Santa dei Santi" room, the Salera room of the apparition. Every 23 June the Feast of the Apparition with solemn procession.

The most western village of the Cinque Terre, divided by the hill of San Cristoforo between the ancient center at the mouth of Buranco and Fegina with the statue of the Giant; places of Montale and the sanctuary of Soviore.
The medieval origins of the city from above.
The garden of the fountains that has been schooled in Europe.
The district of sailors and trattorias.
It climbs from the fourteenth-century staircase with balustrade; it was the hall where the monks sang the night office and preserves the oldest painting of the complex, of the twelfth century.
A curious stop on the road to Pomposa.

Until the 17th century Arzachena was a small group of houses around the church of Santa Maria. From the centre, a short walk leads to the Incappiddhatu Mountains, the "Roccia del Fungo" shaped by the wind and used since the recent Neolithic period; in the village there is also the colorful staircase of Saint Lucia and La Box of Time, a museum on the history of the city indicated among the smallest in Italy.
The seventeenth-century arch erected as a vote for the end of the plague, which closes to the north via Vittorio Emanuele; to the south the eighteenth-century arch of Porta Narzole.

The private chapel of the fourteenth century (the municipality celebrated 650 years of it in 2019, counting since October 1369) with a cycle painted on the life of Saint Stephen; behind the altar a Crucifixion frescoed by a disciple of Giotto. Stefano Porro appears several times in the frescoes of the nave, in front of his patron saint or hidden among the scenes. Visits by reservation on Sunday, writing to the City Culture Office.

Founded in 1979, at about 1,500 meters at the foot of Mount Reit near the Stelvio National Park: about 15,000 m2 with over 2,500 species in four environments (flora of the Park, of the European and world mountain ranges, Arctic and Antarctica); it collects and reproduces rare plants. Open from July to September.
The defensive symbol of the old town.

The town of Marca, crossed by the Sile and the canals with frescoed buildings: Piazza dei Signori, the Pescheria on the island, the Buranelli, the Duomo with Tiziano and the museums of Santa Caterina and Bailo.
The panoramic sanctuary.
The amphitheatre of the ancient Capua, of which the giant arches remain; for dimensions second only to the Colosseum. The ticket to the archaeological circuit also includes the Mitreo.

Built by the princes of Capua around the year 1000, it preserves imposing remains with square towers; from the strategic position on the hill you can see the Abbey of Montecassino and the Gulf of Gaeta.

The main square, with one of the centers of the town life, is striking for the breadth and richness of the palaces that surround it; its trapezoidal shape is best grasped from the center, where is located the Triton Fountain.

Large maritime villa on three levels, excavated in 1988-1991: about 1,300 square meters and 40 rooms between residence with mosaics and heating and productive spaces, in use from the 1st century BC to the 4th A.D., perhaps also station between Aquileia and Tergeste (Fons Timavi) Visits by reservation in the aqueduct park.
Built in 1873 by the company "Della Concordia" on a project by Nazareno Biscarini.

The miracle of herring told in bronze.
The museum dedicated to the career of Giorgio Armani in the Tortona area, next to Mudec.
The two towers Donà and Grimani (Mozza), the remains of the expansive castle of 1138 integrated into the walls; the Tower Donà is 66 meters high.

A walk of about 5.5 km (4 hours and a half) starting from the Fountain of Scorza, passes through the fountain of Pietra della Madonna and the chestnut groves, to reach Monte dell'Uovo (about 1,417 m) and climbs through a steep forest to Pizzo San Michele (1,567 m), where stands the sanctuary of San Michele Arcangelo, indicated as the highest place of worship in Italy. From the summit you can see the Gulf of Salerno, the Monti Lattari, the Partenio, the Vesuvio and the Matese.

Erected in the 11th century (between 1030 and 1080) by the will of the judge of Torres with Pisan maestranzes, on Mount Angellu, where there were a Roman and early Christian necropolis and two churches of the 5th and 7th centuries; it was the cathedral of the diocese from 484 to 1441. Along 58 meters, with two opposite apses and without facade, it has three naves divided by 22 columns of pink granite and grey marble of strip, a Romanesque portal with Adam and Eve to the north and a Gothic-Catalan to the south. In the crypt, reached by a gallery, the sarcophagi with the relics of the martyrs Gavino, Proto and Gianuario, found in 1614.

The village of the noble Milanese villas is located on the opposite banks of the Naviglio Grande, joined by a bridge with donkey back, with a sequence of villas of six-nineteenth-century delight, the church of Santa Maria Nascente, the oratory rococo di San Giuseppe and the Molino dei Biraghi of the fifteenth century.
The sanctuary on the mountain above the village.
Market every third Sunday of the month
The most beautiful metro station in Europe.

The village, built on ancient Etruscan and Roman settlements, has squares, churches, historic buildings and testimonies of rural life of the past, between characteristic villages and vineyards; in Piazza Roma, in Palazzo Carlotti, is the seat of IAT Baldo Garda.
A Neolithic tomb with carved taurine horns.

Sanctuary of the XIV-XV centuries on a rocky spur above the sources of the Menotre, in the hamlet of San Martino, reachable only on foot; inside votive frescoes from the XV to the XVII century, including a Madonna of Loreto and a Saint Christopher attributed to Paolo di Visso.
The Valnerina on foot or by bike.
The last of the seven castle towers.
The baroque residence.

He replaced the ancient fortress: in 1597 the Marquise Claudia di Savoia and his son Francesco Filiberto Ferrero Fieschi built it. In 1624 Masserano, tired of the prince's oppressions, invaded him by destroying the second floor, rebuilt and enlarged by 1634. In the fifth room, called the Zodiac or Throne, ceilings attributed to the Tanzius and friezes attributed to the Gianoli; exposed some coins of the Mint of Masserano. Today it is the seat of the town hall.

A ring of about 3.5 hours (medium-high difficulty, recommended in spring and autumn) from Piazza Santa Croce di Termini: the chapel of San Costanzo on the lower summit (485 m) looks at the gulfs of Naples and Salerno and the islets of the Galli; from the summit of 496 m, the highest of the territory, you see Capri; the path then descends towards Punta Campanella.
In the castle, opened in 1967, the first regional wine shop in Piedmont and one of the oldest in Italy.
Two steps between the walls of the old castrum.

Country residence built in the eighteenth century by the Crispolti in the plain of Bettona, of neoclassical appearance from the second half of the century; the project is attributed to Giuseppe Piermarini, but the Superintendence indicates that the attribution is not certain (other hypothesis: Antonio Stefanucci). Interiors with stuccoes, mirrors, lanterns and helical stairs, stairway, secret garden with water lilies, exedra, obelisks and English grove, straight avenue, courtyard of honor and the church of the Santissima Annunziata. It was the seat of the German command in the Second World War; today it is of the State, which began its restoration.
The vast gardens of the Reggia, part of the UNESCO complex, between the history of the garden and contemporary interpretations; from here you can rent bikes for the Mandria.
The village of the gates and bonfires.

About 5 km from the centre, it dates back to the 12th century, at the time of Ruggero II, on the impulse of Sant'Ugo Abate; it is considered the most significant example of Cistercian architecture in Sicily, with a sober style that reflects poverty and simplicity.
Hiking destinations from the village: Monte Dego (1427 m), Monte Alfeo (1651 m) and Passo di Cariseto (1077 m).

It traces the history of the production of olive oil, from a long period in which the methods of processing seemed unchanged until the early twentieth century, when technological progress marked a turning point. It has ancient tools in use since the eighteenth century, including lever presses and grinders operated by hydraulic wheel; a section with videos and educational panels explains the cultivation of the olive and the production of the oil. Accessible without architectural barriers.
The most spectacular mannerism.
Near the walls, it offers a beautiful view of the surrounding hilly landscape.

Porta della Val di Fassa and Ladin village between Catinaccio, Latemar and Monzoni, in the Alpine Pearls since 2011: above the center of squares and districts dominates the church of San Vigilio, while the memory of the Great War lives in the exhibition La Gran Vera at the Navalge Theatre and in the stable-museum of Someda, next to the Austro-Hungarian fort of 1898.
It preserves a fresco with Saint Lucia, Saint Rocco and the Madonna and Child, probably a pupil of Perugino.
Among the unmissable stages of Venice, famous for Tintoretto's paintings.
A hamlet church painted in the early 20th century.
Elegant Livorno.
The cathedral of the Peligna Valley.
Where a prehistoric Sicilian culture was born.
The Palladian villa on the Brenta, a few kilometers from the lagoon.
The symbol of the small Liguria of Garda.
A 17th century villa with garden of the early 19th century.
In the former monastery of San Biagio, more than 300 paintings and sculptures from the fifteenth century to the contemporary age, especially of Emilia-Romagna area.
The Po museum.
The church of Piazza dei Signori, partly rebuilt at the end of the sixteenth century.
Vittoria, the most recent city in the province, has a chessboard plan and a historic centre with a Liberty area that revolves around Via Cavour and Piazza del Popolo.
The residence of the late nineteenth century in Renaissance style in the 13th century hamlet of Castelmartini, with a garden of particular trees and a rose garden.

Palazzo nobiliare in the historic center, which can be visited with the circuit of the civic museums: guided tours on weekends in spring and autumn, daily opening (except Wednesday) from June to September.

A small town in the lower Seriana Valley, which can be reached by tram from Bergamo, home of the 16th century painter Giovan Battista Moroni, whose works he preserves in the churches of San Giuliano, Madonna del Pianto and Santa Barbara; in the hamlets the medieval bridge over Serio, the ethnographic museums of Comenduno and Valle del Lujo and the museum of Blessed Pierina Morosini in Fiobbio.

About 3 km from the center, which has been reported since the second half of the seventeenth century, put into operation after a long abandonment; the water of the source of San Teodoro flows at about 28 °C, rich in minerals, and is used for crenotherapy. The complex, close to the geosite of the Mefite in Valle d'Ansanto, includes a hotel, restaurant, swimming pools and wellness centre, and next to a small ancient chapel. Open Monday to Saturday 7:30-13 and 14:30-18:30.

Romanesque church of origin of the twelfth century, with sixteenth century aquasantiera in white marble, the Madonna del Rosario of Florentine Domenico Pugliani, the Assumption of the Virgin of Spinamonte (1615) in the apse, two glazed terracottas in the presbytery and two side altarpieces of Santi Buglioni. On the singing hall, the monumental organ, purchased in 1811 by Domenico Achilli from the convent of San Lorenzo di Pistoia: built by Pietro Agati with part of a sixteenth-century instrument by Cesare Romani da Cortona, expanded in 1824 and 1856, has about two thousand rods, three keyboards and two pedals and effects such as roaring and grancassa; every year Italian and foreign organists play there.

Church built in 1335, rebuilt from 1633 and completed in 1770 in Baroque Lecce, with monumental Rococo façade rich in friezes, niches and statues. Inside, frescoes, altars in polychrome marble and paintings, the Captello del Sacramento of the second half of the seventeenth century, the vault frescoed at the end of the nineteenth century with the life of St. Peter and the stone on which, according to tradition, St. Peter rested, brought here in 1670.

At the top of the Fontane hill, in a pine forest with rare Aleppo pines: tradition ties her to the shipwreck of ships of children headed to the Holy Land. Rebuilt in trachite from 1742, enlarged at the end of the eighteenth century by the Porcile family and restored in 1928; a single nave with barrel vault, tombstones of the Porcile, traces of fresco and late Piedmontese Baroque façade.

The capital of the trulli, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996: the Monti and Aia Piccola districts with over 1,600 trulli, the Trullo Soverano with two floors, the house museum of Casa Pezzolla and the Santa Lucia viewpoint on the grey roofs of white houses.

On the main square the church of Santa Maria d'Itria, rebuilt from 1742 after the earthquake of 1693 on the project of the Messinese Giuseppe La Rosa, with interiors decorated in 1863-1864 and facade remained unfinished at the top; in front of the neoclassical Palazzo di Città, built between 1870 and 1882.

Next to the parish church of San Martino, a 14-station Via Crucis with 198 life-size statues in wood and plaster, commissioned in 1752 to Benjamin Simoni by the parish priest Don Andrea Boldini and completed in 1764 by Donato and Grazioso Fantoni (stations VIII, IX and perhaps X); the 14th current station is Giovanni Selleroni (1869), while the original of Simoni is in Breno. The frescoes on the walls are by Scotti and the Corbellini brothers; in the parish there are wooden sculptures of Andrea Fantoni's workshop. Guided tours for groups or individuals organized by parish and municipality, which also include the church of Our Lady of Carmine.
In Palazzo Peloso Cepolla, over a thousand amphorae of a first century BC Roman cargo ship sunk in front of Albenga, recovered since 1950.
The fishing village told in stone.
Municipal forest park at the foot of the Pollino National Park, wooded area with artificial pond and picnic areas.
Over a thousand hectares of historic pine forest planted by monks around the year 1000, 11 km long, in the Po Delta Park.
The painted doors of the city.
The church of the patron on the piazza del castello.
Housed in a noble palace in red trachite of the thirteenth century, it exhibits paintings and sculptures of important Italian artists, in particular of the 1950s of the twentieth century.

The village of Alta Valle Sabbia between Lake Garda and Lake Idro, facing like an amphitheatre on the banks of Brescia del Garda and formed by three medieval districts; on Mount Stino, panoramic between the two lakes, there is the Museum of war finds, set up in the galleries of the fortifications of the Great War.
The early Christian Milan.
The square on top of the village with the Palazzo del Podestà, the Fontana del Duca and the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Assunta, Romanesque with Gothic and Renaissance parts.
Church in the historic center, next to Villa d'Este.
In the former hospital of Santo Spirito del Cinquecento, the Pliocene marine fossils of which Castell'Arquato is a typical place, with the reconstruction of a whale.
Frescoes in a church of the year 1000.
A fortress of 4,500 years ago, older than the nuraghi.

It collects tools and tools recovered by Giuseppe Antonelli and other donors, with testimonies of lost trades such as the coal-making and the hay-making pastor, a section on the care of chestnuts and the processing of chestnuts for sweet flour and books on the history of the territory. Guided tour included, upon request and booking.

Borgo dell'alta valle Scrivia on a wooded cove of Monte Schigonzo, in the Parco Naturale Regionale dell'Antola; the name unites     Â"Croce" (Croce), crossroads of ancient traffic routes, and the Fieschi family, who built the Gemelli Palaces there. Summer holiday destination and base for excursions such as the Rocche del Reopasso.
The eighteenth-century parish church with three naves with octagonal dome and six altars, where the Fallets are buried.
Getting lost in the alleyways.
In Lombardy it signals the museum as temporarily closed, check with the Municipality (0332 601434)

Designed by Fabio Mangone and Francesco Maria Richino, Milanese architects of the seventeenth century. The Salvatore's chapel, with stuccoes, frescoes and Baroque paintings, and the chapel of St. Catherine, with a altarpiece by Lattanzio Gambara, stand out.

In the ancient town hall of Sant'Orsola, a 17th century building frescoed by the popular painter Pietro Albertini of Lavis, the museum tells with minerals and objects of material culture the territory and the history of the valley of Fersina. Highlights a large quartz crystal cave, the municipal council hall and a stream in the garden where to search for minerals; each visit includes two workshops, the search for stones in the stream and the construction of a fossil. Guided tours by reservation in Italian or English, audioguides in German, English and Dutch; open Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 10-12 and 14-17.
Historical district with a thousand facets, with unfinished buildings and others destroyed by the bombings: one of the unusual places recommended to discover another Catania.
The painting of Genoa in the sixteenth-sixth century in a monastery of pass.
The mother church of the city reborn after the earthquake.

Museo-Laboratorio sulle scalpellini (lapicidi) of the valley of Giara, whose school of Cènova produced decorative elements for the architecture of the whole western Liguria. Set up by the Municipality with the Montana Community, it has two sections: the stone museum in Cènova, about 140 m2 on the stone cycle from extraction to laying in operation, with videos, maps and a teaching room where to touch tips, chisels and compass; and three paths in the historical centers of Rezzo, Cènova and Lavina, where each piece is marked on the map with letter and number and described by a plaque. Tel. Common 0183 34015.
Mortara Cathedral, a gallery of Lombard art between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries.
In Barmasc, at 1828 meters, a destination of processions for the source considered miraculous that flows from the foundations of the chapel.
Erected in 1769 in the center of the village, it houses a XVI-century triptych of the Romanino school, 18th-century stucco decorations and wooden works of the Fantonian workshop.
The parish church of the historic centre with its characteristic octagonal bell tower, indicated by the Vesuvius National Park as the most significant monument in the country.
The Town Hall Palace, renaissance of the fifteenth century modified in Spanish age; Palazzo Cavassola, which housed Pope Pius VII; the Palaces Gallesio, Brunengo and the Tribunal.
The relics of the patron and the view from above.
The Red Town Hall.
The walls of the medieval village, still visible in the historic centre.
The two-tone stone streets and the sa burra carpets.
The paradise of the wind with a view of the archipelago.
Art of Meli and views of the Orobie in a morning of walk.
The Renaissance palace of the Strozzi, now home to the great international exhibitions. The courtyard and the loggia are free entrance.
Just a weekend. Winter: Sat 14-17, Sun 10-13 and 14-17
A medieval abbey, today a basilica, which preserves the relics of the saint; it rises next to the remains of the Marmon Bridge and is the twelfth stage of the Way of St. Benedict (Casamari-Arpino).
Bra's symbol.

In the western part of the village, the Venetian imprint is read in the vaults and architraves of the entrances, in the keys of vaults all different and in the removable coats of arms of the noble houses; along Corso Garibaldi a lion of San Marco looks from the first floor of the civic 135. You will meet the goldsmith shop under Palazzo Nuonno, the house of the baglivo and Palazzo Apollonio with its stone lions; at the end of the course the Belvedere Ripa, with a blacksmith shop in front of a Venetian bifora, overlooks the valley of Verrino.

Downtown Sulcis about 60 km from Cagliari, divided into two by the Mannu river: the caves of Is Zuddas with eccentric aragonites, the Phoenician-punic settlement of Pani Loriga, the Archaeological Civic Museum with the findings of the nuragic sanctuary of Su Benatzu and the house-museum Sa Domu Antiga, stage of the Mauritian Wedding in early August.
The papal heart of the village.

On the plateau of Chiavano there are still structures of a temple and the Roman forum, dominated by the small church of San Silvestro; studied in the twentieth century and the subject of recent research led by Filippo Coarelli, connected to an earthquake of 99 BC. In the late antiquity the buildings were transformed into production facilities and burials, and there was found a rare village of Longobard huts.
The peasant world next to the Etruscans.

In the house-studio of the painter Antonio Calderara (1903-1978), building of the late sixteenth century with three loggias on granite columns, there are 327 works: 56 by Calderara and 271 by 133 European, American, Japanese and Chinese artists related to him. The collection documents the international avant-gardes of the 1950s and 1960s (geometric abstraction, programmed and kinetic art, op art, visual poetry); a plan is dedicated to the path of Calderara from figurative to abstract. Open seasonally from mid-May to mid-October, from Tuesday to Sunday 10-12 and 15-18; not accessible to people with motor disabilities for stairs.
Shopping in the old town.
The bright interior wanted by the pope.
Twelve golden altars and a picture gallery in church.

What remains of a Benedictine ward isolated between secular oaks at the slopes of Velino, in the Sirente-Velino Regional Park: the first news dates back to the middle of the 11th century, when the monastery passed under Montecassino. It is one of the most important examples of Abruzzi Romanesque, with Arabic-Hispanic, Byzantine and Longobard influences; it preserves the ambo and ciborium of the 12th century (1150) of Nicodemus and Roberto masters, the iconostasis with plutei decorated with griffins, eagles and lions and a very rare wooden architrave, frescoes of the fifteenth century and the external apse rebuilt in polygonal form in the thirteenth century. Visit by telephone appointment according to the MiC card.

Ancient Messapian city of Salento with sections of the walls, the Castle with frescoes in 1692, the New Archaeological Museum in the former convent of the Friars Minor, the Crypt of the Crucifix and the Regional Natural Park Litorale of Ugento with its white sandy beaches.
Founded in 1753 on the site of a rural newsstand by the architect Silvestro Giugliara, it has an eighteenth-century Baroque façade.

Connected to the tower, it was built in 1279 on the remains of Roman buildings and testifies to the dominion of Acquaviva, dukes of Atri, from the mid-15th century. In a hall of the Town Hall are exhibited some archaeological finds of the territory, others are preserved at the Museo Pigorini of Rome and the Florentine Museum of Prehistory.
A ruin with a creepy name.
Opened in 2011 in the former Archbishop's seminary, Palazzo Muscetola: liturgical furnishings, the largest engraved topaz in the world and embroideries in fine linen.
The eighteenth-century castle became a municipality.
The church on the high ground watching the Serra.
From Bronze to the Renaissance in the Lower.
From the lake to the fort of the Cadorna Line.
At the historic headquarters of the Panizza plant, where felt hats were produced for almost a hundred years exported all over the world.

Example of Romanesque Lombard stone, built on the remains of a previous Lombard chapel; the characteristic leaning bell tower dates back to the 11th century. In the apse frescoes of the 15th century by the brothers Giovan Giacomo and Giovanni Andrea de Magistris. Reported in the FAI census      •The Places of the Heart • • .
Our Lady of the Vecellium and the wood of Brustolon.

The high city, more than 300 meters away, is closed in a medieval defensive structure dominated by the cathedral, between alleys, views and taverns; in a side street next to the Duomo a plaque reminds that there arose the first seminary of the world. Larino is also home to the Gentile di Larino olive oil.
The Molineri in the choir of the ancient abbey.
The peasant life of the Upper Valley.

Costa degli Dei center overlooking the Gulf of Lamezia and the Aeolian Islands, with a succession of bays, cliffs and beaches like Trainiti, Baia Safò, San Giuseppe and Sant'Irene; on the small port of the Rocchetta remains the ruin of one of the most photographed anti Saracen towers on the coast.

In the hamlet of the Pieve, 14th century Gothic church with ogival portal on two columns, central rose window, lateral cusp windows and gray stone arches; inside a table with oil by Camillo and Fabio Angelucci di Mevale.

Military architecture of the fourteenth century then rebuilt, between San Feliciano and Monte del Lago: an inscription of 1372 on the tower recalls the expansion of Cola Masci; passed to Baglioni and Pompilij. It has a gate in a sandstone walled with a fish in key, Palazzo Pula with portico and Renaissance loggia, the 14th century mast and remains of medieval houses.
Cobbled streets, medieval monuments and ancient houses in red trachyte; there stands the parish church of St. John the Baptist, whose patron saint is celebrated at the end of June.
The city theatre built in the nineteenth century.
Michelangelo's David, the Prisons and the Gipsoteca di Bartolini.
A baroque chest behind an austere façade.
One of the masterpieces of the European Romanesque.
The castle of the second half of the fourteenth century that dominates the village.
A former vote of the Great War in neo-Gothic style.
