In the historic centre, it preserves a processional case of Maragliano and a Nativity in polychrome ceramic tiles of about two meters high 1576.

Civic museum in the basement of the Palazzo di Città, at the Civic Library De Pace Lombardi, entitled to the architect Francesco Milizia: funeral supplies of the territory from the IV to the II century BC.
The relic of San Marco in Calabria.
The lava cliff overlooks the sea.
The toolhouse of the peasant world.
On the morainic hill at the entrance of the Valley of Susa, the unfinished Sabauda residence of Juvarra, which since 1984 houses the first museum of contemporary art in Italy.

The village rises on Monte Castro, surrounded by Nebrodi, overlooking the sea and the Aeolian Islands; the historic centre has twenty-two churches and preserves traces of Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Arabs and Normans. In Piazza Aluntina a monumental fountain in local red marble, still worked by artisan workshops.
The rock church that gives the name to the gravina of the center.
The fourteenth-century wooden ceiling of the Sala Magna, the graffiti of the prisoners and the famous painting "La Vucciria" by Renato Guttuso.
The watchtowers recall the border between Bologna and Ferrara.

Neoclassical villa of the late eighteenth-early nineteenth century about 1 km from Valconasso, purchased by the Rays in 1899 and renovated in 1914-15, when it received the façade in Venetian style with graffiti decorations and stables where Edilio Raggio bred the breed of thoroughbreds "Bellotta" (Bellotta); you arrive there from a avenue of lindens. Today it is the pastoral and holiday centre of the Diocese of Piacenza-Bobbio.
An architectural curiosity of the city.

The village of the Magredi, among the graves of Cellina and Meduna at the foot of the Friulan Dolomites: arid prairies with rare flora, the Antiquarium of Tesis, the mill on the roggia and the turnaria dairy.
Rafting and bike along the Walnut.
The Deposition of the Perugino.
Nineteenth-century theatre in neoclassical style.
Municipality of Val di Sangro in whose territory is located the archaeological area of Monte Pallano, fortified italic and Roman settlement with a porticoed hole and the Cyclopic Walls Paladine.
To understand the Brunello before you taste it.

The village preserves three doors of the fourteenth century (Porta Grande on Via Roma, flanked by a crenellated tower (merli added at the beginning of the twentieth century), Porta di Rosa at the Ponte Fontanella and Porta Palazzo incorporated in the Palazzo Marchesale) and remains of the walls towards Largo San Rocco. On top of the medieval center the Torre dei Provenzali, circular, of the fourteenth century, was jailed and from the early nineteenth century it is bell tower of the church of San Marco Evangelista, rebuilt in 1975 after the earthquake of 1962; front opens the viewpoint Mons. Michele Marinella.
The 19th century theatre in neoclassical style next to Porta Dojona.
According to tradition, Anselmo d'Aosta (1033-1109) was born here, abbot of Bec and archbishop of Canterbury.
The FAI Bay in front of the Faraglioni.

The smallest village of Casentino, mentioned already in 967 and lordship of the Ubertini until the eighteenth century, known from the Middle Ages for the sulphurous and ferruginous waters and for the smuggling of tobacco and gunpowder; to see the Castle of the Ubertini, the Ecomuseum of gunpowder and smuggling and the source Buca del Tesoro.
A beach with a castle on the rock.
Reperti dal Paleolithic al Medievalo, tra cui la Venus di Frasassi e oggetti di Piceni e Senoni, nel cinquecentesco Palazzo Ferretti, sede del museo dal 1958.
The most spectacular Baroque façade of Salento.
One of the oldest churches in Vercellese.
The island at the donkey's pass.
In April, the gallery of wisteria in bloom.
The art of Rogliano carvers.

Country of the Modena plain among the vineyards of Lambrusco di Sorbara, born as a transit place on the Naviglio di Modena: here in 1432 the octagonal basin of the Support was built and the mill extended to sixteen millstones; today the Museum of peasant civilization and the Baroque sanctuary of San Clemente.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione at the entrance of Valle Imagna, in the Park of Romanico (the ancient Lemine), known for the Romanesque roundabout of San Tomè; in the village the parish with works by Moroni and Vivarini, the Museum of carpenter Tino Sana and the nineteenth-century Fornace Parietti.

Rococo fillings and a painted organ.
Parish of the village, indicated as eighteenth century in the card of the municipality and as late doggy style in that of the itinerary; the feast is celebrated in mid-August.
The symbol of the papal port.

Finds of the plain and the pedemontana from the Bronze Age to the Roman and Middle Ages: bronze, ornaments, amulets, agricultural tools in iron, ceramics, cinerary and balsamary urns in glass, coins. It is part of the Lis Aganis Ecomuseum; times to ask the Cellina Meduna Archaeological Group.

Città del Tirreno cosentino with a medieval village perched under the castle, churches from the thirteenth to the fifteenth century, the Tower of Coreca on the sea and a promenade with nineteenth-century villas, beaches like Coreca and Tonnara and the Scogli di Isca for diving.

The walls, which began in the 14th century and strengthened as the Wall of Leo X against Turkish incursions, make the sanctuary a fortress with walks of the rounds, towers and guard bodies; the route offers views of the city and the sea.
The mountain life of the early twentieth century.

About 2,030 hectares of wild and rugged forest on the border with Tuscany, on a plateau of lava of the last phase of the volcano of Latera, with ancient eruptive cones, piles of lava called " " "murce" , craters of sinking and forre. Lecceta, mixed woods, beech trees at unusually low altitudes; traces from the Middle Paleolithic, necropolis, fortified villages, Roman roads and rural churches. It is crossed by the Trail of the Briganti and by about 50 km of white roads that can be used by car, as well as a network of paths.
Medieval frescoes with views.
A stop on the ancient Valeriana street.
A nuraghe inhabited by bats.

Nuraghe is a corridor of the Bronze Age, hidden in a grove of olive groves near a granite massif, with the remains of a village around. At 80 meters there is the Tomb Moru, born from the transformation of an allée couverte into the tomb of Giants. It is part of the Arzachena archaeological park, open every day 9-19.

A journey of about 45 km in four stages between Abbadia Lariana and Piantedo, on paths that In Lombardy attributed to the ancient Romans. In the first stage passes through San Giorgio and bypasses Mandello from above through Maggiana and Rongio, crosses the shady gorge of the river Meria, climbs to a viewpoint on the Olcio and descends between woods and olive trees towards Lierna; the villages are connected by the train, so you can shorten the route.
The medieval nucleus from which the village was born.

The entrance door to the village, the first stage of the official itinerary that from the Roman origins leads to the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.
The fountain of the 12th century fed by the fountain of the Fortress, which supplied the castle of Ripa and was for a long time the only fountain of the village.

It preserves, although modified over the centuries, a medieval structure with lean houses and narrow streets designed for defence; Piazza del Popolo was enlarged by demolishing the old Palazzo Gallo. Among the churches of San Rocco and, in the locality of the Reformation, the Madonna de Jesu next to the former Monks Convent.
A dip in the lake a few kilometers from Lecco.
Understand how sulfur was extracted and how to live in a mine.
The monumental tombs and the Red Tomb.

In the upper part of the village, on the remains of a Roman castrum and above the ancient walls: it belonged to the Farfenses and was the residence of the Lords of Loro; the fortified nucleus included the palace of the priors and the palace of justice, which since 1692 hosted the Monastery of Corpus Domini.
Archaeological site where traces of frescoes are still visible.

The ruins of the Rock of Arm.
A Roman city on the Appia.
Walk between the Alpe Valmeriana and Bellecombe with remains of millstones sketched in the rock similar to solar discs.
Romanesque and Gothic overlooking the Dora along the Francigena.
Founded in 1906 by Count Agostino Sieri Pepoli in the former Carmelite convent of the fourteenth century next to the Annunziata: Sicilian art, corals and Trapani goldsmiths.

Built in 1956-1957 to host the artists involved in the frescoes of Arcumeggia and home to the school of frescoes (summer courses since 1961), it preserves sketches, cardboards, tiles, sketches and ceramics that document the birth of the works; it has a large panoramic terrace on the valley and Lake Maggiore. Owned by the Province of Varese, it hosts exhibitions and guided tours.
The museum next to the Cavallino factories, with Formula 1, historic road cars and driving simulators.

Municipality of Val Pellice where the Ecomuseum Feltricio Crumiere, in Jervis square, tells the chain of felt with large intact machinery, some still functioning; the Waldensian temple of 1706, wanted by the Huguenot marquis Pierre de Belcastel, has a bell tower with unique pyramid in the Waldensian valleys.
The merchants' neighborhood.

Church deliberately stripped, consecrated in 1697 on the project of the friar Vitus Rastbichler; in the cloister the cycle of St. Francis, 31 large tables with 72 scenes painted by Lukas Platzer between 1706 and 1709. The main altarpiece of Christoph Unterberger, statues of Johann Pater and Andreas Fasching, was restored in 1992 and received the Europa Nostra Prize in 1994.

Borgo 37 km from Rome on the Via Francigena, with historic center that opens from the Porta Romana, the Fontana dei Delfini attributed to the Vignola, the Collegiate Church of San Giovanni Battista and Palazzo Venturi, home of the Archaeological Museum dedicated to the Roman mansio of Baccano sulla Cassia; outside the village the church of the Pietà and the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Sorbo.
Enter the Mandello eagle factory and see a century of Italian bikes.
In the former church of the SS. Crucifix collects the finds of the sanctuary of the Cuma: ceramics of various eras, architectural decorations and bronze objects dedicated to the gods.
A mountain village between medieval doors and stairs.
visits only by appointment or in extraordinary openings, via Infopoint Discover Parre (tel. 331 774 0890)

Built in the eighteenth century on the site of an ancient church of Roman times, of which remain the arch of the altar and a niche; the bell tower is from 1885. The interior is rich in decorations and furnishings and preserves an ancient cedar statue. Visitable during religious services.
Pieve in the homonymous hamlet, with a Romanesque plan with three naves with terracotta pillars and trusse roof, several times renovated.
The war on the Gustav Line seen from Pontecorvo.

Natural terrace at 1.998 meters above Vigo, reachable on foot or by cable car, starting point of excursions; in winter there are the facilities of the Skiarea Catinaccio and there is the Kinderpark Ciampedie Laurin, among the highest baby parks in the world.

Sanluri, in the Middle Campidano, is dominated by the medieval castle with four towers, the only Sardinian castle still habitable, today house-museum with the collection of waxes. It tells of an extraction present in the territory for more than two thousand years with thematic rooms on geology, extraction, liatura, transport, processing and historical memory, a litoteca of stones from all over the world, plastic, video and multimedia guide; closes the path the Botticino Visitor Center dedicated to marble, wine and stockings. Open on Sundays and holidays 15-18 (free entrance, by reservation according to the Municipality); closed on 1st January, Easter and Easter Mondays, 25 April, 2 June, 15 August, 8, 25, 26 and 31 December. He has been a candidate for the FAI Heart Places several times.

Inaugurated in 2007 on the ground floor of the town hall, it was born from donations collected since 2000, stimulated by the School of Embroidery of Pro Loco: objects of historical families of Foligno, Spello and Perugia and, later, Tuscan and Ligurian artifacts, including a collection arrived thanks to contacts with the Museo del Merletto di Rapallo. About 400 pieces between women's fashion of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, underwear and accessories, household linen with the "learned" ones, the samples on which the girls showed the techniques learned, and child clothing. Underground environments dug into the rock along the Natisone, on several levels, with niches, benches and two carved faces; preroman, perhaps Celtic, of uncertain function: tomb, prison or cistern.

Marsicano village at 1005 meters at the foot of Mount Lent, in the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise: here are the Visitor Centre of the Bear, the museum dedicated to the botanist Loreto Grande and, in Val Cervara, a beech wood included in the UNESCO site of the ancient primordial beech woods of Europe.

Ancient river centre on the flat and alluvial island that divides the Po into two branches, crossed in Roman times by Via Popilia: in San Basilio the Romanesque church and the archaeological museum renovated in 2023, between San Basilio and Grillara the fossil dunes of Sant'Ariano, in Grillara the workshop of the ocarines and, on the river, the village of Santa Maria in Punta.

On a small church of the fifth century dedicated to the Assumption, rebuilt in 1008 and enlarged between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, the basilica has the current layout since the last decades of the eighteenth century, with late Baroque façade by Giovanni Ruggeri and nave decorated with illusionistic frescoes by the Galliari brothers. It houses the Polyptych of San Martino, tempera on wood by the Treviglians Bernardino Butinone and Bernardo Zenale (1485-1490), with the center San Martino giving the mantle to the poor, presented in an exhibition space with multimedia path. The bell tower, 68 meters high, is among the highest in Lombardy.

Bersezio is the most populous town and seat of the town hall, with ancient houses with very steep roofs once covered with rye straw. The church of San Lorenzo is of medieval age and on the outside it has a Roman marble slab with the bas-relief of two warriors.

The underground complex of ancient stone quarries, which can be visited with the guides of the Pro Loco Alte Montecchio; in summer it opens on Sunday afternoon, at Christmas it becomes the real home of Santa Claus and on Halloween it hosts themed events.

Inaugurated in December 1989 after the excavation of the Roman mansio of Baccano sulla Cassia, it is located at Palazzo Venturi, seventeenth-century palace next to the Roman Gate, in the former stables of the pontifical carabinieri on horseback (1818). The route goes from the geology of the Sabatino district and of the lake of Baccano disappeared to the Etruscan furnishings of Quarticciolo and Vallelunga, to the mansio room with a sea mosaic with thermal baths, lamps, a bronze statue of Jupiter, coins up to Constantino (including a denarius of Marco Antonio) and panels on brigands, taverns and via Francigena.

On the square, Casa Licini, an eighteenth-century manor house on three floors where the painter was born on 22 March 1894 and lived with his Swedish wife Nanny; he died in 1958, the year of the Grand Prix of the Biennale.

Municipality to the south-west of Milan for more than half in the South Milan Agricultural Park, between fountains, farmsteads and lakes of quarry; in the agricultural village of Buccinasco Castello rises the Castle Visconteo, with traces fourteenth-century and loggia of the sixteenth century, and in Viale Lombardia the Foundation of the painter William Congdon.

Bronze statue created in 1965 by the sculptor Carmelo Mendola, inspired by ancient models, in the district of Schisò: it celebrates the bond with the Greek city of Calcide in Eubea.

The courtyard house of Campidano left to the Municipality by the last heir, stop of the itinerary Domus Guspini in the historic center: it tells in parallel the family of landowners of Ignazio Murgia, doctor, and Anniva Garau and the viticulture and olive growing of the community. One of the oldest parish churches in the Pisan territory, dating back to the VI-VII centuries, with news from 877; in stone, today only one nave because rebuilt after the violent earthquake of 1846 that hit the Pisan Hills. The original building remains the base of the bell tower, three capitals, some sculptures, a Robbian ceramic and a basin of the baptismal font.

Since 2012 in the former convent of the Hermits of St. Augustine, it collects sacred art from demolished churches and suppressed orders: works of Hercules Ramazzani, Domenico Peruzzini and two of Claudio Ridolfi, a Veronese painter who died in Corinaldo in 1644, eighteen Sicilian bust reliquaries of the early seventeenth century, a silver processional cross of 1615 and a section on the Prince's Tomb, a Piceno necropolis of the VII century BC, with a princely helmet. It is part of the Cultural Places card for sale at IAT.
A natural cave just a stone's throw from the centre.

Roman city founded at the bottom of the valley after the conquest, in 293 BC, of the Sannita Saipins; archaeological park established by the MiC in 2021. There are still more than 1 km long walls with towers, doors similar to triumphal arches such as Porta Bojano, the basilica, the forum and the theatre of the first century A.D. (up to 3,000 spectators), on which peasant houses arose that follow the curve; cardoon and decuman follow ancient ways of transhumance. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 9-18, Monday closed.

In the Palazzo Cigno-Constantino, probably built between the end of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries and already the residence of the princes of Trabia, exhibits finds of agriculture and handicrafts as a wooden press of the eighteenth century and a frame of the late eighteenth century, with the farmer's room and halls for exhibitions. Free admission.

Archpriest's church also called Santa Maria del Colle, which tradition connects to an ancient temple dedicated to Diana; a Roman inscription dedicated to the goddess is walled in the building. It preserves works of the seventeenth century, including sculptures by Orazio Marinali and 15 copper tiles by Francesco Maffei.

The castle of the XIII-XIV century remains ruined; on the summit the Loggetta Belvedere, Renaissance, once a covered market. From Piazza San Marco the panorama embraces the valley of the Esino to the sea.

The castle of Buttrio was destroyed in 1306 and rebuilt several times; in the seventeenth century the de Portis acquired the property and started the villa, then passed to Varmo, Morpurgo, Vidoni and Felluga, who restored it. The neoclassical dominical body with pentapartite façade flanks an older building with towers and the small church of Santi Gervasio and Protasio, between park and vineyards; today it is home, winery and restaurant.
Ladin art and panorama of the Monzoni.

In the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie, he documents the community's connection with the Wheat Festival, celebrated every July 26 in honour of Sant'Anna for over two hundred years: documents, paintings, photographs and videos on the history of the festival, the phases of cultivation from the grain to the spike and allegorical floats of past editions; he also carries out research and teaching activities for schools and groups. According to the MiC card is open from Tuesday to Sunday 8.30-19 with mandatory booking.
The quarry of the Romans.
The patron's sarcophagus.
The royal hunting castle.

Opened in 1990 for the re-introduction of the Apennine suede on Majella, with educational, scientific and conservation purposes: about five hectares divided into five fences with rocky walls, woods and clearings, and a veterinary center. You can see the chamois from close up; the guided tours are booked at the Visitor Center.

13th century tower in good condition, only rest of the abbey castle of the monastic complex of Pier, at the top of the hill above the village; inside, a cistern of about 30 cubic meters and holes for rain water. From the top the view stretches over Monte Leco, Monte Tobbio, the sanctuary of the Guardia di Gavi and the Castle of Sorli. Visible from outside, free parking in front of the tower.

Built in the 13th century on overhangs of pudding as a hospice of the monastery of Santa Maria di Banno along the salt road between Alto Monferrato and Liguria, it was expanded by Spinola between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Along the road the newsstands of a Via Crucis; the last Sunday of May there is held the New Festival. It is reached by a side road before the bridge over Piota, on the road between Tagliolo and Lerma.

It is the oldest church in Sorianello and houses a small museum run by the parish of Santa Maria e San Nicola, with oil paintings of the Neapolitan school of the eighteenth century and other works of the three churches of the village. The patron saint of St. Nicholas is celebrated on 6 December.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the small lake of the same name, among Romanesque churches, the monumental elm of the lakefront and the memory of granite.

In the crypt of the convent, founded in 1574, the mummies of local notables dressed in clothes of the early nineteenth century are exhibited in niches; mummification, with drying in the putridarium of the Mother Church, lasted sixty days and was practiced until 1876. The place fascinated Hercules Patti and Leonardo Sciascia.

Ancient seat of parish church, from 1070 it had a fortress of the bishop of Reggio, of which they remain ruined on an oliolithic outskirts next to the road; the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta, built in 1600, preserves a "Noli me tangere" of the Tiarini.
The Map of Bedolina, paper engraved in the rock.

Between the old town and the Esino, founded in the fifth century, it is the only abbey in the area that survived the Middle Ages; the neoclassical aspect with a single nave is the result of the eighteenth century restoration. The crypt preserves a sarcophagus, three tombs of the III-IV century and a fresco with the face of an angel of the X-XI century. Free entrance.

Museum, didactic and scientific center of the Park born from a geo-paleontological research started in 1984 on the fossiliferous deposits of the Alburni Mountains and the dorsal Vesole-Chianiello; Magliano was chosen for the presence of a site with fossil plants of the Cretaceous. It comprises four paleontological sections, a large hall with the reconstruction of a Paleoambiente of the Cretaceous, three workshops and two educational areas, with guided tours for schools and non-specialized public. The FAI reports a 30% discount for members.
The widest views of the Val Nure.

The Piazza Alta, an ancient plateau communis, was the center of the social and religious life of the village and is dominated by the Torrione del Podestà of the fifteenth century; in the village also the fifteenth-century house with dovecote, the Porta San Giacomo with Ghibellines merlons and two coats of arms of the fifteenth century and the viewpoint on the east side of the Sibillini.
Get on the roof of Terni province.

Fortress wanted by King Carlo Alberto, built from 1834 to 1847 with a break between 1837 and 1839: it develops for about 10 km on three levels (Front Superior, Front of Attack, Lower Front). In the Great War it became a prison for Austrian soldiers, then a warehouse; abandoned after 1950, it was restored by the City since the late 1980s. Today it hosts the multimedia route "Mountain in motion" with virtual reality and itineraries for families, guided tours between bastions and galleries; at the gates two large statues of the Scottish David Mach and at the feet an artificial lake with free access. Price of the free routes in 2024, free with Museums Subscription; seasonal opening.

Along the coast of the municipality alternate the sandy beach of Sciumara, Cala Trana, a small beach protected by dunes between granite rocks with sand tending to pink, and the coast of Porto Faro; Porto Rafael is a marina surrounded by olive trees, myrtle and lavender.

Piceno village among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with intact historical center closed by walls and six towers of the XV-XVI century; in the ancient Franciscan convent the museum polo of San Francesco houses the polyptych of Carlo Crivelli and the works of Adolfo De Carolis.

Country on the slopes of Mount Covello, founded according to the tradition by refugees of Toco and Caria fleeing from the Saracens (836) and devastated by the earthquake of 1783: the baroque fountain of 1663, the six-cinette Canaletta, the Ducal Palace of the Caracciolo, the Matrice Church, St. Rocco and the Addolorata, the former psychiatric hospital and the ruins of Pietra dei Monaci.

Small village on the hills of Oltrepò Pavese, among oak and chestnut woods, with stone houses, wooden fixtures and paved streets in porphyry; to see the seventeenth-century church of San Giorgio with the triptych of Pesina and, just below, the remains of the castle with the fifteenth-century tower.

Marble village Melandro surrounded by oak, beech and fir woods, known for the archeoparch of the Basileus with the tomb of a sovereign of the Peuketiantes; the historic center preserves noble palaces, small churches and the remains of the so-called castle.

Hosted in the former convent of San Francesco, dating back to the 14th century, it offers guided tastings with cold cuts, cheeses, cakes and bread and a selection of the best labels from Marche, including Offida DOCG.
Romanesque façade with Renaissance details and, below, a crypt with relics of San Bassiano.

Ring of about 2 and a half hours (change in altitude 358 m, medium difficulty, recommended from April to October) starting from Prazzo Superiore, signposted with illustrative panels. It crosses the ancient hemp fields, the hamlet Rabiera with the mill and the beater of hemp (the only remaining in the Maira Valley) and the maceration tanks, the hamlet Church with the house of weaving, the old town hall and sundials, the museum "La memorio di nosti soulà" in Chiotto and the Museo della canna in Prazzo Inferiore.

The valley is about 14 km long between Modica, Ispica and Rosolini, inhabited without interruption from the Bronze Age to the Early Middle Ages: Sicule necropolis with oven tombs, Byzantine hypogeans, Christian catacombs and caves; the visit starts from the Horse Mill.

One of the oldest Romanesque churches in the diocese, cited in a document of 945 and of Matilda foundation, with few ancient remains. It preserves a 13th century fresco with the Madonna and Child and a school table of the Garofalo.

The first giant bench of the Ossola valleys (b. 186), yellow on a green lawn, overlooking the peaks of the Valle Antigorio and the hamlet of Viceno; it is easily reached from the road to the hamlet Foppiano.

Open Saturday and Sunday (16-19 in summer, 15-18 in winter).

At the bridge that connected the castle to the inhabited, the new parish church of San Lorenzo was started in 1440 and ended in 1445, as the epigraph of the portal says, by the master Francesco Garone, with local masters similar to those of San Lorenzo di Genova; in 1676-1681 the Baroque reconstruction incorporated the Gothic columns into the pillars, but remain the portal, the rosette in terracotta, the gate On a column re-emerged in the restorations is painted Santa Caterina d'Alessandria with date 1459. The nearby Oratorio di Sant'Agostino was born from a fourteenth-century fortification, adapted to oratory at least from 1573, and preserves a late-fourth-century cycle of the Passion on all walls, now in rediscovery.
All about Botticino marble, a stone's throw from the quarries from which it comes.

The center preserves Palazzo Bozzuti-Pizzillo (16th century, of the noble Neapolitan family of the Bozzuti), the portal with balcony of Palazzo Caccese (second half of the 17th century), Palazzo De Cillis (XVIII century, portal in stone with floral motifs), Palazzo De Marco (XIX century, portals with stone coats of arms) and Palazzo Peluso, of which today interest the cellars extended under the whole area.

Borgo del Parco Regionale del Matese between Lake Letino and Lake Gallo, with the Grotta del Cauto where the river Lete falls and, at the top of the village, the Sanctuary of Santa Maria del Castello at 1,200 meters.

The Center visit to the north entrance of the Park, completely renovated and managed since 2008 by the association Montagna Grande onlus, illustrates the project "Men and Trees" , which links four species to guided paths in the Valley of Giovenco: the beech at the Valle della Fossa, the maple at the historic center, the apple to the orchards of the valley of the Prata, the pine to the nature path. You book excursions and rent mountain bikes and snowshoes. Opening hours from the Park card: in winter on Sundays 10-13 and 15-18; in summer, holidays and prefectures 10-13 and 15-19; every day from 20 July to 31 August and from 24 December to 6 January.

The parish church presented by the municipality as a Romanesque-Gothic parish church; according to the archival documents cited by the parish priest in a pastoral visit, around 1200 was officiated by a chapter of canons, and the first building dates back to the previous century. Subsequent pastoral visits record changes and adaptations; wheelchair accessible.

Church on a hill in Gothic-Aragonese style, with subsequent interventions, altars, wooden statues and paintings; the bell tower was rebuilt between 1868 and 1870. The museum of art of the parish collects altars and baptismal sources in marble, paintings, wooden and silver statues.

Theatre built between 1947 and 1949 by Antonio De Gioia on a former cellar near the station, with hotel and restaurant attached and 1,062 seats; the name comes from a operetta by Ralph Benatzky. Inaugurated on February 3, 1949 with the Rigoletto di Verdi, in 1980 he hosted the Living Theatre. Place: https://www.cavallinobiancogalatina.it, tel. +39 0836 633424.

Along the course you will find the Church of Abbadia, with a living stone façade on three orders and a sumptuous portal, the nineteenth-century Palazzo Mocciaro with frescoed rooms, one of which depicts the Gangi of the past, and, in the square of the same name, the sixteenth-century Church of São Paulo with a seventeenth-century portal with bas-reliefs.

Municipality of the Euganean Hills between Este and Monte Cero: on the top of Monte Gemola stands Villa Beatrice, of the Province of Padua, with exhibitions on Euganean flora and fauna, and on the hill above the village remain the ruins of the castle of the da Baone, sold in 1183 to Obizzo d'Este.

About 9 km of sandy beach protected by a pine forest planted at the beginning of the twentieth century, when the swampy coast was reclaimed, among Mediterranean maquis, vineyards and olive groves. From the beaches you can see the Aurunci Mountains, the Gulf of Gaeta and the islands of Ischia and Ponza.
Site with traces of human presence over 200,000 years ago: the triple burial, rock engravings and objects of prehistoric daily life.

Canyon covered with vegetation of about 600 hectares in the Cilento National Park: from the village a path along the stream, between springs, waterfalls and an ancient stone mill, descends to the cave where the Bussento re-emerges, with a portal about 20 meters high, a staircase dug in limestone and wooden walkways; it is geosite of the park. Visits by reservation, with seasonal times (last admission two hours before closing time).

One of the largest beaches in Baronia, a southern stretch of a coast of about four kilometers about three kilometers from the village: clear and fine sand, dunes, pine forest and behind the ponds Tondu and Longu and the mouth of the Posada river, with pink flamingos; in the background the castle and Montalbo. Windy, loved by surfers; from the parking lot a path with wooden bridge crosses the ponds.

It rises in Isola Pescaroli, a hamlet of San Daniele Po, along the margins of the Po; the church was designed by Rastelli with the engineer Filippini. It was born from the devotion of Don Martino Aletti for Our Lady of Trust: in 1951 a disastrous flood struck the neighbouring countries saving Isola Pescaroli, and the sanctuary, obtained from the remains of the previous church of San Biagio, was inaugurated in 1952. Archbishop Giovanni Cazzani proclaimed Our Lady Queen of the Po and Pius XII blessed her crowns on May 8, 1952. Each year around May 8th the festival includes mass, procession and the blessing of the waters by boat on the river. Without architectural barriers.

Coffered ceiling painted by G.B. Fagiani between 1750 and 1752 and, behind the altar, a table of Durante Nobili of 1554 with the Madonna enthroned with the Child and saints; cloister with frescoed lunettes and a chapel with the reproduction of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem.

He tells about the events of the university and the characters who made it great through the historical-scientific material, including the one sent to Florence in 1929 for the first national exhibition of history of science.

A height of 1,121 meters northwest of the village: on the south wall a castelluccian rock necropolis (2300-1700 BC) with ten small cells dug into the rock. The linear naturalistic path of about 1.3 km (average difficulty, ±100 m) has center visits, picnic areas, panoramic point, astronomical position and on the summit a giant bench, with views of the Etna and the Gulf of Augusta; the sky is classified as "gold" by Astronomicaly.
The walls surround the entire ancient village, climbing up to the castle, and is marked by 24 crenellated towers "alla ghibellina" (Ghibelline).
Forest area of about 8 hectares with hiking and biking trails and picnic areas.
Via Sisto V is the street of silver shops, religious objects, ceramics and fabrics; from the viewpoint of Piazzale Giovanni Paolo II the panorama opens onto the Musone Valley.

Built between 1954 and 1959 by the Italian-Venetian entrepreneur Filippo Gagliardi, in Gothic style; it incorporates the remains of the ancient church of Santa Sofia. Facade rich in statues and rosettes, two high bell towers (one with sundial, the other with clock), interior with three naves with lateral altars, frescoes and sculptures.

In the underground environments of the convent of San Marco, objects from the eighteenth century to the seventies of manual and animal work: carpenter's workshop, snowshoe, weaving room, mill with oil tools, cellars and a threshing machine from the early twentieth century.
Rare fortified mill active since 1320 in the valley of Aso, organized in three sections, sold in 1567 to Felice Peretti and sister Camilla; restored, hosts events and guided tours.

The civic museum of the valley in Sant'Antonio, with a reconstruction of the peasant life; in the village there is also a visitor center of the Park with virtual reality viewers. Visits during the opening hours or by reservation for guided tours.

18th century church built on the remains of a medieval church, of which remains the base of the bell tower; inside baroque decorations, a baptismal font in white marble, frescoes in the presbytery and a wooden door of 1700.

Civic museum inaugurated in 2000 in the former Gothic church of Saint Lucia, the Gothic Temple, built on a Roman cistern of imperial age then transformed into a Christian oratory: the first cult building of 1102, desecrated in 1669 for the construction of the Collegiate Church of San Barnaba, damaged by the bombings of 1944 and purchased by the Municipality in 1974. Exhibits of the territory: classical statuary, sepulchral cippes, sarcophagi, inscriptions, protohistoric depositions.

Longobard stronghold of the tenth century, passed to the Sanseverino, Ferrillo and Orsini of Gravina; it is remembered for the imprisonment and killing of Queen Joan I of Anjou. It collapsed with the earthquake of 1694, it was rebuilt and expanded.
Mother church of the historic center, with a bell tower that is the second highest in the area after that of the Cathedral of Lecce.
Towers of the coastal defensive chain against pirates, built in the Spanish era in the mid-500s.

Municipality of Alburni in the Cilento National Park: the abandoned village of Roscigno Vecchia, left between 1902 and 1908 for a landslide and remained like a country still in time, with the museum of peasant civilization and, above, the wine-lucano site of Monte Pruno.

The main square is closed to traffic; at the marina at dawn you buy fish directly from the fishermen.

Fortress in brick dating back to the 13th century between two branches of Lambro, probably on a Roman settlement: Queen of the Scala, wife of Bernabò Visconti, made it a summer residence and built the Mastra tower (36 meters) with bifores; in 1452 Francesco Sforza donated it to Michele Matteo Bolognini, from whom the name, and Giacomo Casanova there was guest in 1763. Restored at the beginning of the twentieth century by Count Gian Giacomo Morando Bolognini, it is managed by the Morando Bolognini Foundation (1933). In the 24 rooms of the Morando Bolognini Museum furniture from the 15th to the 17th century, weapons, paintings, sculptures, ceramics and a historical library; frescoed rooms and chapel with fifteenth-century tombstone.
