The Viareggio liberty seafront.
The valley-door of the Dolomites of Sesto.

Ruins of a small Romanesque church, dated between the end of the 10th and the half of the 11th century, rectory of the lost village of Livion cited in 1209: single nave of 4.62 x 3.80 m, three arches on two columns towards the presbytery, a bell tower almost to tibury over the presbytery and a fragment of fresco with a hand holding a book, perhaps a St. Peter. The name means "chiesona" (church), it is located isolated at the intersection of two country roads between the vineyards, along the Via Francigena.
The Three Peaks, symbol of the Dolomites.
Church of the sixteenth century overlooking Piazza dei Martiri, along the path dedicated to Dino Buzzati.
The Santa Spina and the August party.
Built in the 15th century and restored in 1770, on Piazza Duomo.
A short walk to the shrine of the wooden cross.

Arboreto with over 100 tree species typical of Val di Scalve, planted in the early 2000s, about 500 m from Vilminore on the road to Bueggio, near the Povo stream. It includes the Museum of Woods with 72 types of wood described, a multimedia classroom, a garden with the yellow potato of the valley, a picnic area and an area where coal is produced using the traditional method (poiat).
Duccio's Majesty and the view from the Façade.

Sanctuary of Hellenistic age (IV-III century BC) dedicated to Cibele, on the south side of the Colle Orbo: twelve large niches and reliefs carved into the rock, largely with the goddess seated on the throne, along with figures such as Hermes, Attis, Hecate, Dioscuri, Gauls and Coribanti. In 2021, the Superintendence started the race for its recovery.
Megalithic walls and views of the valley.
A shrine at the top with the Madonna dei Gagini.

The well, excavated from 1853 on sixteen levels up to more than 500 meters of depth, is dominated by a Neo-Gothic crenellated tower that hid the extraction structures; the coiled winch, electrified in 1919, carried men and minerals to the surface until closing in 1988. You can visit tower, winch and compressor rooms, workshops, forge, lighthouse, power plant, workers' accommodations with numbered rooms on the long corridor and storage with mineralized rock samples. Only guided tours (about 45 minutes, 90 for two routes), in Italian and English.
A church-fortress of the sixteenth century with a rock church under the floor.
The second polyptych of Casanova in the municipality.
Country church of the sixteenth century, back in operation since the end of the twentieth century.
€10 whole; €8 groups; €5 from 13 to 18 years old and students
A recently restored Medieval Universal Judgment.

Born from the deconsecrated church of Sant'Antonio, transformed into a theatre by the Municipality at the beginning of the nineteenth century; in 1817 a condominium of 28 members promoted by Giacomo Nobili started the construction and was probably inaugurated on 26 December 1819. It has an elliptical audience, unique and favorable for acoustics, baroque interiors and a Liberty ceiling frescoed by Sigismondo Martini; restored, it still hosts a theatrical season.

Inaugurated in 2007 and dedicated to the sculptor Carlo Conti, honorary inspector of the Superintendence, exhibits palaeontological and archaeological finds from the excavations begun in the 1930s in the caves of Monte Fenera: casts of bone remains of Neanderthal, the skeleton re-composed of a cave bear, the pleistocene fauna and the human presence from the Middle Paleolithic. Open on Saturday 15-18.
The ruins of the first inhabited.
The Roman history of Angera, including loaves.
A devotional ascent to one of the views of the valley.

The city of the two seas founded by the Spartans in 706 BC: the Old Town on the island with the cathedral of San Cataldo and the Doric Temple, the Aragonese Castle and the revolving bridge, the Umbertino Village with the Marta and the Ori of Taranto, the promenade on the Great Sea.
Three kilometers of beach and diving bottoms.

In the nineteenth century, the former civil hospital, together with the Treccani library: more than 400 paintings, sketches, letters, prints and drawings by the portrait artist Antonio Pasinetti (1863-1940), donated in 2006 by his nephew Laura. Free admission.
The country of the first Italian dinosaur.
The crucifix of the year 1000.
A nineteenth-century whim of shells and lava stone.

Museo diffuso founded in 2003 on the initiative of the Piedmont Region, dedicated to the dorsal of the Rocks, geological formation of about 250,000 years born from the change of course of the Tanaro and more than 30 km long, and to the eight historical villages arose after the Mille on the ridges. Paths through woods, vineyards and Rocche to walk or mountain bike, with geolocalized audio guides on legends and nature; map and audio guide to the site, free GPS tracks on the site. Office open from Tuesday to Saturday 9.30-12.30.
The story of Sulmona's confection.
The door of the Oriental Orobie.
A country church among the corks.
Picnic on the grass around a karst pond.

Late Baroque town rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693, UNESCO heritage with the towns of Val di Noto: the Duomo of San Giorgio on top of 250 steps, San Pietro, the rock church of San Nicolò Inferiore and, out of town, the valley of Cava d'Ispica.

Borgo delle Madonie on a rocky ridge at 917 meters, overlooking the mountains and the valley of Impera: the Mother Church with the triptych attributed to Rogier van der Weyden, the Town Hall in the former Jesuit College with the Civic Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Abies Nebrodensis, Santa Maria delle Grazie, the ruins of the Commenda and the Vallone Madonna degli Angeli with the last fir trees of the Madonie.
The patron's birthplace and the devotion of the country.

Common at the foot of the Ortles (3,905 m), in the Stelvio National Park, which includes Solda, Trafoi and Stelvio Pass, at 2,757 meters the highest road pass in Italy; in Solda the Messner Mountain Museum Ortles dedicated to ice and the Museum for the region of Ortles, in Trafoi the sanctuary of the Three Holy Fountains.
Designed in 1952 by Vittorio Montiglio Taglierini, an invalid architect of war and pupil of Marcello Piacentini, remembers the fallen of all wars.
The sea of Cosenza.
Oratory of the fifteenth century; according to tradition the place was chosen by a flock of sheep who stopped there.
The diamond-pointed façade.
The peasant memory of the Four Provinces.
The most beautiful view of Civita.
The largest natural basin in Abruzzo, shaped like a heart, for canoeing, windsurfing, bikes and excursions.
The sign of Florentine domination.

Villa Fontana (Villa Maria), purchased in 1892 by the publisher Emilio Treves and frequented by Verga, Gozzano, Boito and D'Annunzio, with an English garden, overlooking the lake; Villa Carlotta, nineteenth century, today hotel; Villa Bonghi (1858-1861) by Ruggero Bonghi; Villa Cairoli, which hosted Garibaldi; Villa Conelli with the Italian garden; Villa Dal Pozzo d'Annone, Villa Fontana-Fedeli known as the castle and residence of Princess Matilde, nephew of Napoleon. They are seen from the outside: the sources do not indicate them as visitable.
Michelangelo inside the spa.

Country of the Piana di Lucca on the ancient lake of Sesto, historical cross between Via Francigena and Via Cassia, mentioned as Castrum Porcari from 780; dominates the village the white church of San Giusto at the foot of the hill of Torretta, while in the plain there is the archaeological area of Fossa Nera with finds from the Bronze Age to the Roman era.

Born from the collection of J.M. Alberto Paronelli, a wholesaler and then a pipe designer who had been collecting since the 1940s and in 1984 founded the Académie Internationale de la Pipe in Gavirate, with a meeting room in the museum; run by the family for three generations. About 30,000 pieces in 9 rooms on two floors: terracotta pipes, plaster, ceramics, rootwood, boxwood, cork and sea foam, tobacconist, mouthpieces, lighters and a prehistoric chocolate of herbal heather petrified by Sardinia. From Monday to Friday only by reservation (tel. 340 744 4130).
A seaside village with the Norman cathedral, part of the Arab-Norman UNESCO itinerary; one of the most beautiful villages in Italy.

Fortified complex on a spur above the village, the medieval  "Castrum Costae" with about two thousand years of history from Roman finds to medieval walls; Antonio Maria Brandolini (died 1530) added the Venetian façade. Today it is a hotel with museum areas, reachable also by funicular; guided tours (1 hour or 1 hour and 15) touch the sections "CastelBrando in armi" and "Potere e giustizia" (Power and justice) and, in the path "B," the church of San Martino. Visits on Sundays, on other days by reservation.

Founded in 1989, on two floors and four rooms (welcome, frame, totem, costume): Albanian costumes, a photographic exhibition on the countries of Italy, iconography of Byzantine rites and a library of Albanian texts. Among the notable pieces is an icon of Our Lady Odigitria and notes of a storyteller on the history of Skanderbeg.
Inaugurated in October 2008 on the first floor of the Palazzo Comunale, it preserves traces of the Neolithic period found in the territory.

Octagonal temple in white travertine with a lead-coated dome, desired in 1828 by Pope Leo XII and designed by Giuseppe Valadier in a cave of the Throat of Frasassi; behind the hermitage, quoted in 1029, partly dug into the rock and once Benedictine cloistered monastery. It is reached with about 700 meters of paved path.

Once inhabited only by the shepherds, today it is a group of restored houses with stone walls and roofs in "ciappe" (the local stone slabs); the Park indicates it, with the alpine pastures of Pian del Latte, among the destinations around the village.
Near the station the remains of the first Roman settlement; not far from the Romanesque church of San Pietro, with the bell tower among cypresses.
Baroque church of the seventeenth century, recently restored, with interior paintings by Giovanni Battista Pozzo (1683-1685).

Properties of the Maggi since 1609, which in 1727 obtained from Pope Benedict XIII the private oratory in the hall then called "the columns" (the columns), in 1899 the landscape painter Giovanni Corvini bought it, who rebuilt a wing and decorated it with classical themes. Since 1975 it is part of the Municipality, restored in 1997-1999 and bound since 1973; the Salone delle colonne is intended for art gallery, with the park of the villa.
Very popular beach in a closed bay between two rocky promontories.
One of the most beautiful and intact villages of the Langhe del Barolo, dominated by the 14th century castle.

Rural shrine was built, according to legend, where around 1200 the Virgin appeared to a shepherd on a hornbeam: the wooden statue found did not allow itself to be brought into the church of the village, becoming too heavy. On May 8th, from the church of San Lorenzo comes the procession of the Virgins, girls in silk tunic and crown of flowers, ritual born after the drought of 1794.
Church where, according to sources, Emperor Arrigo VII died in 1313 with a date of 1103 engraved on the façade; inside a Madonna with the Child of Matthew of John and a Coronation of Saint Peter.
Rebuilt in the 18th century, with bell tower of the fifteenth century.
It once housed pilgrims; inside a Renaissance fresco of 1536. Today is the hall of the city council.
Museo-laboratorio dedicato al scultore offidano Aldo Sergiacomi, author of the Merlettaia Monument.

The village of Prelà 14 km from Imperia, with 42 inhabitants and 144 painted doors, number growing year after year: during the summer, during the festival in Valloria you are partying, three painters paint new doors live.

In the Franciscan monastery enlarged at the end of the seventeenth century, with the cloister frescoed in 1712 with stories of the Virgin; it tells the tradition of the capital of the ceramics of Abruzzo.
The Serenissima story.

Cultivated on the lava soils of Etna, introduced according to the tradition by the Arabs, it is still harvested entirely by hand, shaking the branches on curtains or dropping the fruits in containers carried on the shoulder; the green pruning is handed down from father to son. In October the Festival of the pistachio animates the center with stands and shows.
The palafittic villages of the Bronze Age of Tartaro, in three rooms.
The best view of the Ducal Palace.
Built towards the end of the fifteenth century in the ancient Giudecca, then enriched with baroque stuccoes, with Gothic portal, marble altar and bell tower of 1560; today it is used as auditorium.
Symbol of Crispiano, built at the end of the nineteenth century by the wealthy engineer Carlo Cacace as a family funeral mausoleum. From the top, the view extends over the ravines to the Ionian Sea.
Ancient little square still today home to furnaces and art studios, including Lucio Fontana.

Ruins of a medieval church of the X-XI centuries with a single nave with domes in axis and apse to the east, last phase of a settlement between the VI and the X-XI century, in an area with a vast necropolis; bound since 1975. It is reached from a small road on the provincial road 122 Rutigliano-Turi.
A farm-fortress of the eighteenth century.
The ancient cathedral of the village.

It is located in the former church of Santa Maria Maggiore in Santo Spirito, an eighteenth-century building wanted by the Congregation of the Noble Ones; it collects local heritage from the 16th to the 18th century, largely from the former convent of the Capuchins: paintings, silver sacred vestments, liturgical vestments and carved wooden works of the local masters, active especially in Rogliano and other areas of Calabria. It has a room for educational activities.

Benedictine church with three naves with semicircular apse and sailing bell tower, documented since 1021: it was a cell of Montecassino, grange of San Liberatore at Maiella and then of the Celestines. It is known for its shape, without the central roof, with the ruins restored; the thirteenth-century frescoes of Armanino da Modena, detached in the sixties, are at the National Museum of Eagle. Church is tratural along the paths of transhumance, it is a national monument since 1902. Outside the town, visible from the state; the MiC card does not record usable times.
A Campidano house that hosts exhibitions.

At the summit of Monte Ingino, 850 meters, reachable on foot or by cable car: it guards the urn with the remains of the patron and is the finish line of the Corsa dei Ceri on May 15th; enlarged in the sixteenth century with monastery and frescoed cloister, it has five naves and windows on the life of the saint.
seasonal openings: the Ecomuseum indicates July-August times from 2022 and booking through the Proloco
Paths in chalk above the caves.

The former Parco Regina Margherita, today Parco Mazzini, with the Luigi Zoja Thermal Baths built between 1967 and 1969 on a project by Franco Albini and Franca Helg, notable for its architecture as well as its thermal equipment.

It tells of the spring and autumn migration of birds, the role of the island and the historical relationship between islanders and migrants, with dioramas and models of birds of life size; about 1.5 km from the center. Admission fee, 10-12 and 18-20 hours.
The modern and contemporary art gallery in the Palazzo delle Muse, on the promenade.

Church of late early Christian origins, known for the crypt called Specus Martyrum, a catacomb with the remains of Christians killed during the persecutions; there are traditionally preserved the graves of Romulus and Bishop Sabino (VI century).
The "small Venice" of the Po Delta: canals, Trepponti, the valleys by boat, the eel and seven beaches on the Adriatic.
The ancient market square, of eighteenth-century plant and portico, in front of the castle.
The main façade is dominated by bell towers in Arab-Norman style crowned by two bulb domes; on the sides baroque buttresses mark the secondary entrances.
The house where Tiziano was born.
Walking paths overlooking the sea on one of the most beautiful promontories of the Adriatic.
Panoramas and nuraghi on the plateau.

In the church of Santa Maria del Gamio: sixteenth-century polyptych of unknown southern painter (remain side panels and predella) with the coats of arms of the Sanseverino; the throne and the monstrory of 1746 of the silversmith Salvatore Vecchio, a processional cross of the mid seventeenth century, the Madonna della Purità painted on metal plate, reliquary busts, canvases and vestments from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century. The sacristy depicts the legend of liberation from the Saracen siege.
The neo-Gothic temple.
On the ground floor of Mount Frumentario an ancient oven of end Renaissance still bakes bread with natural yeast as it used to be.

Reserve of about 10 km2 established in 1985 between Borriana, Cerrione, Mongrando and Zubiena: an artificial landscape of heaps of stones up to 10 meters high, residue of the auriferous exploitation conducted by the Romans between the II and the I century BC with the work of the Ictimuli, with washing channels, roads of the wagons and remains of huts; today colonized by oaks, cherry, birch and chestnuts, with owls and barbagianni. From the Vermogno tour centre, the easy routes start: Ciapei Parfundà (2,07 km, panels on geology, history and archaeology) and Rive del Ger (1,75 km); from Zubiena, also the rock engravings (3,8 km) and the "Mezza Bessa" (4,1 km, about 2 hours); from Vermogno, the parking lot for the bike routes. Spring is the best time.
In the district of Licese, at the foot of Mount Sant'Angelo, in the wood of Savignano of 12 hectares; its waters are known for its healing properties.
Baroque stone Lecce and a mosaic floor.
13th century building along Corso Garibaldi, with Gothic façade enriched with family coats of arms.
In the center of the village, built in 1300 with the offers of the population and decorated in the eighteenth century with shovels of the Turinese painter Rebaudengo; today it houses a library.
The ruins of a Pallavicino rock on the cliff.

Well preserved castle with a seven-sided tower and a stretch of underground passage; there are the church of San Fortunato (X century), with frescoes from the fourteenth century and paintings from the seventeenth century, and the remains of the convent of San Bartolomeo, where St. Francis stayed.
A legend to tell the children.
A medieval farmhouse in the countryside.
Sanctuary in the village of Soliera.
Panorama of the Tagliamento on the places of the Great War.
Courtyard houses and noble palaces in the squares of the village.
Romanesque Apulian near the castle.

Benedictine Abbey founded in 703 by three Beneventan princes in a rustic villa abandoned at the springs of the Volturno; supported by Charlemagne, it came to drive a network of more than 130 monasteries. The excavations have returned an archaeological park of 11,000 m2 with evidences of the monastic life and the Crypt of Epifanius, rich in frescoes, discovered by a farmer while working the camp; today the monastic house was reopened by a community of nuns from the United States.
Outside the country the life-size reconstructions of dinosaurs.
Decorated with the Venetian lion and with the coats of arms of ancient podestà, as evidence of the influence of Venice.
The noble palace today cultural center.
Golf among centuries-old olive trees a few kilometers from the sea.
The palace that closes the piazza del Duomo, historical seat of justice.

The Ministry of Culture defines Marzabotto as a unique case among the Etruscan cities: from the end of the sixth to the middle of the fourth century BC. Kainua occupied the Pian di Misano and the hill of Misanello, with roads, isolated, acropolis and necropolis still legible in the park. The museum next door preserves the excavations that began in the nineteenth century, including bronze kouros and votive bronze bronzes.
The view of the plateau, with 27 named peaks.
Behind the Town Hall, in Piazza Giroldi, the church has a terracotta bell tower considered the symbol of the village; inside a seventeenth-century painting of the battle of Lepanto.

Cala Rossano, in the basin of the new port, has clear sand mixed with pebbles and turquoise water between high cliffs, with umbrellas and sunbeds; Cala Nave looks at the faraglioni Earth Ship and Outside Ship. The coves to the south and west (Cala Battaglia, Parata Grande, Capo dell'Arco) are less accessible.
The country seen from the top of the cliff.

Born in Superga and since 2008 in the Villa Claretta Assandri, he is curated by volunteers of the Association Historical Memory Granata and tells the story of the Turin Football Club about 650 square meters: finds of the Philadelphia Stadium demolished, the trumpet of the "Trombettiere" that gave the charge to the Grande Torino, wheel and propeller of the plane fallen in Superga in 1949, the Fiat Balilla by Gigi Meroni, shirts, photos and documents. Only guided tours of about an hour and a half, with mandatory booking; open Saturday 14-19 and Sunday 10-19. Free under 10 years and with Museums or Torino+Piemonte Card.
The living room of the city, with many cafes.
To read the reliefs of the Arch.

Opened in 2006 in the home of Alcide De Gasperi, it is a multimedia path of vintage testimonies, sounds and images that goes from the Austro-Hungarian Trentino to the birth of the European Union. Open Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 14.30-18.
At Christmas the boats host the floating nativity scene.
The Gothic portal of 1425.
The submerged village.
The frescoes of Pietrafesa in his country.
Guided tours for a fee
Science and history of the territory of Lecca.
Where Gigli made his debut.

The village runs through steps, colorful facades and artisan workshops up to the recently renovated lakefront; the Salita Serbelloni was in the Middle Ages the Fossato, main defense of the village, and on the right you can still see the ancient walls. Along the way, the Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni, a private villa that became a hotel in 1873, and the neo-Gothic Villa Gotica, former Anglican church of the late nineteenth century.
Former parish church of the beginning of the fourteenth century, among the most important churches in Sardinia, in the passage from Romanesque to Gothic.
the stretch Jupiter-Saturno is interrupted to Baldissero Torinese for a yard, with alternative path indicated from the Municipality

Verdi bought the property in 1848, enlarged it following sketches and indications of his fist and lived there since 1851 with Giuseppina Strepponi. The museum path, in one part of the building, includes the original rooms, the bedroom-study, the pianos used by the Master, portraits, autographs, the music library and the reconstruction of the room of the Grand Hotel in Milan where he died on January 27, 1901. Around, the English park designed by Verdi, with pond, rare plants, sculptures by Giuseppe Torretti and the burials of his dogs. In December 2024 the MiC signed the decree of expropriation that acquires it to the State, with urgent interventions of restoration.
The fountain in the center of Piazza Testaccio with the amphorae symbol of the district.

Small medieval village of alleys around a central square, with stretches of the ancient walls of the castle and wide views of woods, olive groves and valley of the Albegna. It was of the Aldobrandeschi, then of Siena and the Medici; in the square the Medici cistern of the seventeenth century collected rainwater with a system of pipes, and in the village rise the churches of San Martino and Madonna del Conforto. Every year medieval festival and, in autumn, Bindina festival with roasted chestnuts.

Set up in the restored farmhouse of the Environmental Education Centre Oasi La Valle, open in 2013 for schools and visitors: exhibits agricultural tools of local farmers and a late nineteenth century frame for linen sheets.
The Roman necropolis discovered by high-speed construction sites.

Roman house of the I-II century A.D. excavated between 1979 and 1984: atrium with impluvium in marble, rooms and two shops with dolia, mosaic floors and frescoed walls in fourth style, a stretch of the lower decuman with an inscribed altar and a dozen late Christian burials in the garden.
Spain in a fraction.
On Mount Armidda, near the park of Selene, it is described as one of the largest public observers in Italy.
The medieval village.
An example of a farmhouse in Val d'Agri.

In the historic house Sias, on three floors, tells the school of Atzara, born when in the early twentieth century Eduardo Chicharro, Antonio Ortiz Echagüe and Bernardo de Quirós, attracted by the costumes of the village, stayed there, followed by Ballero, Ciusa, Figari, Biasi and Delitala. About one hundred works from the late nineteenth century to the early thirteenth century, including the Mujores de Mamojada of Ortiz and the evening appeal of Ballero, a photographic section on the village and a room for temporary exhibitions; wheelchair accessible.

Country on the southern shore of the ancient lake of Fucino, with the Basilica of Saints Cesidio and Rufino, the Febonio Tower which was the lighthouse for the fishermen of the lake and the sanctuary of the Madonna of Candelecchia.
Monfalcone seaside resort suitable for kitesurfing, kayaking, SUP and windsurfing.
A Madonna di Lorenzetti 15 km from Florence.
Outside only if closed.
A tiny village with a lot of spirit.
Archaeological exhibition with finds of the Bronze Age and Romans and Renaissance ceramics, transferred from the Rocca to via Mazzini 15.
The most famous Gothic façade of Molise.

Borgo dei Monti Dauni perched on a hill, a few kilometers from Bovino and Sant'Agata di Puglia, dominated by the Norman-Svevo Castle, a national monument since 1902. Between alleys and courtyards of the center, the convent of Sant'Antonio and the chapel of the Greek Rite; around oak woods such as the Bosco Macchione.
Church of the eighteenth century with Greek cross, with wooden dome, eighteenth-century organ and wooden pulpit.
A great post-war theatre with a lively history.
Snorkeling between red cliffs.
Streets tree-lined a stone's throw from the center.
Walk on the Francigena between the two doors.
At the center of the municipal territory.
Neanderthal tracks in the trulli campaign.
The MiC tab indicates   ... Closed every day; check the opening (tel. 0171 986370)

Country of about 4,000 inhabitants in the valley of Cixerri, mentioned for the first time in 1272, dominated by the castle of Acquafredda, the fortress of Count Ugolino della Gherardesca remembered by Dante, on the Andesitic dome declared natural monument in 1993; in the territory also the WWF oasis of Monte Arcosu.
The spa with historical swimming pools like the fifteenth century Bagno dei Frati.
The three monumental gates of access to the city; in the donation of the Cividale Porta is located part of the military historical museum.

In Governolo you can visit the Chiusa and the Conca di navigazione, designed between the end of the XIV and the beginning of the XVII century, adapted over the centuries and partially renewed in 1886-87: they are considered among the greatest testimonies of hydraulic archaeology of the Po Valley. The Rijeka Museum, inaugurated on October 19, 2013 by Roncoferraro and Bagnolo San Vito with Lombardy Region, tells with panels, videos, models and objects the story of the Bass Mincio, the lakes of Mantua and the engineers and machines that regulated the water; the classrooms propose hydraulic experiments. Open all year round by reservation and according to the calendar of events.

You enter the medieval village surrounded by walls from Porta Ascolana up to the square with the Civic Tower and Palazzo Giustiniani; on the edge of the center a panoramic terrace on the hills and the Sibillini Mountains. In the village the churches of the SS. Sacramento e Rosario (mid 18th century), Saints Leonardo and Flaviano, Saint Mary of the Snow and Saint Anne.

Borgo on a hill on the left of the Tavo river, crossed by via del Baio that joins the Chiola Castle to the abbey church of San Pietro, with doors four-fifth-century and the Fonte Grande of 1838. Outside the center, the church of Santa Maria in Piano preserves a Judgment of the late 1920s, one of the most important paintings in Abruzzo.
Church of the seventeenth century with a walled cross of the fifteenth century on a gold background, the Complaint on Christ died by Giuseppe Velasco and two baroque altars by Giuseppe Serpotta.
Forty thousand finds of the city that begat Venice.

The smallest village of Ogliastra, about 500 meters above sea level, can be reached by train: the old 19th century granite station, the parish church of San Gavino, the museum house and, at the top, the Carmine Park with the 17th century sanctuary and the ruins of two nuraghi.
Founded in 1495 by Giuliano da Sangallo and completed by Vasari, with a dome of 59 meters.
The town rebuilt in the 1920s and 1930s, today studied as an example of the city of foundation of the twentieth century.

The oldest public museums in the world, born in 1471 from the donation of Sisto IV bronzes: the original Marco Aurelio, the Wolf, the dying Galata, the Capitolina Venus; from the Terrazza Caffarelli one of the most beautiful views.

Mount of about 1,062 meters above Laveno, reachable in about 15 minutes by cable car with two cabins from the center to Poggio Sant'Elsa, or by car to Casere (via Cittiglio) and then walk in the woods. From the top you can see the lake, the Campo dei Fiori, the lakes of the province, the Val Grande and the Alps up to Monte Rosa; it is also a takeoff point for hang gliding and paragliding. On arrival bar, restaurant, hotel and shop of local products.

Rebuilt in late Baroque style in the mid-18th century on a fifteenth-century building, it has a facade with eight niches with statues and an eighteenth-century portal in stone of Sarnico. Inside the frescoes of the eighties of the eighteenth century by Ludovico Gallina, the main Baroque wooden altar by Andrea Fantoni, the altarpiece of the Madonna del Rosario by Giacomo Ceruti called the Pitocchetto (coming from the church of Santa Maria) and paintings by Gaspare Diziani in the presbytery, including an Adoration of the Magi.

Inaugurated on 27 May 2023 in the outdoor area of the cultural center Cascina Grande, realized with the Astrofili Group Rozzano, active in the city for over 40 years. The dome, almost 7 meters in diameter with petal opening, offers a 360 degree view; according to the Municipality it is the largest of its kind in Europe and the second in the world.
Garden-museum with over 50 twentieth-century ceramic works, including the great Crocodile by Lucio Fontana of 1936.
The shrine of pilgrimage of the transaccans.
The castle of the Abbots of San Michele above the village, reported by Turismo Torino.
Built during the Spanish domination to defend the city from raids, it was the Navy's anti-air station in the Second World War.
The 17th century wooden statue.

Two cities in one on the Riviera dei Fiori: Oneglia, with Calata Cuneo, the porticoes of Piazza Dante, the Museo dell'Olivo and Villa Grock, and Porto Maurizio, with Parasio, the great Cathedral of San Maurizio, the Loggia of Santa Chiara and the Naval Museum on the sea.
Get on a crater and get wet between the fumaroles.

On 24 August 1291 Mainardo II of Tyrol opened the market of San Bartolomeo: under the porticos of Laubengasse there were trade of Inntal salt, Valtellina wine, sheep and wheat, today shops and coffee. Around the square, with two large chestnut trees and a fountain, and in the nearby streets: Frölich house (1570) with coats of arms and allegory of the seven deadly sins, the hotel Corona wanted in 1562 by the knight Reinprecht von Hendl, the town hall of 1573-1591 (Hendlspurg residence from 1604), the ancient court of about 1510 and the tower Flurin, prison from 1825 to 1931. The church of the Hospital, dedicated to the Virgin, was rebuilt in 1665-1669 after the fire of 1664.

The 18th-century Baroque Collegiate Church, built in the place of the ancient Romanesque Cathedral (1150-1200): Alexander was probably bishop's seat from the Norman era until 1818. The nineteenth-century façade has remained unfinished; inside a painting of the Caravaggio school, Tobiolo and the Angel.
The village waterfall.
In the single ticket with Palazzo Pretorio (€5 full)
Built in the 9th century by Pope Pasquale I in the Esquilino district and restored several times over the centuries.
The city painted between doors, walls and frescoed buildings.
A Barnabas from Modena in a village church.
The 12th century castle that dominates the village, contested between Lucca, Pisa and Florence: from here Castruccio Castracani led the troops to the victory of Altopascio in 1325.
Two poets in a garden.
The world of the Messapians told by their kit.

House of the thirteenth century that preserves much of the fourteenth-century structure, with sixteenth-century loggia (1546); the rooms were frescoed in the sixteenth century with scenes inspired by Canzoniere and Africa. Petrarca moved there in 1369-70 and died in July 1374: you can see the study, the library, the chair and the mummified cat, with a permanent exhibition on the life and work of the poet.

Born as an oasis of protection of fauna in 1968 (ENEL, Municipality and WWF), Ramsar area since 1977 and established in 1979 as the first regional natural reserve of Italy, it covers about 800 hectares between the provinces of Rome and Rieti. The lake of Nazzano, about 300 hectares deep 20-100 cm, formed between 1953 and 1955 after the barrier ENEL on the Tiber downstream of the confluence with the Farfa: reeds, willows and poplars host pilgrims, brown nibbi, herons ashes, folk and pigs, and the site is among the most interesting in central Italy for birdwatching. Paths such as La Fornace (1.5 km on wooden walkways) and the Meana riparian ring (1 km, with observation tower); areas equipped for stopping.

From the hills of Aspromonte to the Strait: above the village the Castle of Santo Niceto, byzantine fortress of the 11th century shaped as a ship; on the coast, in Lazarus, the white cliff of Leucopetra with the lighthouse of Capo d'Armi, the remains of the villa where Cicero and the Antiquarium with the Jewish skylight with the menorah.
It matches the Francigena ride.

A family workshop with a tradition dating back to the 16th century and over 300 exclusive designs handed down from generation to generation: silk damasks, lampshades, voiles, shantungs, satin and linen, and recently cashmere and silk cashmere; Giuseppe De Martini has built and patented a frame that reproduces the fabrics once handmade. Open Monday to Saturday 9-18 (tel. 0185 977302).
Emilia Romagna Tourism indicates it temporarily closed for restoration
Stars under the dome.
materials available only for scholars waiting for the new setup
Verona along its river.

The centre of the Lomellina is located around the Castello Sangiuliani, of which there are traces of 14th-XV century walls, a loggia and a crenellated tower; the castle houses the civic museums, with the works of the futurist sculptor Regina Cassolo and the archaeological and naturalistic collection Ugo Fantelli.
In the hamlet of Santa Croce, the house of the artist Pietro Ghizzardi, which preserves the largest collection of his paintings, sculptures, graphic works and manuscripts.
The Baroque welcome to Collecchio.
On the town hall square, the church built between 1887 and 1893, probably on the remains of the parish church of Santa Maria of the 11th century; it is advisable to check the opening hours.

Historic pilgrimage site at 2,045 meters below the Sas dla Crusc: perhaps an ancient pagan place of worship, in 1010 there arose a chapel and in the fifteenth century a small church; desecrated by the emperor at the end of the seventeenth century and left in ruins, it was rebuilt by pilgrims and valleys and in the mid eighteenth century enlarged and equipped with bell tower. Documents of 1511 attest to the pilgrimage; the altar preserves relics of saints including Leonardo, Ippolito and Virgilio. In the summer processions go up there, with an important function on the first Sunday of June. It can be reached with the lift from Badia.

Church of the Most Holy Name of Mary on a height between Lucedio and Montarolo: the abbot of Lucedio Vincenzo Grimani had the octagonal part enlarged, designed by Antonio Bertola and then by Giovanni Battista Scapitta, and was blessed in the new form on July 21, 1713. Several times reported to the FAI census
18th century portal and walnut altar finished by Ferdinando Moscow in 1716.
Romanesque church of 1110, the oldest in the country and among the oldest in the diocese, with a fresco of the fourteenth century; it was probably founded on the remains of an ancient necropolis.

Under the monastery of San Domenico, the underground path of aqueducts, cisterns, tunnels and crypts with the torture hall of the Court of the Inquisition; the excavation dates back to the Etruscan era.
Founded in 726, one of the lighthouses of culture in the Carolingian age, with abbey church, monastic building, four frescoed chapels and a park; over 15,000 visitors a year.
The frescoes of De Magistris in the town hall.
The works of Canciani and exhibitions on the territory.
A historic theatre still on stage.

An eighteenth-century villa built on the remains of the medieval castle of Della Gherardesca, later belonged to the Pucci and the Marquises Baciocchi, who gave it its name. On the ground floor the Zoological Museum exhibits over 1,400 specimens of mammals, birds, reptiles and invertebrates in natural settings; on the noble floor the Archaeological Museum tells the Valdera from prehistory to the Middle Ages, with ceramics, coins, stone finds, Etruscan and Roman sections and reconstructions of houses, including a Neolithic village and Etruscan houses. Open from Thursday to Sunday, 9.30-12.30 and 15.30-18.30 in winter, 9.30-12.30 and 16-19 in summer; visit to the underground €3, free under 6 years.
Divided and relics of aviators.
The big fir forest.
By bike or on foot along the stream.
Another layer of the city's history.

Comune dell'hinterland milanese noto per Villa Visconti Borromeo Litta, villa of delights designed around 1585 by Count Pirro I Visconti Borromeo, with the Nymphaeum (Palazzo delle Acque) whose water games still work as originally and a historical park of about three hectares.
The cathedral of the towers.
From the stairs you will dominate the padule of Fucecchio.
One of the most important fairs in Romagna for centuries, in March: exhibitions of animals, agricultural machinery, handicrafts, temporary taverns and amusement park.
Medieval village between the Arno and Monte Pisano, fortified by Filippo Brunelleschi.
The museum dedicated to the Roman centuriation, the regular division of the fields that still draws the plain around Cesena.
The door of the Serenissima that lost its lion at the hands of Napoleon.
Ludovico Lana outside the museum.
Village of Versilia at the foot of the Apuan Islands, with the Medici Palace UNESCO World Heritage among Medici villas.
Founded in the second half of the 10th century and rebuilt in the 18th century by the architect Domenico Cerato; the bell tower dates back to 1314.
From the 10th century, north of the church, home to Rodolfo di Valpelline then bishop of Sion, with court, stable and barn of the lord.
One of the oratories built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, with a magnificent Baroque bell tower.

Fountain in stone, octagonal outside and circular inside, with a tub; bears the inscription of the mayor Carlo Pacino and the date 1663, while the upper part is dated 1830. Legend has it that it appears in a single day: it was actually mounted in a few hours by the local stonemasons, who had prepared the modules in the cave of the stonemasons near the Stone of the Monks. Unknown author.

It is located in the eighteenth century Palazzo Lercari, commissioned by Cardinal Nicolò Maria Lercari, where Franz Liszt stayed in the summer at the time of Pius IX. Booking recommended one day in advance.
A hike to the alpine pasture.
For the kids.
The museum that tells the local history lived during the Second World War and the Allied landing, with multimedia settings.
The facade of 1231 and Byzantine sculptures.
Our Lady with the country in hand.
X century castle in Val Freddana, strategic observation point on the Via Francigena, together residence and defensive structure.
Next to the Roman amphitheatre, with a 12th century Romanesque portal carved in relief and a later Gothic portal.

The mountain village of Cittiglio is about 750 meters away from the plains by a valley, with wide views of Lake Maggiore and Lake Varese; in the valley of Vararo (757 m) passes the road of Cuvignon. From here you walk towards the Pizzoni di Laveno and at sunset in the meadows it is easy to spot wild animals.

The village, with its fan-shaped houses on the sea outlet of the valley of Mount Caitas around the parish church of San Giovanni Battista, preserves the remains of wells, machinery, villages and palaces of the direction; in the village the sculptures of Pinuccio Sciola dedicated to the fallen miners.
Glacial lakes between the peaks of Frignano.

Golfo di Squillace on the Ionian side of the Serre, with the historic center on the hill rich in noble palaces six-seventh-century and, on the coast, the seaside resort of Pietragrande, which takes its name from the large rock near the shore, 13 meters high and loved by those who dive.

Country of the Vigezzo Valley distributed on three plains of the Costa di Faedo, with the hamlets of Gagliago, Vallaro and Londongo: it is known for its forty sundials scattered among the houses, and preserves the remains of the castle of Ferrari, the parish church of San Bartolomeo frescoed, the oratory of San Rocco and the peasant museum "La Ca di Feman da la Piaza" .

Small museum of sacred art in the former oratory of the Society of the Name of Jesus, leaning on the left aisle of the parish. It keeps busts in glazed terracotta by Benedetto Buglioni (San Giovannino, Santo Stefano and probably San Romolo) and an angel polychrome regiment, a thirteenth-century processional cross in chiselled and gilded copper with Christ in golden bronze, a plate in copper painted with Nativity of the sixteenth century perhaps of workshop of Limoges, the Circumcision attributed to Benedetto Veli and eighteenth-century furnishings with figures of nativity scenes of Neapolitan taste.
The largest plane tree in Italy, over six centuries old.

Roman ass-back bridge on the river Titerno, 13 m long and about 1.50 m wide, with a light of 9.15 m; tradition ties him to the passage of Hannibal in the Second Punic War. It is reached by a path north of the village, near the road to Cusano Mutri.

Over 65 km of dirt roads and marked paths on the Valdera hills, organized in rings with departure and arrival in the same spot, to walk, by bike or on horseback; touch the villages of Alica, San Gervasio and Colleoli. The best known is the Great Nature Path; the tracks are on the profile Wikiloc    .
The most typical castle of the territory.
The holed rock of the Tuttavista.
The great Neolithic village of Sammardenchia.
The symbol of the 11-metre-high Antique Appia with the Castrum Caetani and the medieval church of St. Nicholas.
The place of Chiara.
Two hours on foot between reeds and herons in the south lagoon.
The church of the patroness and her bronze portal.
The Marmilla of knights and noble families.

These are the typical rural houses of Poggiomarino: cubic plant, often only one room and dome roof, built in compact and waterproof Vesuvius stone. The dome caused the water or lapilli to flow in case of eruption and also served to dry the products of the countryside; the walls, solid and rough on the outside, look like bulwarks of rock.

Municipality of the eastern Friulian plain where Villa de Brandis, built between 1718 and 1724 and left to the Municipality in 1984 by the last Countess Caterina de Brandis, houses a painting from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century and an English park open to the public.
Fortified complex in Castiglione della Valle; inside the 12th century church of Saints Paul and Ubaldo with frescoes by Meo da Siena.
The history of the partisan republic in the place where it was born.
The old town, perched on the hill, preserves the long row of terraced houses where the blacksmiths lived when the main activity of the area was the processing of steel and iron.

Built between the 10th and 11th centuries and restored in 1964 (facade and bell tower), it has six chapels, three of them baroque, with decorations attributed to the Zuccari. It preserves a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century, an icon of the sixteenth century Madonna Refugium Peccatorum and canvases of Bartolomeo Poliziano (Sant'Antonio and Santa Lucia) and Ricci da Urbino (Madonna del Rosario).
The medieval abbey on the Way of Saint Benedict.

In the center there are churches of the Longobard Age: San Giovanni a Corte of the IX century, San Salvatore a Corte founded in 960 by the Countess Adelgrima with bell tower of the early thirteenth century, San Michele a Corte of the IX-X century with Byzantine elements.
It preserves a painting of the Wedding of Cana dated 1600.

San Donà is housed in the MUB - Museum of Reclamation, one of the Sandonese Civic Museums together with the Galleria Civica d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea and the Space Exhibitions. Battistella is the history of the relationship between man and the environment in the eastern Veneto, from the peasant life before the Bonifiche to the Great War; the parish church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, destroyed in 1918, was rebuilt between 1919 and 1923.
One of the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2004, with the church of Sant'Erasmo, the Clock Tower reminiscent of Caravaggio, who died here in 1610, and the forts Filippo, Stella and the Rocca.

Waterfall of the river Campanaro about 20 meters high, in a forest of the Sila National Park along the road between Sersale and Zagarise. From the road edge, with few parking spaces, a marked path of a few hundred meters descends for about 70 meters of difference in altitude, with a small parking area; it is not accessible to the disabled and we recommend trekking shoes.
A small isolated village, a hamlet on the edge of the world, with natural balconies dominated by a wide landscape.
The walls seen from inside.
Made from a medieval castle.

Inaugurated in 2011, it collects sacred and profane painting of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries from churches and suppressed convents of the village, including a San Nicola da Tolentino that intercedes for the souls of Purgatory; the archaeological collection of piceno finds of municipal property is in the nearby church of San Marco, renovated in the eighteenth century.
Built in 1597 by Camilla Peretti in memory of his brother Felice Peretti, Pope Sixtus V, next to the pontiff's birthplace; he conserves an organ by Francesco Fedeli of 1752.
Theatre of 1852 with neoclassical façade by Giuseppe Aimi, interior decoration completed in 1898; still in operation.

Documents on the political and cultural history of the country, relics of the composer Amilcare Zanella and other illustrious mountains, paintings of local contemporary artists and a showcase dedicated to music; during the fairs it hosts temporary exhibitions. Open on Sunday 15.30-17.30.
Reservation required: tel. 095 662060 (URP Common), prolocoraddusa@gmail.com
14th century frescoes.
Cumulation €25 with Spezieria di San Giovanni, Castello di Torrechiara and archaeological area of Veleia
The Holy Door of wheat and the floats of the feast.
The fortress built by the Aldobrandeschi and then by the Orsini, home to the Museum of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.

The sacred mountain dedicated to Maja, on whose slopes Bomba rises, is divided between the municipalities of Bomba and Tornareccio. The well-marked trails run on foot or by mountain bike and open views of the Sangro Valley, the Adriatic and Majella. On the mountain a Hellenistic-Roman settlement is documented by the researches of 1984-1993; the megalithic walls of the 5th century BC, of rocks framed without mortar, fall in the part of Tornareccio.
Open area in limited days and hours
In the hamlet of Dégioz, dedicated to the predatory animals of the park and in particular to the lynx.

In the former convent of San Francesco, contemporary art and the link of artists with marble: works of the International Biennale of Sculpture since 1957, donations and works of the project         Â Design the marble in the cloister.
A palace of delights of the Norman kings.
A village on the medieval road to Valais, with views of the Valpelline mountains and the Grand Combin.
The riverfront with flower beds and vineyards leads to Castel Mareccio and Castel Roncolo, from which a forest road climbs to the panoramic walk of Sant'Osvaldo.

Built between 1260 and 1276 in the defensive system of the Scaligeri to control the valley towards Garda, it is a castle fenced with an elongated and polygonal plan with five towers, two of which real buildings closed; lost military function in the eighteenth century. Access from a single staircase, not suitable for wheelchairs and strollers; audioguide in Italian, English and German.
Visitable only by groups and schools by reservation, during guided tours of the museum
The town of Peligna at the origin of the village.
The Lombard heart of the city.

Borgo on a spur of tufa of the Prenestini Mountains, home of Pope Martin V, with the Colonna Castle, the Nymph of Bramante and the sanctuary of the Mother of Good Council; on the first Sunday of July the center is covered with the Inflorata of the Sacred Heart.
MiC card indicates the site temporarily closed for PNRR work
Casa-torre dei Panciatichi passed to the Medici in 1583 and renovated by Buontalenti, base for hunting in the Royal Barco; Italian garden, lemon and romantic park; in the halls the Museo del Filet.

The saffron, DOP since 2005, grows around Navelli and was the heart of the economy of the village; the flowering attracts visitors every year and the harvest, in October, is done at dawn with flowers picked and handmade.
The spacious cloister with four doors and garden, remains of walls, votive cippi and finds of the museums of the Canonica.
Palazzo di fine Quattrocento, today the town hall, with the tombstone of the first Festa degli Alberi in Italy (1899) and the tower of 1724.
The seventeenth-century complex on the Panaro, formerly a Montecuccoli country residence, with a large dovecote tower.
A Romanesque pearl.
Fountain in cast iron of the village, made with the iron of the local mines, operating for over two centuries.

Large karst chasm born from the collapse of a cave, about 60 m deep and about 300 m broad, about 1 km from the village on the slopes of the mountains La Monna and Rotonaria; on the bottom grows a vegetation with trees up to 20 m tall. In the past, sheep with ropes for seasonal grazing were dropped.
The Benedictine church with the dome of the Vision of St. John in Patmos del Correggio; in the monastery you can visit cloisters, library and refectory.
Walk in the green on the hill of Doss Trento up to the mausoleum dedicated to Cesare Battisti, with views over the whole city.

Cittadina del Novarese with one of the most important Romanesque churches in northern Italy, San Michele, frescoed around 1060; in the center there is the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul with the Museum of Religious Art, the Ethnographic and Archaeological Museum Fanchini and the neoclassical Palazzo Bellini.
The two monumental gates at the ends of the Cassaro (Corso Vittorio Emanuele): New Gate next to Palazzo dei Normanni, Happy Gate to the sea.
Erected in 1324, it houses numerous sacred works of art among frescoes and paintings.
Copertino is known for its cellars that have made its red wine famous and for its quality olive oil.

The garden on Lake Borromeo, born from the union of Intra and Pallanza: the Botanical Gardens of Villa Taranto, the lakefront of Pallanza, villas and churches on Castagnola, Suna and, at Fondotoce, reeds and memory of the Resistance.
Eight centuries of monastic life in the center of Cagli.
The bell tower of the Oltrepò.
The history of the territory from Volsci to Longobards.

Romanesque church probably of the twelfth century, entirely frescoed around 1400 by masters of the school of Bolzano (reconsecrated in 1410), with paintings similar to those of the parish church of Terlano and of Saint Catherine in Aica di Fiè, perhaps commissioned by the nobles Niederthor, whose coat of arms re-emerged in 1885. Outside St. Helena, St. Christopher and the Crucifixion; inside the evangelists in the vault, the Christ judge in the apse, Cain and Abel and Creation on the triumphal arch, the stories of Jesus' childhood on the walls; altarpiece signed J. G. Plazer 1723. About 30 minutes walk from the Pfösl stop; the key is asked at the farm in front of the church.

Municipality of the Brescia plain with the parish, Palazzo Tinti and the Museo della Civiltà Contadina born in the seventies by the master Dino Gregorio; in the hamlet of Pievedizio stands Palazzo Soncini, with two towers that recall the ancient strong houses.
The flavors of Lepini, strawberry grape on the head.
This is where the poems of the "soundhorse" are born.
Natural cave on a side of Mount Antuni, overlooking the lake, frequented from about 1300; it preserves two frescoes painted in 1640.
Small excavation area with a votive deposit of the fourth century BC and a Roman thermal facility in the locality Le Casette; the former anatomical votes found are at the civic museum.

The sculptor, born in Savignano in 1879, left in the village the Compianto sul Cristo morto (1924) in the parish church, the bronze of the Redeemer on the family tomb, the monument to the Fallen of the First World War in front of the cemetery; in the village also his birthplace.
Unattainable after the 2016 earthquake according to the Touring
From convent to sanctuary in the woods of the Park.
The strength of the water that cuts the wood.
One of the most complete ethnographic museums in Italy.

Example of Baroque designed by Baldassare Longhena, author of the Salute of Venice; in the aisles side works of Jacopo Palma il Giovane and a Callido organ with 1617 reeds. It rises south of the square, between Porta Garibaldi and the Tempietto di San Martino.
The fresco attributed to Vincent Pagani.
Mother Church of the village, dedicated to the patron saint of Bartholomew, dominates the highest part of the village. There is celebrated the solemn Mass of the feast of Our Lady of the Carosene.
Seeing an old trade in the valley at work.

City Swabian on the Table, stop of the Via Francigena: the Swabian-Ange fortress, the Gothic cathedral, the Augustan amphitheatre from 16-18 thousand spectators and the Civic Museum Fiorelli in the center enclosed by the walls.
A memory of the Grand Ducal Spa.

Main square of the village, dominated by the Apostolic Palace, with the Bernini fountain of 1661 and the oldest mailbox, installed in 1820. From the eastern side you reach the viewpoint on the lake; the Corso della Repubblica crosses the medieval village to Piazza Cavalletti, with another view of the lake and Mount Cavo. Outside the village remained practically unchanged from the seventeenth century, ceramic doves of local craftsmen mark the five entrances.
A Romanesque church on the hill of Borgonato.
The green lake at the foot of the fort.
An easy ride in the nature of Val d'Intelvi.
The Byzantine icon venerated by pilgrims.
Tratto della via delle Gallie engraved in the rock to open the entrance to the valleys of Mont Blanc.
One of the smallest and oldest theatres in the region.
In Roncaglia, remains of the theatre, the porch and a early Christian basilica, protected by the special natural reserve of Augusta Bagiennorum.
The "Matitone" and the panorama of the lake.
A few steps from the castle, overlooking Piazza Duomo.
The gastronomic calendar includes the gnocchi festival in March and the wild boar pappardelle festival in April.
Church developed from a nucleus of the 11th century, with frescoes of the 14th century; the bell tower, among the highest in Europe with 380 steps and 96 meters, offers views of the lake and city.
Sanctuary of great popular devotion in a monastic complex perhaps founded around the 11th century, several times rebuilt, last time in 1947.
Nature and fauna of Montefeltro a stone's throw from the village.
Baschenis frescoes in hamlet.
The symbol of the 2012 earthquake.
Paths and nature of the Umbrian Apennines.
The church of devotion to the Crucifix.

Sarcidano country on a plateau between the lakes of Flumendosa and Mulargia, known for the nuraghe Arrubiu, the red Giant with twenty-one towers, for the naturalistic and archaeological park of Su Motti with its domus de Janas and for the manor house Omu Axiu, ethnographic museum and embroidery.
Industrial archaeology of wool.
The castle from the seven-sided tower.
A painter of Reggiolo in his town hall.
A fishing village on the lake.
The portal of Cecco Bonanotte.

Romanesque parish church shaded by badgers, cited in Vatican Code 4322, list of the Vercellian parish churches of the 10th century that reflects a situation of the 5th-6th century. Inside there are frescoes from different eras, including a Madonna of Late-Gothic Milk.
The religious heart of the medieval centre.
The Aldobrandesco village overlooking Val di Paglia and Lazio.
The altarpiece of Pordenone.

In the Palazzo Ducale, managed by the Accademia Italiana del Peperoncino di Diamante: four rooms with objects and utensils of all origins, the routes of diffusion of the plant, seeds, spices and sauces, and a video room with advertising posters and satirical cartoons on the chili. Between the pieces a lithography by Renato Guttuso and the image of chili taken from a recipe book of the sixteenth century found in Frankfurt.
The church in Piazza San Lorenzo, a few steps from the Palladio Museum, with the imposing portal of the fourteenth century and a Renaissance cloister of the fifteenth century.

The only museum on the island dedicated to birdlife, in the 19th century former Managu hospital: about three hundred sedentary and migratory birds, from raptors to sultan chicken and coral grecko, a small section on Sardinian mammals, a tactile path on the evolution of birds and on the first floor the island's natural environments, from lagoons to mountains.
The ancient Lomellina in the castle.
Fountain of Via Roma inaugurated in 1886 and restored in 2013.
Originally the church of Santa Maria e San Basso, born from the union of two medieval buildings; it was enlarged in 1745 and restored in 1868, and preserves a fresco of the fifteenth century.

A small mountain town in the Upper Lake Como, a landmark of Val Cavargna, with a territory that rises from over 1,000 meters to over 2,000 of Garzirola; here you will find the Museum of the Valley, the oratory of San Lucio on the homonymous pass at the Swiss border and the alpine pastures of the municipality.
The palace houses the Museum of Taste, the Art'900 collection by Davide Lajolo and the Regional Enoteca of Nice.
Fourth century mosaics.

The first such museum in Italy, in a former chocolate factory: it tells the history of cocoa from Maya to today and the phases of processing from plant to seeds, with advertising prints, vintage packages, scales and ancient chocolate makers and a room that reconstructs a factory with original machinery; children can make their own tablet and the visit ends with a tasting.
A small eighteenth-century sanctuary on the hill.

The ski resort of Mondolè offers summer tubing, bike park and a bob descent on a monorail of 1.3 km; in the area the giant red bench of Chris Bangle, reachable all year round, from which on clear days you can see the sea from 1,500 meters. The network of trails Mondolè Ring you can walk, bike or horseback.
The portal with the beasts carved.
A Venetian villa with its family collection.
Cumulation 4 museums €8, reduced €5
Also known as Piazza delle Erbe, in the centre: historical buildings and open-air rooms in front of the church of San Giacomo.
The UNESCO stilts.

About 3 km from the city, founded between the 10th and 11th century by the bishops of Concordia; the church remains three naves and three apses, arranged in 1211 by the abbot Richerio, with facade of 1740. The sacellus conserves frescoes from the 11th to the 11th century with stories of the Redemption and the Judgment, the central apse frescoes from the early thirteenth century with the Virgin in almond and Christ with the twelve Apostles.
It preserves a major baroque altar in polychrome marble coming from the destroyed church of San Domenico in Soriano.
The treasure of the pilgrims of San Donnino.

Ethno-anthropological museum of artisan and agricultural tools on the first floor of the Aranciaia, the building of the early eighteenth century, perhaps of Bibiena, which in winter repaired the citrus fruits of the court and today also hosts temporary exhibitions. Open from March to June, September, October and first weekend in November, Sunday and holidays 10.30-12.30 and 15.30-17.30, with guided tours at 11 and 16; weekday groups only by reservation.
the Touring Club indicates it temporarily closed
36 km cycle path on a former railway line at the foot of the Berici hills that runs from Vicenza along Villa La Rotonda to Noventa Vicentina.

In the right wall of the mother church there is a golden rococo urn (about 2 × 2 m) with the remains of the child martyr Crescenzo, who died at 11 years probably during the persecution of Diocletian: five centuries remained in the Roman cemetery of Santa Ciriaca, were found by Father Luigi Vincenzo Cassitto, native of Bonito, and transferred here on July 27, 1800 after the Papal authorization. Free access, reachable by wheelchair.

Special Area of Conservation of the Natura 2000 network in the Ticino Park, rich in biodiversity: it is the site chosen by the Park for the repopulation of the gloomy pelobate, the rare and protected "rospo della vanga" about 4 cm long. A ring of about 4 km starts from the SS oratory. Cosma and Damiano, cross the historic center and enter the woods of farnie, chestnuts, silvestri pine trees and holm oaks, alternating agricultural, wooded and humid areas; dirt ground with muddy stretches, not suitable for people with motor disabilities. The Park also offers the ring with guide on reservation.

Rich in sacred art, with a museum in the bell tower and the chapel of the Blessed Sacrament painted by Tiepolo; the baptistery, with a Gothic dome, preserves the Ark of the Saints Hermacora and Fortunato, Friulian sculpture of the fourteenth century.
A fresco from 1536 in the council room.
In the village, the Palazzo Comunale of 1696 and the fifteenth-century Palazzo Miccinelli.
The best documented of the country towers.
The former convent where St. Pius of Pietrelcina made the novitiate.

Fraction among the first inhabited places of the valley, near the natural park of Monte Corno, known as the Italian grand cru of Pinot Noir: the first vineyards were planted in the nineteenth century by Ludwig von Barth; here passes the Pinot Noir Path. The church of San Michele, mentioned at the end of the fourteenth century, has a bell tower with Romanic double windows.

The village appears in 1173 in the catalogue of Norman barons, as a fief of Gualtieri di Rainaldo.

Church in Lombard Gothic style started in the seventies of the thirteenth century on Roman and Lombard structures and completed at the end of the fifteenth century, with chapels added in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; the place welcomed in the early Middle Ages the cult of the pilgrim Fiorenzo, then bishop of Orange. In the apse cycles of frescoes by Lombard painters between the late 15th and early 16th centuries with Crucifixion and stories of the saint; the main altar is designed by Giovanni Paolo Panini (1741), and on the altars the Miracle of San Fiorenzo by Marco Benefial (1741) and a Madonna with San Bernardo by Giulio Cesare Procaccini. Open every day 7-12 and 15-19, entrance from the side door.

Five signposted rings, about 20 km in all, start from the village square among wooded hills, maquis, clearings, streams, ridges and narrow gorges; in winter snow is not uncommon. From the panoramic points you can see to the south the gulf of Baratti and the promontory of Piombino, to the west the sea, the Tuscan archipelago and Corsica, to the north the plain of Pisa with the Tower and the Apuan Islands. Along the trails you can meet foxes, roe deer and raptors; from 1 October to 31 January the Municipality recommends to walk them only Tuesday and Friday, days of venatory silence.
